quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."

community_organizations: Community Foundation of Anne Arundel County
Anne Arundel County Trust for Preservation, Inc.
Arts Council of Anne Arundel County Foundation

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Annapolis envisions a highly livable, equitable, and resilient community that addresses the needs of all residents. Through major initiatives like the Eastport Choice Neighborhood Initiative and the Annapolis Ahead 2040 Comprehensive Plan, the city aims to transition public housing into vibrant, mixed-income neighborhoods, expand equitable transportation and public water access, eliminate food deserts through community-driven cooperatives, and proactively adapt its historic downtown and critical infrastructure to climate change and rising sea levels.
geographic_addresses: 160 Duke of Gloucester Street, Annapolis, MD
Forest Drive & Hilltop Lane, Annapolis, MD
Bay Ridge Avenue & Forest Drive, Annapolis, MD
Bywater Road, Annapolis, MD

quotes.text: The Eastport Choice Neighborhood Initiative (CNI) which is focused on revitalizing the city’s largest public community. Supported by a CNI planning grant from HUD, the City and the Housing Authority of the City of Annapolis (HACA) recently completed a community-led Transformation Plan which proposes to fully redevelop the existing property into a mixed income and mixed use community better integrated with the surrounding neighborhoods while preserving affordable housing options.
quotes.briefing_quote: In coordination with local housing officials, the community seeks to redevelop public housing into a mixed-income and mixed-use community that is better integrated with surrounding neighborhoods while preserving critical affordable housing options.

quotes.text: A restrictive zoning ordinance restricts the construction of many of the diverse housing types which have historically defined the city.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that a restrictive zoning ordinance restricts the construction of many of the diverse housing types which have historically defined the city, pointing to a need for zoning reform to encourage housing variety.

quotes.text: Amend the City’s zoning standards to include more housing options
quotes.briefing_quote: To address the lack of housing diversity, planners recommend to amend the City's zoning standards to include more housing options.

quotes.text: Limited commercial space available to absorb large business relocations or expansions
quotes.briefing_quote: Economic development summaries emphasize that there is limited commercial space available to absorb large business relocations or expansions because the city's historic footprint is already largely developed.

quotes.text: Coordinate retail strategy as part of the Eastport CNI project to ensure a small grocery or other healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment
quotes.briefing_quote: To target localized food deserts, the plan highlights the opportunity to coordinate a retail strategy to ensure a small grocery or healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment.

community_organizations: Housing Authority of the City of Annapolis
Anne Arundel County Watershed Stewards Academy

plan_quotes.community_vision: In the coming years, Annapolis aspires to become a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It envisions a walkable and connected community where multiple safe and reliable transit and active transportation options reduce dependency on personal vehicles. The city will prioritize public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities, expand housing options accessible to residents of all income levels, and foster a diverse ecosystem of local entrepreneurs through inclusive economic opportunities, all while proactively protecting its critical natural and watershed resources.

quotes.text: One of the consequences of this will be that the redevelopment of commercially zoned properties will increasingly be looked at to meet housing demand.
quotes.briefing_quote: In evaluating future infill capacity, the planning commission projects that 'the redevelopment of commercially zoned properties will increasingly be looked at to meet housing demand.'

quotes.text: In fact, more than 60% of the properties in the city zoned for residential use do not permit a simple duplex...
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan's housing analysis emphasizes that 'more than 60% of the properties in the city zoned for residential use do not permit a simple duplex,' highlighting a historical barrier to creating varied housing stock.

quotes.text: For the first time in the City’s Comprehensive Planning, the plan does not provide a designation specifically for commercial use. Instead it classifies land presently in commercial use as mixed use. Land recommended for mix use may be improved with commercial and residential side by side on adjoining lots or within the same building.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting a structural pivot toward walkable neighborhood design, the document explains that 'the plan does not provide a designation specifically for commercial use. Instead it classifies land presently in commercial use as mixed use' to facilitate commercial and residential flexibility.

quotes.text: Where raw land for new housing is in short supply, which is the future for Annapolis, restrictive zoning rules worsen affordability.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the municipal growth constraints, the planning commission notes that 'where raw land for new housing is in short supply, which is the future for Annapolis, restrictive zoning rules worsen affordability.'

quotes.text: Zoning reform that legalizes modest apartment dwellings such as duplexes, triplexes, and fourplexes is one of the key recommendations of this Plan’s approach to housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better serve changing demographics, the authors recommend that 'zoning reform that legalizes modest apartment dwellings such as duplexes, triplexes, and fourplexes is one of the key recommendations of this Plan’s approach to housing.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: Glen Burnie aspires to revitalize its historic Town Center into an attractive, vibrant, and walkable destination. By leveraging flexible zoning overlays, public-private partnerships, and multimodal transportation enhancements, the community aims to stimulate the redevelopment of underutilized commercial corridors while preserving and upgrading its diverse, affordable housing stock to support a younger, growing workforce.
geographic_addresses: 7409 Baltimore Annapolis Blvd, Glen Burnie, MD
Baltimore Annapolis Boulevard & Dorsey Road, Glen Burnie, MD
Dorsey Road & Cromwell Light Rail Station, Glen Burnie, MD
MD 2 & MD 10, Glen Burnie, MD

quotes.text: The County’s efforts to secure a private developer to redevelop the large County property at 7409 Baltimore Annapolis Boulevard in the Town Center with new residential and retail uses were not successful and so must begin again.
quotes.briefing_quote: The renewal plan details a key opportunity for mixed-use development, noting that 'The County’s efforts to secure a private developer to redevelop the large County property at 7409 Baltimore Annapolis Boulevard in the Town Center with new residential and retail uses were not successful and so must begin again.'

quotes.text: Due to the lack of vacant land, it is difficult for Glen Burnie to attract newer businesses or office parks since location in Glen Burnie will typically require renovation of an older building or redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the constraints of commercial infill development, the report emphasizes that 'Due to the lack of vacant land, it is difficult for Glen Burnie to attract newer businesses or office parks since location in Glen Burnie will typically require renovation of an older building or redevelopment.'

quotes.text: Legislation was passed in 2020 to establish a Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay within the County’s zoning and development codes. The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To catalyze local investment, the plan highlights that 'The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.'

quotes.text: Additionally, newer residential and commercial development near Arundel Mills, Fort Meade, BWI Airport, and in other areas where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Acknowledging regional market headwinds, the application notes that 'newer residential and commercial development... where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.'

quotes.text: While no major affordable rental developments are planned in Glen Burnie at this time, the County has supported the redevelopment and preservation of existing affordable units when possible.
quotes.briefing_quote: In outlining housing goals, the application specifies that 'While no major affordable rental developments are planned in Glen Burnie at this time, the County has supported the redevelopment and preservation of existing affordable units when possible.'

Housing Commission of Anne Arundel County

quotes.text: Due to the lack of vacant land, it is difficult for Glen Burnie to attract newer businesses or office parks since location in Glen Burnie will typically require renovation of an older building or redevelopment.

quotes.text: Legislation was passed in 2020 to establish a Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay within the County’s zoning and development codes. The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To catalyze local investment, the plan highlights that 'The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.'

quotes.text: Additionally, newer residential and commercial development near Arundel Mills, Fort Meade, BWI Airport, and in other areas where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Acknowledging regional market headwinds, the application notes that 'newer residential and commercial development... where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.'

quotes.text: While no major affordable rental developments are planned in Glen Burnie at this time, the County has supported the redevelopment and preservation of existing affordable units when possible.
quotes.briefing_quote: In outlining housing goals, the application specifies that 'While no major affordable rental developments are planned in Glen Burnie at this time, the County has supported the redevelopment and preservation of existing affordable units when possible.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

The community aims to capitalize on its strategic role as a logistics and technology hub, revitalizing key commercial corridors like East Drive and Linden Avenue with diverse retail, arts, and mixed-use transit-oriented developments that serve residents and students alike.

quotes.text: The proposed Arbutus Station is a mixed-use development by a local developer at the intersection of Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road. It is within the proposed Sustainable Community boundary and the County's Commercial Revitalization District that can take advantage of the County's revitalization programs if it meets the County revitalization goals and efforts. The community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan.

quotes.text: Finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners. Though the community is always looking for prospective homeowners, there is a lack of rental options to attract the UMBC students and programs to benefit both the landlords and student renters. At the same time the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup discussions highlighted the challenge of "finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners," noting that while there is a lack of student rental options, "the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership."

quotes.text: Bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques similar to Ellicott City and Catonsville.

quotes.text: Convene group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.

quotes.text: In 2018, the New Town Preliminary Development Plan (PDP) was increased by 315 units to allow for a mixed-use redevelopment project at the Long Reach Village Center. quotes.text: The Housing Commission has expressed interested in redeveloping the Columbia Landing apartment community. Due to existing debt on the property, the Commission would have to significantly increase density to be able to finance the redevelopment. With elementary schools in the area currently overcapacity, the project would likely not be able to proceed for up to 5 years due to the Adequate Public Facilities Ordinance requirements and would need a waiver to proceed.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Housing Commission expressed a strong desire to update local housing, but noted that 'due to existing debt on the property, the Commission would have to significantly increase density to be able to finance the redevelopment', which is currently paused due to local school capacity and Adequate Public Facilities Ordinance requirements.

quotes.text: The Housing Opportunities Master Plan recommends adding affordable units in all new and redevelopment communities, especially if the existing affordable units are not accessible, energy efficient or integrated into market rate communities. However, community feedback within the Long Reach community suggest that Long Reach already has a disproportion share of affordable housing, as compared to the rest of the County.
quotes.briefing_quote: While county plans recommend adding affordable units to all new developments, 'community feedback within the Long Reach community suggests that Long Reach already has a disproportionate share of affordable housing' compared to the rest of the county, indicating a need for a more balanced approach to market-rate and affordable integration.

quotes.text: The most recent subdivision constructed in Long Reach --Arnold’s Corner -- consisted of 18 single-family dwellings with an advertised starting price of $900,000. quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Frederick's vision, driven by its CommUNITY 2030 Strategic Plan and 2020 Comprehensive Plan, focuses on sustainable, equitable development across three distinct corridors: Downtown, the Golden Mile, and East Frederick. The community seeks to revitalize underutilized commercial areas and preserve its historic character through selective redevelopment, adaptive reuse, and strategic infill. quotes.text: The High Density Residential (R2) zoning district encompasses only 16.4 acres, or roughly 2.2% of the Town's land area. This zoning district allows for a density of eight (8) dwelling units per acre, permitting townhomes, multi-family dwelling units, two-family dwelling units, and single-family dwelling units. With higher residential densities, future properties zoned R2 should be located in areas with ample transportation access and public facilities to minimize congestion and overloading of existing public infrastructure.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that 'with higher residential densities, future properties zoned R2 should be located in areas with ample transportation access and public facilities to minimize congestion and overloading of existing public infrastructure.'

quotes.text: The Smart Growth Residential (R1-SG) zoning district encompasses 122.8 acres, or roughly 16.8% of the Town's land area. Overall, the R1-SG zoning district is found within the Saber Ridge subdivision on the north end of Town, and within the proposed Quail Run subdivision on the west end of Town. The R1-SG zoning district is comparable to the R1 zoning district; however, the R1-SG zoning district allows for a more compact design with no specified maximum density for residential units and a smaller minimum lot size of 8,000 square feet, whereas the R1 zoning district employs a minimum lot size of 15,000 square feet. This zoning district is unique and should be expanded in future residential housing projects as additional lands are annexed into the Town for development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Town highlights a sustainable layout strategy, stating that 'the Smart Growth Residential zoning district is unique and should be expanded in future residential housing projects as additional lands are annexed into the Town for development.'

quotes.text: The GC zoning district area is located on the south end of Town along I-70. This district includes more modern-style commercial development with two (2) drive-through restaurants, two (2) gasoline pumping stations, and four (4) tracts of undeveloped commercial land. Most of the Town's future commercial development will likely take place within this district or will be added to this district as adjacent commercial land is annexed into the Town and developed.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners expect commercial activity to concentrate near major transport nodes, observing that 'most of the Town's future commercial development will likely take place within the General Commercial district or will be added to this district as adjacent commercial land is annexed.'

quotes.text: The Village Center (VC) zoning district is the Town's sole mixed use zoning district, allowing for an array of light commercial and residential uses. The VC zoning district encompasses 73.7 acres, or roughly 10.1% of the Town's land area. The VC zoning district is exclusively found along Main Street in the older areas of the Town developed during a period when individuals lived within close proximity to the Town's central business district (CBD). The Town employed this zoning district to continue to encourage light commercial activities and office space along Main Street while still permitting residential uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: To maintain historic corridor vitality, the plan notes that 'the Town employed the Village Center zoning district to continue to encourage light commercial activities and office space along Main Street while still permitting residential uses.'

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.

quotes.text: The existing, very low-density development pattern in the Sugarloaf Planning Area, consisting primarily of large-lot, single-family residential dwellings, is suitable for a rural area with significant and sensitive environmental resources. A constrained and limited transportation network, sensitive forested watersheds with high-quality waters, and the surrounding open space and low density, rural characteristics of the Sugarloaf Planning Area warrant further evaluation and scrutiny of new large-scale commercial and institutional land uses or additional residential growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights an opportunity to preserve the very low-density residential pattern and sensitive environment by exercising rigorous scrutiny over any proposed large-scale commercial, institutional, or additional residential expansion.

quotes.text: The Urbana CGA borders the Sugarloaf Planning Area along I-270, which is currently a boundary that demarcates a large mixed-use (commercial, employment, residential) community from an area with dispersed residences, unique environmental and historic resources, and a distinctively rural sense of place; however, minor commercial development exists in the Sugarloaf Planning Area in the vicinity of the MD 80/I-270 interchange.
quotes.briefing_quote: Livable Frederick planners emphasize using I-270 as a firm planning boundary to concentrate mixed-use commercial and high-density employment growth within the Urbana Community Growth Area, thereby shielding the adjoining rural sanctuary.

quotes.text: The RC zoning district, as with most zoning districts, provides the opportunity for property owners to subdivide land parcels to create new lots for purposes of development and establishment of land uses or activities permitted by the Zoning Ordinance. The minimum lot size for new subdivision lots in the RC zone is 10 acres; thus, a 50-acre parcel could, theoretically, create five new residential lots through the current zoning and subdivision regulations. The RC zoning district’s development prohibition on steep topographical gradients, plus soil percolation limitations, and other environmental protection measures result in far fewer lots than the theoretical maximum permitted in the RC zone.
quotes.briefing_quote: Although zoning allows large-lot subdivisions, steep slopes and soil percolation limits naturally restrict buildable residential density, aligning development capacity with environmental preservation goals.

quotes.text: Policy 8.8 Reduce greenhouse gas emissions by limiting the growth of high vehicle trip-generating land uses in the Sugarloaf Planning Area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To align with County climate directives, developers should expect policy parameters that limit high vehicle trip-generating commercial land uses, ensuring compatibility with rural infrastructure and emission reduction targets.

quotes.text: Policy 5.2 Future transit centers, park-and-ride facilities, and transit-oriented development projects associated with future interchanges on I-270 should be thoroughly evaluated in order to serve the Urbana Community Growth Area, as well as potential points along the I-270 Corridor that may support compact employment and mixed-use development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a vision to evaluate transit-oriented and mixed-use development projects at planned interchanges along the I-270 corridor, capturing regional transit benefits while keeping commercial density outside of the protected Sugarloaf interior.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of New Market is navigating rapid population growth by balancing its historic character with smart growth principles. The town seeks to transition from an antique-dominated commercial district to a diverse, resilient local economy by attracting new commercial entities like restaurants and coffee shops, pursuing infill opportunities, and diversifying its housing stock—which currently consists mostly of single-family market-rate homes—to include multi-family housing, townhouses, accessory units, and senior housing options. The vision also focuses on correcting critical pedestrian connectivity gaps and upgrading physical stormwater and utility infrastructure.

quotes.text: Previous developments in the town have provided a mono-product offering; usually single-family targeting market rate and middle income brackets. Few townhouses or accessory units are available for rental, no senior housing; and no managed apartments exist within the town...
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning narrative notes that past housing developments have created a mono-product landscape, emphasizing that 'few townhouses or accessory units are available for rental, no senior housing, and no managed apartments exist within the town' to serve a diversifying population.

quotes.text: The Town will work with developers on infill lots within the town and selectively annex land that can accommodate a market rate apartment development... The town will accept annexation and development proposals for land sufficient to provide a broad range of housing types targeting a range of income brackets...
quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate diverse community needs, town officials state they will 'work with developers on infill lots within the town and selectively annex land that can accommodate a market rate apartment development' to offer a wider variety of housing choices.

quotes.text: In 2016 the historic structure at 39 West Main Street was still functioning as the Town Hall, however, during that time it was becoming increasingly clear that its location was better suited for a commercial or residential use... There is interest in leasing the now vacant, yet delightfully appealing historic structure. It is unfortunate that this structure has serious structural and code related issues that need to be addressed before it can be economically viable.
quotes.briefing_quote: The town identifies the former town hall at 39 West Main Street as a prime redevelopment asset, though acknowledging that 'this structure has serious structural and code-related issues that need to be addressed before it can be economically viable' for new commercial or residential uses.

quotes.text: The array of uses need to be further updated to accommodate newer types of businesses on Main Street; mixed-use development and added housing types to accommodate blended income needs of the Town... some of the Special Exception approval processes required in the 2009 LDO are no longer appropriate and have caused difficulty in attracting a diverse commercial base...
quotes.briefing_quote: Reviewing their planning policies, town leadership indicates that local 'uses need to be further updated to accommodate newer types of businesses on Main Street; mixed-use development and added housing types' to modernize the commercial district and ease the regulatory process.

quotes.text: The Calumet development proposal which was active as of 2016 is now going through changes... The project met with continual delays because a necessary Sewer Water agreement could not be reached between the County and the Town.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting major regional growth challenges, the plan reports that residential development projects have met 'continual delays because a necessary sewer and water agreement could not be reached between the County and the Town.'

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Highland Beach aspires to preserve its unique history as Maryland's first African American incorporated municipality and oldest resort community. The town seeks to manage orderly, low-density residential growth while strictly prohibiting commercial intrusion, protecting environmentally sensitive coastal areas, and utilizing green infrastructure to maintain its quiet, family-oriented atmosphere.

quotes.text: Although founded as a summer resort, it is now a town of both summer and year-round residents who choose not to permit commercial establishments.

quotes.text: It is the desire of the community to control housing density and to maintain the architectural character already established in Highland Beach.
quotes.briefing_quote: To protect the town's unique heritage, the plan highlights a strong community desire 'to control housing density and to maintain the architectural character' already established.

quotes.text: With the exception of town property and vacant parcels, Highland Beach land use is exclusively residential. All homes are of the single-family detached variety. It is our intention to remain an exclusively residential community with no commercial intrusion.
quotes.briefing_quote: Developers should note the town's strict stance on land use, expressing a clear 'intention to remain an exclusively residential community with no commercial intrusion.'

quotes.text: Future residential development should be limited with regard to intensity (or density) and placement of structures, and lot dimensions should be controlled to preserve the present character of Highland Beach.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community outlines that 'future residential development should be limited with regard to intensity (or density)' and structure placement to safeguard the neighborhood's scale.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Annapolis envisions a highly livable, equitable, and resilient community that addresses the needs of all residents. Through major initiatives like the Eastport Choice Neighborhood Initiative and the Annapolis Ahead 2040 Comprehensive Plan, the city aims to transition public housing into vibrant, mixed-income neighborhoods, expand equitable transportation and public water access, eliminate food deserts through community-driven cooperatives, and proactively adapt its historic downtown and critical infrastructure to climate change and rising sea levels.

Supported by a CNI planning grant from HUD, the City and the Housing Authority of the City of Annapolis (HACA) recently completed a community-led Transformation Plan which proposes to fully redevelop the existing property into a mixed income and mixed use community better integrated with the surrounding neighborhoods while preserving affordable housing options.
quotes.briefing_quote: In coordination with local housing officials, the community seeks to redevelop public housing into a mixed-income and mixed-use community that is better integrated with surrounding neighborhoods while preserving critical affordable housing options.

quotes.text: A restrictive zoning ordinance restricts the construction of many of the diverse housing types which have historically defined the city.

quotes.text: Amend the City’s zoning standards to include more housing options
quotes.briefing_quote: To address the lack of housing diversity, planners recommend to amend the City's zoning standards to include more housing options.

quotes.text: Limited commercial space available to absorb large business relocations or expansions
quotes.briefing_quote: Economic development summaries emphasize that there is limited commercial space available to absorb large business relocations or expansions because the city's historic footprint is already largely developed.

quotes.text: Coordinate retail strategy as part of the Eastport CNI project to ensure a small grocery or other healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment

quotes.text: In fact, more than 60% of the properties in the city zoned for residential use do not permit a simple duplex...

quotes.text: Where raw land for new housing is in short supply, which is the future for Annapolis, restrictive zoning rules worsen affordability.

quotes.text: Zoning reform that legalizes modest apartment dwellings such as duplexes, triplexes, and fourplexes is one of the key recommendations of this Plan’s approach to housing.

quotes.text: Additionally, newer residential and commercial development near Arundel Mills, Fort Meade, BWI Airport, and in other areas where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Annapolis envisions a highly livable, equitable, and resilient community that addresses the needs of all residents. Through major initiatives like the Eastport Choice Neighborhood Initiative and the Annapolis Ahead 2040 Comprehensive Plan, the city aims to transition public housing into vibrant, mixed-income neighborhoods, expand equitable transportation and public water access, eliminate food deserts through community-driven cooperatives, and proactively adapt its historic downtown and critical infrastructure to climate change and rising sea levels.

quotes.text: The Eastport Choice Neighborhood Initiative (CNI) which is focused on revitalizing the city’s largest public community. Supported by a CNI planning grant from HUD, the City and the Housing Authority of the City of Annapolis (HACA) recently completed a community-led Transformation Plan which proposes to fully redevelop the existing property into a mixed income and mixed use community better integrated with the surrounding neighborhoods while preserving affordable housing options.
quotes.briefing_quote: In coordination with local housing officials, the community seeks to redevelop public housing into a mixed-income and mixed-use community that is better integrated with surrounding neighborhoods while preserving critical affordable housing options.

quotes.text: A restrictive zoning ordinance restricts the construction of many of the diverse housing types which have historically defined the city.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that a restrictive zoning ordinance restricts the construction of many of the diverse housing types which have historically defined the city, pointing to a need for zoning reform to encourage housing variety.

quotes.text: Amend the City’s zoning standards to include more housing options
quotes.briefing_quote: To address the lack of housing diversity, planners recommend to amend the City's zoning standards to include more housing options.

quotes.text: Limited commercial space available to absorb large business relocations or expansions
quotes.briefing_quote: Economic development summaries emphasize that there is limited commercial space available to absorb large business relocations or expansions because the city's historic footprint is already largely developed.

quotes.text: Coordinate retail strategy as part of the Eastport CNI project to ensure a small grocery or other healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment
quotes.briefing_quote: To target localized food deserts, the plan highlights the opportunity to coordinate a retail strategy to ensure a small grocery or healthy food provider is part of the redevelopment.

plan_quotes.community_vision: In the coming years, Annapolis aspires to become a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It envisions a walkable and connected community where multiple safe and reliable transit and active transportation options reduce dependency on personal vehicles. The city will prioritize public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities, expand housing options accessible to residents of all income levels, and foster a diverse ecosystem of local entrepreneurs through inclusive economic opportunities, all while proactively protecting its critical natural and watershed resources.

quotes.text: In fact, more than 60% of the properties in the city zoned for residential use do not permit a simple duplex...
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan's housing analysis emphasizes that 'more than 60% of the properties in the city zoned for residential use do not permit a simple duplex,' highlighting a historical barrier to creating varied housing stock.

quotes.text: For the first time in the City’s Comprehensive Planning, the plan does not provide a designation specifically for commercial use. Instead it classifies land presently in commercial use as mixed use. Land recommended for mix use may be improved with commercial and residential side by side on adjoining lots or within the same building.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting a structural pivot toward walkable neighborhood design, the document explains that 'the plan does not provide a designation specifically for commercial use. Instead it classifies land presently in commercial use as mixed use' to facilitate commercial and residential flexibility.

quotes.text: Where raw land for new housing is in short supply, which is the future for Annapolis, restrictive zoning rules worsen affordability.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the municipal growth constraints, the planning commission notes that 'where raw land for new housing is in short supply, which is the future for Annapolis, restrictive zoning rules worsen affordability.'

quotes.text: Zoning reform that legalizes modest apartment dwellings such as duplexes, triplexes, and fourplexes is one of the key recommendations of this Plan’s approach to housing.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

community_organizations: Arts & Humanities Council of Montgomery County

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

quotes.text: Given that most new residential growth in the city will come in the form of multiple unit residential buildings, as apartments or condominiums, and that not all locations are appropriate for mixed-use development, Rockville needs a higher density residential zone.
quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate evolving multi-family housing demands, the plan notes that "most new residential growth in the city will come in the form of multiple unit residential buildings, as apartments or condominiums, and that not all locations are appropriate for mixed-use development, Rockville needs a higher density residential zone."

quotes.text: One way to accommodate more affordable housing options, flexible space for an office or shared family living arrangements, and financial assistance for current homeowners, while maintaining the city’s predominantly residential character, is with accessory apartments and accessory dwelling units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address affordability while maintaining neighborhood fabric, the plan highlights that "one way to accommodate more affordable housing options, flexible space for an office or shared family living arrangements, and financial assistance for current homeowners, while maintaining the city’s predominantly residential character, is with accessory apartments and accessory dwelling units."

quotes.text: Steady additions of commercial and amenity space on the ground floor of new buildings bring the opportunity for new shops and restaurants, supported by new residential units and offices on upper floors. This Plan promotes an intensification of development that encourages an active street scene and vibrant commercial district.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support local businesses and create active downtown corridors, the plan outlines that "steady additions of commercial and amenity space on the ground floor of new buildings bring the opportunity for new shops and restaurants, supported by new residential units and offices on upper floors."

quotes.text: These 'missing middle' housing types, also discussed in the Land Use Element, include: Duplexes; Triplexes; Fourplexes or quads; Sixplexes; Townhouses or rowhouses; Small apartment buildings; and Garden apartments. These housing types are largely missing in American suburbs, including Rockville, in part because land use policies and zoning do not allow their type of construction in single-unit detached residential zones...
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies the need for diversified housing forms, noting that "these 'missing middle' housing types... are largely missing in American suburbs, including Rockville, in part because land use policies and zoning do not allow their type of construction in single-unit detached residential zones."

quotes.text: The most successful office clusters in Montgomery County are part of mixed-use development with a strong sense of place and quality environment. Transit connectivity is increasingly important to office tenants.
quotes.briefing_quote: Citing a countywide office market assessment, the plan underscores that "the most successful office clusters in Montgomery County are part of mixed-use development with a strong sense of place and quality environment. Transit connectivity is increasingly important to office tenants."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Calvert County seeks to maintain its high quality of life by balancing environmental protection, social equity, and economic growth. These designated growth centers are intended to offer a mix of housing, retail, and commercial options, creating convenient and interesting places to live, work, and shop.

quotes.text: Nearly 85 percent of Calvert County residential development is categorized as low or very low density development. Most of the residential development has occurred outside the Town Centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: A baseline assessment of local housing reveals that nearly 85 percent of residential development is categorized as low or very low density, occurring mostly outside designated Town Centers, presenting a major opportunity to rebalance growth toward the county's core nodes.

quotes.text: A mixed-use center is envisioned with a focus on multi-family housing and more public open space.
quotes.briefing_quote: For the Prince Frederick area, planners envision a vibrant mixed-use center with a focus on multi-family housing and more public open space to create a more dynamic and walkable core.

quotes.text: The overall appearances of Town Centers are somewhat different from the vision, and achieving walkable, bikeable neighborhoods has proven elusive... Many commercial areas look more like strip centers than mixed use, pedestrian-friendly communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: While past growth patterns have resembled vehicle-centric strip centers, community workshop participants strongly emphasize the opportunity to redevelop existing commercial areas into mixed-use, pedestrian-friendly communities with complete sidewalk and bicycle networks.

quotes.text: Explore the potential to incorporate multi-family housing into commercial areas to bring uses closer together and allow for redevelopment and infill housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To foster vibrant, walkable environments, the plan recommends that developers and county partners explore the potential to incorporate multi-family housing into commercial areas to bring uses closer together and allow for active infill redevelopment.

quotes.text: Do not permit additional commercial and retail development along highways outside Town Centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: In an effort to prevent sprawling auto-dependent corridors, county directives specify that they will not permit additional commercial and retail development along highways outside Town Centers, driving future business density into designated town cores.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
