quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."

plan_quotes.community_vision: In 2040, Chesapeake Beach is a growing and economically vibrant and healthy town with a compact arrangement of housing, businesses, institutions, and green open spaces that honor the Town’s historic development while broadening citizen connection with and access to the scenic and recreational attributes that Chesapeake Beach is endowed with by virtue of its unique geography and natural setting. In embracing limited residential growth and focusing on steadily developing recreational and commercial amenities, we have guided residential and commercial development into ways that enriched the lives and experiences of Town residents and visitors.

quotes.text: Rescind the bonus density overlay district in its entirety. This provision of the Zoning Ordinance has allowed the Planning Commission to approve apartment and condominium buildings that can exceed 50 feet in height. Without the overlay district, building height would remain capped at 35 feet and new housing would be compatible with existing housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To protect traditional community scale, the Planning Commission recommended that the Town "rescind the bonus density overlay district in its entirety," ensuring building heights remain capped at 35 feet to keep new housing compatible with existing neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Remove multi-family housing, duplexes, and townhouses as permitted uses in those parts of the Residential Village district designated on Map 13 as Residential Village 1 (RV-1). With this change, townhouse developments in areas designated RV-1 would be permitted only where they are built today.
quotes.briefing_quote: To safeguard neighborhood character, the plan recommends the Town "remove multi-family housing, duplexes, and townhouses as permitted uses" in the Residential Village 1 zone, limiting future higher-density configurations to where they currently exist.

quotes.text: Convert the Maritime District to Maritime Commercial (MC) and remove all new housing types from the list of permitted uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: Reflecting the community's desire to focus on tourism and commercial waterfront vibrancy, planners recommended the Town "convert the Maritime District to Maritime Commercial and remove all new housing types from the list of permitted uses."

quotes.text: New residential uses would be allowed only as residences above street level commercial and existing residential uses would remain as permitted uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: To catalyze a lively main-street feel along Bayside Road, the land use plan dictates that in the Town Commercial district, "new residential uses would be allowed only as residences above street level commercial."

quotes.text: The purpose is to allow space for low intensity commercial uses (such as coffee shops, florists, salons, and offices) and to ensure that new buildings are generally compatible with surrounding houses.
quotes.briefing_quote: For the Neighborhood Commercial areas, the Town seeks to "allow space for low intensity commercial uses" while ensuring any new structures remain visually and functionally compatible with neighboring residential homes.

quotes.text: A mixed-use center is envisioned with a focus on multi-family housing and more public open space.

quotes.text: The overall appearances of Town Centers are somewhat different from the vision, and achieving walkable, bikeable neighborhoods has proven elusive... Many commercial areas look more like strip centers than mixed use, pedestrian-friendly communities.

quotes.text: Explore the potential to incorporate multi-family housing into commercial areas to bring uses closer together and allow for redevelopment and infill housing.

quotes.text: Do not permit additional commercial and retail development along highways outside Town Centers.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.

quotes.text: Maryland wants to limit urban sprawl and get homes off septic systems, yet will not help with the expansion of the wastewater treatment plant. Currently, there are plans for an assisted living development. Once that has been completed, the town will probably not have the wastewater capacity for any other new developments. Only a few individual housing will be allowed. We cannot implement a housing plan until we get financial assistance with the expansion of the wastewater treatment plant.

quotes.text: Town is willing to encourage new developments of affordable housing. Twelve new houses have been built, with plans for an additional three underway. quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting local collaboration, the renewal application outlines that the 'Town is willing to encourage new developments of affordable housing,' as evidenced by twelve new homes built and three more underway in partnership with Habitat for Humanity.

quotes.text: Codes need updating to allow for more housing options for residents and to encourage new development.

quotes.text: This project has provided an impetus for increased development at the Industrial Park and will allow the Town of Hurlock to raise its economic indicators. quotes.text: The Town has attractions which can be marketed to the heritage tourism market. These historic assets can be developed to draw more people into town, promoting business growth and the town economy.

The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Langley Park envisions transitioning into a vibrant, transit-oriented gateway that leverages the construction of the Purple Line light rail while preserving its naturally occurring affordable housing and rich cultural diversity. The community seeks to revitalize its commercial districts—especially the International Corridor—through denser, mixed-use development, streetscape beautification, and creative placemaking. Addressing persistent infrastructure and social challenges, the plan aims to improve pedestrian and bicycle safety, modernize aging multifamily rental housing, preserve environmental assets like the Northwest Branch Trail, and elevate the quality of life through enhanced health, language, and youth recreation services.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."

quotes.text: In 2018, the New Town Preliminary Development Plan (PDP) was increased by 315 units to allow for a mixed-use redevelopment project at the Long Reach Village Center. However, the redevelopment project was hindered by a complex zoning process and the need to acquire multiple properties under different ownership and was unable to overcome these barriers.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning analysis indicates that while the New Town Preliminary Development Plan was expanded by 315 units to enable mixed-use development at the Village Center, 'the redevelopment project was hindered by a complex zoning process and the need to acquire multiple properties under different ownership', highlighting a critical area where public-private coordination can streamline future efforts.

quotes.text: The Housing Commission has expressed interested in redeveloping the Columbia Landing apartment community. Due to existing debt on the property, the Commission would have to significantly increase density to be able to finance the redevelopment. With elementary schools in the area currently overcapacity, the project would likely not be able to proceed for up to 5 years due to the Adequate Public Facilities Ordinance requirements and would need a waiver to proceed.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Housing Commission expressed a strong desire to update local housing, but noted that 'due to existing debt on the property, the Commission would have to significantly increase density to be able to finance the redevelopment', which is currently paused due to local school capacity and Adequate Public Facilities Ordinance requirements.

quotes.text: The Housing Opportunities Master Plan recommends adding affordable units in all new and redevelopment communities, especially if the existing affordable units are not accessible, energy efficient or integrated into market rate communities. However, community feedback within the Long Reach community suggest that Long Reach already has a disproportion share of affordable housing, as compared to the rest of the County.
quotes.briefing_quote: While county plans recommend adding affordable units to all new developments, 'community feedback within the Long Reach community suggests that Long Reach already has a disproportionate share of affordable housing' compared to the rest of the county, indicating a need for a more balanced approach to market-rate and affordable integration.

quotes.text: The most recent subdivision constructed in Long Reach --Arnold’s Corner -- consisted of 18 single-family dwellings with an advertised starting price of $900,000. New Town Zoning, comprising most of Long Reach, does not require Moderately Priced Housing Units (MIHU’s) and they were not constructed as part of this development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan documents that the newest local subdivision, Arnold's Corner, 'consisted of 18 single-family dwellings with an advertised starting price of $900,000' and did not include moderately priced housing units because the underlying New Town zoning does not mandate them.

quotes.briefing_quote: Market evaluations indicate a strong opportunity to reposition commercial space, highlighting 'a shift in use from primary retail to community and institutional uses, an arts theme to complement the Columbia Art Center, and new housing'.

quotes.text: The Warfield Complex is a de-accessioned 140-acre portion of the historic Springfield State Hospital, lying at the Town's eastern boundary... The Town and Warfield Development Corporation purchased the site from the state and then sold it to an LLC as an ongoing economic development project, intended to become a major job center by reusing the historic buildings as offices and commercial establishments.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights the 140-acre historic Warfield Complex as a major opportunity for reuse, noting that the ongoing redevelopment is "intended to become a major job center by reusing the historic buildings as offices and commercial establishments" alongside residential integration.

quotes.text: Near completion of the Parkside at Warfield housing development. Once complete, this project will have created 145+ new townhouse style homes to help meet the growing demand of residential housing in the Sykesville area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address growing local housing demands, the town celebrated the "creation of 145+ new townhouse style homes" in the Parkside at Warfield development, expanding the local housing options.

quotes.text: The Planned Employment Center (PEC) zone was created to facilitate the growth of a whole new development in Sykesville at the historic Warfield property. This zone is intended to create a new business district within the Sykesville limits and allow for a multitude of mixed uses including retail and residential.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Town established a Planned Employment Center zone at the historic Warfield property, designed to "create a new business district... and allow for a multitude of mixed uses including retail and residential."

quotes.text: Downtown zoning needs updating to reflect the high-density development currently found there and encourage more economically feasible development
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies a key regulatory opportunity, stating that "downtown zoning needs updating to reflect the high-density development currently found there and encourage more economically feasible development."

quotes.text: Explore the provision of Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) to create smaller, independent, residential dwelling units located on the same lot as a single-family home.
quotes.briefing_quote: To diversify housing types on existing land, the Town aims to "explore the provision of Accessory Dwelling Units to create smaller, independent, residential dwelling units located on the same lot as a single-family home."

quotes.text: Promote the construction and conversion of existing housing into attached or multi-unit housing to provide more selection by offering smaller efficiency units at a lower price point.
quotes.briefing_quote: To expand affordable options on built-out land, the Town proposes to "promote the construction and conversion of existing housing into attached or multi-unit housing" to offer smaller, cost-effective efficiency units.

quotes.text: Infill at the old carriage house location on Main Street to create additional retail and residential space in the Downtown area.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan showcases successful historic infill development, pointing to the "old carriage house location on Main Street to create additional retail and residential space in the Downtown area."

quotes.text: The developers of the historic Warfield property are unsatisfied with the zoning text for the Planned Employment Center that they agreed to build and progress on certain aspects of the project are stalled while the issues get worked out.
quotes.briefing_quote: While the Warfield site holds immense promise, developers have noted that "progress on certain aspects of the project are stalled while issues get worked out" regarding the Planned Employment Center zoning text, highlighting an opportunity for collaborative zoning refinements.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.

quotes.text: Apartments were added as a permitted use in the B-3 zoning district.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support local housing variety and downtown density, the City of Aberdeen amended its zoning code to permit apartments as a permitted use in the B-3 Highway Commercial district.

quotes.text: Within the requested area, there are two undeveloped parcels that have been available for development for the past seven years. There is also a shopping center space site that has two vacant units and attracting tenants has been difficult. The zoning of the added parcels is M-1, light industrial and B-3, Highway Commercial.
quotes.briefing_quote: City planners noted that adding these commercial parcels to the Sustainable Community area targets an opportunity to attract tenants to a struggling shopping center and unlock development on long-vacant highway commercial and light industrial lands.

quotes.text: One investor took advantage of the Opportunity Zone by purchasing and renovating the Parke Street Apartments located at 114-118 S. Parke Street.

quotes.text: The City passed two new business incentives for the Transit Oriented Development (TOD) area, which is in the SC Area. The new business incentives offer a real property tax credit on the total assessed value of the property available for commercial property owners, and a water/sewer connection charge waiver available to commercial and residential property owners.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City established strong financial mechanisms to support transit-oriented growth, offering real property tax credits and waiving water/sewer connection charges for both commercial and residential developers within the Transit Oriented Development area.

quotes.text: Lack of available undeveloped sites for new housing development; Building inventory is old and investment has not been consistent in the SC Area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planners identified a significant growth constraint in the core area, pointing to a lack of undeveloped sites for new housing alongside an aging building inventory that has received inconsistent investment.

quotes.text: There have been no new housing opportunities in the TOD area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Despite planning initiatives, municipal evaluations highlight a persistent gap in local development, noting that no new housing opportunities have been constructed in the Transit Oriented Development area.

quotes.text: There is a weak market for retail, restaurants, and entertainment in the Main Street and U.S. Route 40 corridor:
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's assessment of downtown economic health points to a weak market for retail, restaurants, and entertainment along the Main Street and U.S. Route 40 corridor, emphasizing the need for targeted commercial tenant recruitment.

quotes.text: The TOD-D is intended to be the heart of the TOD area and provide a highly visible presence and identity for Aberdeen along the US 40/Philadelphia Boulevard corridor. This zone will feature a high-intensity, highly walkable mixed-use district with buildings ranging from two to eight stories in height with bonus provisions for up to four additional stories; ground-floor shopfronts, with wide sidewalks to promote a highly walkable district; improved public spaces including public plazas, street trees, pedestrian-scale lights, and public art; and the majority of parking is consolidated in structures, at curbs of public streets and behind buildings.
quotes.briefing_quote: To establish a vibrant core near transit, the plan outlines an opportunity for a "**high-intensity, highly walkable mixed-use district with buildings ranging from two to eight stories**" featuring ground-floor shopfronts, improved public spaces, and consolidated parking within the Transit-Oriented Development Downtown zone.

quotes.text: In 2022, the Aberdeen City Council approved the sale of three plots of land on Franklin Street to a local developer. This land, located across from City Hall and Festival Park, was purchased with the intent to develop the space into a three-story, mixed-use development with commercial and retail space on the bottom floor and residential space on the upper levels.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local leaders catalyzed downtown revitalization by approving the sale of land on Franklin Street for a "**three-story, mixed-use development with commercial and retail space on the bottom floor and residential space on the upper levels**," serving as a prime showcase for downtown reinvestment.

quotes.text: The size of the traditional family household has been declining and the proportion of smaller households is increasing... Despite the shifts in household size, new construction has continued to focus on delivering larger homes with more bedrooms. This results in gaps between the needs and demands of residents and the supply of appropriate housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing analysts highlighted a mismatch between market supply and demographic shifts, noting that while smaller households are increasing, "**new construction has continued to focus on delivering larger homes with more bedrooms**," leaving a gap in attainable, smaller housing options.

quotes.text: The light industrial land use provides for existing warehouse distribution facilities that may be redeveloped into such uses as light manufacturing, commercial, defense contractors/research and development supporting the Aberdeen Proving Ground, military installation, and e-commerce and fulfillment centers which have access to major roads.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights opportunities for redeveloping warehouse distribution facilities into "**light manufacturing, commercial, defense contractors/research and development supporting the Aberdeen Proving Ground**, military installation, and e-commerce and fulfillment centers."

quotes.text: The purpose of the Integrated Business District (IBD) is to provide residential, recreational, educational, retail, entertainment, and other commercial uses in an aesthetically pleasing and functionally compatible manner, to complement existing residential areas, to blend development with the environmental characteristics of the land, and to facilitate the efficient delivery and use of public services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Integrated Business District zone offers developers flexibility to "**provide residential, recreational, educational, retail, entertainment, and other commercial uses in an aesthetically pleasing and functionally compatible manner**" that complements existing neighborhoods and aligns with local environmental features.

quotes.text: Look for opportunities to further encourage and incentivize affordable housing, including multi-family housing, in the City’s designated Transit Oriented Development area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address regional housing pressures, the plan urges the City to "**further encourage and incentivize affordable housing, including multi-family housing**, in the City’s designated Transit Oriented Development area."

Center stage is the Branch Avenue Metro Station area, where the community intends to foster high-density, walkable, mixed-use developments that blend multifamily residential spaces with retail and services. quotes.briefing_quote: To maximize transit-oriented development, the plan recommends that stakeholders 'explore strategies with the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority that would incentivize development of the parking lots on either side of the Metro station with a dense mix of commercial and residential uses' to build a solid consumer base for retail.

quotes.text: More than 100 acres on either side of Auth Road and Auth Way leading to the Branch Avenue Metro Station were rezoned from a combination of C-S-C, C-M and I-3 to RTO-L-e (Regional Transit-Oriented - Low Intensity [edge]), which allows a maximum of 60 dwelling units per acre.

quotes.text: There is an imbalance between the amount of existing retail space and other land uses that generate demand for retail, which has resulted in more retail space than the area can support.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the retail vacancy rates, planners highlight a key opportunity to adjust local density, noting that 'there is an imbalance between the amount of existing retail space and other land uses,' pointing to a need for more adjacent households to bolster commercial success.

quotes.text: The RSF-65 (Residential, Single-Family) subdivisions are stable with vacant lots available for additional infill housing development.

With a strong commitment to serving its diverse population, the City seeks to expand senior housing options and enhance municipal, recreational, and youth services while fostering walkable, safe, and highly connected neighborhoods.

quotes.text: One of the largest barriers to Smart Growth in the City is the lack of land for major development. The City is landlocked and most of its existing land inventory is developed.
quotes.briefing_quote: Because the City is landlocked with a fully developed land inventory, the primary avenue for smart growth lies in the "redevelopment of underutilized commercial parcels" rather than new greenfield construction.

quotes.text: The City's Smart Growth Strategy to support future opportunities for major development consists of the redevelopment of the commercial business district (CBD), and the preservation of the City's existing housing stock and natural resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: To overcome physical growth limits, the City's strategy centers on "redeveloping the commercial business district while preserving the existing housing stock and natural resources" to create sustainable development.

quotes.text: The City owns the 11-acre property behind the Aldi on Marlboro Pike, slated to become a mixed-use development with a large recreational facility and a senior housing element is proposed on site.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City has identified a key opportunity on an "11-acre municipally owned property behind the Aldi on Marlboro Pike," which is slated for a mixed-use development featuring senior housing and a major recreational facility.

quotes.text: The City's commercial corridor is oversaturated with service-oriented businesses such as beauty salons, barber shops and small convenience stores. There is no active business association, and therefore no real platform to engage business owners in discussion around the City's revitalization goals.
quotes.briefing_quote: Revitalization efforts note that the current commercial corridor is "oversaturated with service-oriented businesses," pointing to a critical need for targeted retail diversification and the establishment of a formal merchants association.

quotes.text: Support and incentivize the forthcoming mixed-use development including senior housing for the St Paul's Town Center site adjacent to Great Eastern Plaza.

By targeting revitalization within its historical core, expanding green infrastructure, and implementing forward-thinking sustainability initiatives like curbside composting and widespread EV charging, the City seeks to grow responsibly. Laurel aims to deliver a diverse and affordable housing stock, enhance multimodal transit connections (such as transit-oriented development near the MARC station), and foster inclusive public spaces that support a high quality of life for multi-generational residents.

quotes.text: LAUREL MARC - TRANSIT ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT. Located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space. The building is planned in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Transportation.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a premier transit-oriented opportunity at the Laurel MARC station, noting that 'located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space' coordinated alongside state transit partners.

quotes.text: ANDERSON’S CORNER. A mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex known as Avalon Bay (constructed), an approved 55-unit townhouse community entitled Avery Place and a Royal Farms gas station and convenience store.
quotes.briefing_quote: Anderson's Corner serves as a successful template for mixed-density development, showcasing 'a mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex, an approved 55-unit townhouse community... and a Royal Farms' convenience center.

quotes.text: WEST SIDE. A mixed-use community consisting of a 469-unit apartment complex known as Modera at Westside (constructed) and 56-unit townhouse community, which is complete. The site also has other undeveloped parcels for commercial, a hotel and a second phase townhouse development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The West Side master-planned area illustrates the demand for integrated density, featuring 'a 469-unit apartment complex... and a 56-unit townhouse community' alongside undeveloped parcels reserved for commercial space and a hotel.

quotes.text: PATUXENT GREENS GOLF COURSE. The golf course closed in December 2018. The property was approved to be re-developed into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units. The development will also include a clubhouse, swimming pool, hiker/biker trails and other community amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: Following the transition of local recreational lands, the City approved plans for Patuxent Greens 'to be redeveloped into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units' paired with extensive walkable amenities.

quotes.text: Per the City of Laurel Unified Development Code, any multifamily development of 100 dwelling units or more approved after November 23, 2020, shall include a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as work force housing units, a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as moderately priced housing units and a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as age-restricted housing units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To ensure equitable growth, the City's Unified Development Code mandates that large-scale multifamily projects deliver 'a minimum of four percent workforce housing, four percent moderately priced housing, and four percent age-restricted housing.'

quotes.text: The redevelopment of the Main Street area and the retention of commercial uses is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability and attract shoppers.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan underscores that proactive commercial retention 'is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability.'

quotes.text: Encourage a substantial portion of future housing stock to be single-family detached homes, including high-quality custom-built homes. Strategy B: Preserve and restore single-family residences within the Historic Districts.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing strategies focus on preservation and diversity, seeking to 'encourage a substantial portion of future housing stock to be single-family detached homes, including high-quality custom-built homes' while safeguarding historic structures.

quotes.text: Compact, mixed-use, walkable design consistent with existing community character and located near available or planned transit options is encouraged to ensure efficient use of land and transportation resources and preservation and enhancement of natural system, open spaces, recreational area, and historical, cultural, and archeological resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City strongly favors sustainable design frameworks, stating that 'compact, mixed-use, walkable design consistent with existing community character and located near available or planned transit options is encouraged' to optimize resources.

quotes.text: In 2010 the City of Mount Rainier purchased underutilized and abandoned properties and combined them into a parcel on 3200 Rhode Island Avenue and Eastern Avenue, the Washington DC borderline. In 2020 the City sold the property to the IFG Group. Their mixed-use development project consists of 97 condominiums, 11 street-level retail outlets and a 2 level underground parking garage.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a key redevelopment milestone at the Washington D.C. border where the City "purchased underutilized and abandoned properties and combined them into a parcel on 3200 Rhode Island Avenue and Eastern Avenue... [selling] the property to the IFG Group" for a mixed-use project consisting of 97 condominiums and 11 street-level retail outlets.

quotes.text: The Singer Building, a long vacant historic landmark on Rhode Island Ave at Perry Street has been completely renovated by The Menkiti Group and is open for business. The mixed-use development has 12 residential units (fully leased) and 3 new business establishments operating within 10,000 sq. ft. of retail space.
quotes.briefing_quote: Illustrating the success of local adaptive reuse, the plan notes that "The Singer Building, a long vacant historic landmark on Rhode Island Avenue at Perry Street has been completely renovated... [into a] mixed-use development with 12 residential units (fully leased) and 3 new business establishments."

quotes.text: The expansion of housing choice in the Mount Rainier Community is designed to be located in the MUTC where the city currently owns property. This is virtually the only existing area excluding a few lots in the city which are privately owned to building additional housing. The current policy is to create development of high quality without the need to access services by car. In addition, housing will be energy efficient and make use of environmentally sensitive design. Housing will increase from 100-200 units depending upon the configuration of the development according to several developers that the city has consulted with. Workforce housing will consist of approximately 8-10% of the total units.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing future growth, the plan states that the expansion of housing choice is targeted for the Mixed-Use Town Center, noting that "housing will increase from 100-200 units depending upon the configuration of the development" with workforce housing comprising about 8 to 10 percent of the units.

quotes.text: Many vacant commercial properties are privately owned and often these owners are primarily interested in leasing the properties for way above market value rate in anticipation of the speculative influx of Washington DC residents moving into the city based upon our rising housing prices and potential economic boom.
quotes.briefing_quote: Economic development officials noted a significant barrier to commercial retail growth, explaining that "many vacant commercial properties are privately owned and often these owners are primarily interested in leasing the properties for way above market value rate in anticipation of the speculative influx of Washington DC residents."

quotes.text: Vacant and underutilized sites on Rhode Island Avenue give the appearance of a deteriorating commercial environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize the downtown corridor, the plan emphasizes the need to address aesthetic and vacancy challenges, observing that "vacant and underutilized sites on Rhode Island Avenue give the appearance of a deteriorating commercial environment."

quotes.text: Mount Rainier is considered one of the last affordable housing areas in Prince George's County with homes averaging between $200k and $300k. Since property values had previously remained affordable, many homes have not suffered the 'mansionization' trend of 'flippers' doing poor quality renovations and expansions.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting the preservation of neighborhood character, the document notes that Mount Rainier remains "one of the last affordable housing areas in Prince George's County," which has protected many historic homes from the "mansionization" trend of lower-quality flipped expansions.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Catonsville-Patapsco community envisions a sustainable, well-connected, and culturally vibrant future. Key aspirations include expanding the local arts ecosystem through the newly designated Catonsville Arts and Entertainment District along Frederick Road, improving active transportation and trail connectivity via groups like Catonsville Rails to Trails, and preserving watershed resources near Patapsco Valley State Park. The community aims to revitalize legacy neighborhoods, address commercial vacancies, and expand quality housing choices—including affordable housing partnerships and accessory dwelling units (ADUs)—while navigating existing low-density zoning constraints that historically limit larger-scale infill development.

Under this vision, future development will increasingly focus on mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects on previously developed sites, guiding new investment and redevelopment to older commercial corridors while preserving the unique character of existing low-density neighborhoods, waterfront communities, and agricultural lands.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Where raw land for new housing is in short supply, which is the future for Annapolis, restrictive zoning rules worsen affordability.

quotes.text: The B-1 zoning stated purpose and intent is "to encourage the provision of small, safe, attractive and well-located shopping areas for primarily pedestrian use in a manner that will make them compatible assets to the residential environment."

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Frederick's vision, driven by its CommUNITY 2030 Strategic Plan and 2020 Comprehensive Plan, focuses on sustainable, equitable development across three distinct corridors: Downtown, the Golden Mile, and East Frederick. The community seeks to revitalize underutilized commercial areas and preserve its historic character through selective redevelopment, adaptive reuse, and strategic infill. Key goals include diversifying and increasing housing options (especially affordable and multi-family residential units), enhancing multi-modal transportation systems with shared-use paths, implementing form-based codes to encourage vibrant mixed-use environments, and fostering robust public-private collaborations to ensure high quality of life for all residents.

quotes.text: The amendment eliminated the restriction on the density to make the maximum density for DB zoned properties the same in the CCO as it is outside of the CCO. It also increased the density beyond the maximum density allowed under Section 405 when structured parking is built as part of a development project.
quotes.briefing_quote: A text amendment to the Carroll Creek Overlay District "eliminated the restriction on the density" and allowed increases beyond the maximum permitted density when structured parking is built, opening up new opportunities for high-density downtown housing.

quotes.text: Investment in the construction of 249 new multifamily rental units and 12 condominium units for sale to low to moderate income households.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City's partnerships with affordable housing developers have successfully driven "investment in the construction of 249 new multifamily rental units and 12 condominium units for sale" to low- and moderate-income households.

quotes.text: Improve local connectivity through dedicated bus lanes, new cross easements between shopping centers, and introduction of mixed-use development
quotes.briefing_quote: To support strategic redevelopment along the Golden Mile, the City plans to "improve local connectivity through dedicated bus lanes... and the introduction of mixed-use development."

quotes.text: Sustain the vitality of Downtown Frederick by promoting adaptive reuse/redevelopment of underutilized properties and strategic infill developments
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning documents highlight the goal to "sustain the vitality of Downtown Frederick by promoting adaptive reuse/redevelopment of underutilized properties and strategic infill developments" to meet modern housing and economic needs.

quotes.text: Ensure flexible land use regulations to allow suitable mixtures of residential and non-residential uses within new and existing development
quotes.briefing_quote: The City aims to "ensure flexible land use regulations to allow suitable mixtures of residential and non-residential uses" within both new and existing developments.

quotes.text: Consider creating an Affordable Housing Fund with a dedicated stream of revenue. For example, tax rental units owned by non-City residents at a higher rate and place the difference in the AHF to discourage investors from buying up properties within the City.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City is exploring strategies to support affordable housing, such as "creating an Affordable Housing Fund with a dedicated stream of revenue" to discourage out-of-town investors from buying up properties.

plan_quotes.community_vision: By 2030, the City of Frederick aspires to be a welcoming, progressive, and authentically charming community of over 85,000 residents. The City intends to manage sustainable urban development that balances economic prosperity with housing, employment, and cultural opportunities for everyone. Through active civic engagement, Frederick aims to strengthen its vibrant downtown and diverse, walkable neighborhoods, supported by well-coordinated, multimodal transportation choices that connect residents locally and regionally.

quotes.text: Except for the Downtown area, the majority of the City’s residential neighborhoods are characterized by lower densities, wider streets, and uniformity in the types of structures and styles. quotes.briefing_quote: Urban planners noted that, outside of the downtown core, 'the majority of the City’s residential neighborhoods are characterized by lower densities... Low-density residential districts drive land consumption rates and generally create the most infrastructure demand.'

quotes.text: One of the concerns consistently stressed by residents is the segregation of land uses and the lack of nearby supporting retail and service uses. This segregation of land uses contributes to an increase in the length and number of automobile trips.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public workshops, citizens consistently voiced concern regarding 'the segregation of land uses and the lack of nearby supporting retail and service uses,' urging the City to encourage mixed-use neighborhoods to reduce dependency on cars.

quotes.text: The majority of the existing strip centers give little regard for efficiently integrated vehicular and pedestrian access. To provide a more coherent and more attractive environment, future redevelopment along these corridors should be integrated with surrounding businesses and neighborhoods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes that 'the majority of the existing strip centers give little regard for efficiently integrated vehicular and pedestrian access,' recommending that future commercial corridor redevelopments tie seamlessly back into surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: The residential land uses are proposed at greater densities than previously approved by City Comprehensive Plans. The purpose of this is to provide incentives towards infill and redevelopment and to encourage a higher population served by existing services and utilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To leverage existing infrastructure, 'residential land uses are proposed at greater densities than previously approved' to incentivize urban infill and support a growing downtown customer base.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Glen Burnie aspires to revitalize its historic Town Center into an attractive, vibrant, and walkable destination. By leveraging flexible zoning overlays, public-private partnerships, and multimodal transportation enhancements, the community aims to stimulate the redevelopment of underutilized commercial corridors while preserving and upgrading its diverse, affordable housing stock to support a younger, growing workforce.
geographic_addresses: 7409 Baltimore Annapolis Blvd, Glen Burnie, MD

Dorsey Road & Cromwell Light Rail Station, Glen Burnie, MD

quotes.text: The County’s efforts to secure a private developer to redevelop the large County property at 7409 Baltimore Annapolis Boulevard in the Town Center with new residential and retail uses were not successful and so must begin again.
quotes.briefing_quote: The renewal plan details a key opportunity for mixed-use development, noting that 'The County’s efforts to secure a private developer to redevelop the large County property at 7409 Baltimore Annapolis Boulevard in the Town Center with new residential and retail uses were not successful and so must begin again.'

quotes.text: Due to the lack of vacant land, it is difficult for Glen Burnie to attract newer businesses or office parks since location in Glen Burnie will typically require renovation of an older building or redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the constraints of commercial infill development, the report emphasizes that 'Due to the lack of vacant land, it is difficult for Glen Burnie to attract newer businesses or office parks since location in Glen Burnie will typically require renovation of an older building or redevelopment.'

quotes.text: Legislation was passed in 2020 to establish a Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay within the County’s zoning and development codes. The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To catalyze local investment, the plan highlights that 'The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.'

quotes.text: Additionally, newer residential and commercial development near Arundel Mills, Fort Meade, BWI Airport, and in other areas where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Acknowledging regional market headwinds, the application notes that 'newer residential and commercial development... where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.'

quotes.text: While no major affordable rental developments are planned in Glen Burnie at this time, the County has supported the redevelopment and preservation of existing affordable units when possible.
quotes.briefing_quote: In outlining housing goals, the application specifies that 'While no major affordable rental developments are planned in Glen Burnie at this time, the County has supported the redevelopment and preservation of existing affordable units when possible.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Odenton-Severn community envisions a vibrant, walkable, transit-oriented future centered around the Odenton Town Center and MARC Station, while simultaneously preserving, rehabilitating, and stabilizing affordable housing options in established Severn neighborhoods. Growth is guided by a commitment to expanding multimodal transportation connectivity, delivering inclusive community spaces, and leveraging strong regional economic drivers like Fort George G. Meade to attract diverse employment and retail opportunities.

quotes.text: There has been a long-standing need to increase parking capacity for commuters at the Odenton MARC Station, ideally through redevelopment of the surface parking area to include a parking garage with increased capacity combined with new office, retail, and or residential uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners highlighted a transformative opportunity at the transit station, noting a 'long-standing need to increase parking capacity... ideally through redevelopment of the surface parking area to include a parking garage with increased capacity combined with new office, retail, and or residential uses.'

quotes.text: Relaxing the required mixed-use ratios to improve flexibility for developers while improving opportunities for the private sector to provide community amenities
quotes.briefing_quote: To incentivize well-rounded growth, the updated Master Plan includes 'relaxing the required mixed-use ratios to improve flexibility for developers while improving opportunities for the private sector to provide community amenities.'

quotes.text: Some of the older retail and office establishments need to be updated or revitalized, particularly along MD 175, and their appearance detracts from this gateway corridor and may discourage potential users.
quotes.briefing_quote: County economic development reviews indicate an opportunity to reinvest in primary corridors, pointing out that 'some of the older retail and office establishments need to be updated or revitalized, particularly along MD 175' to improve this key gateway corridor.

quotes.text: In addition to addressing the Countywide need for more affordable housing, this will help to achieve the goal of providing more affordable units near public transit opportunities in the Odenton Town Center as well as near Fort George G. Meade.
quotes.briefing_quote: In alignment with new housing policies, local housing advocates emphasize that these efforts will 'help to achieve the goal of providing more affordable units near public transit opportunities in the Odenton Town Center as well as near Fort George G. Meade.'

quotes.text: The Odenton Town Center would benefit from more employment and retail uses in its Core; however, market trends and competition from other commercial and office developments in West County have made it more difficult to attract these uses in the Town Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning staff noted that despite regional competition, the community 'would benefit from more employment and retail uses in its Core' to solidify its status as a complete, mixed-use hub.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Calvert County seeks to maintain its high quality of life by balancing environmental protection, social equity, and economic growth. The community envisions a future where the rural landscape remains dominated by fields and forests, and growth is successfully directed away from these areas and concentrated within vibrant, attractive, and walkable Town Centers. These designated growth centers are intended to offer a mix of housing, retail, and commercial options, creating convenient and interesting places to live, work, and shop.
geographic_addresses: Old Town Road & Hunting Creek Road, Huntingtown, MD
Thomas Street & MD 260, Owings, MD
Appeal Lane & MD 2/4, Lusby, MD
Stoakley Road & Prince Frederick Boulevard, Prince Frederick, MD
MD 2/4 & MD 231, Prince Frederick, MD

quotes.text: Nearly 85 percent of Calvert County residential development is categorized as low or very low density development. Most of the residential development has occurred outside the Town Centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: A baseline assessment of local housing reveals that nearly 85 percent of residential development is categorized as low or very low density, occurring mostly outside designated Town Centers, presenting a major opportunity to rebalance growth toward the county's core nodes.

quotes.text: A mixed-use center is envisioned with a focus on multi-family housing and more public open space.
quotes.briefing_quote: For the Prince Frederick area, planners envision a vibrant mixed-use center with a focus on multi-family housing and more public open space to create a more dynamic and walkable core.

quotes.text: The overall appearances of Town Centers are somewhat different from the vision, and achieving walkable, bikeable neighborhoods has proven elusive... Many commercial areas look more like strip centers than mixed use, pedestrian-friendly communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: While past growth patterns have resembled vehicle-centric strip centers, community workshop participants strongly emphasize the opportunity to redevelop existing commercial areas into mixed-use, pedestrian-friendly communities with complete sidewalk and bicycle networks.

quotes.text: Explore the potential to incorporate multi-family housing into commercial areas to bring uses closer together and allow for redevelopment and infill housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To foster vibrant, walkable environments, the plan recommends that developers and county partners explore the potential to incorporate multi-family housing into commercial areas to bring uses closer together and allow for active infill redevelopment.

quotes.text: Do not permit additional commercial and retail development along highways outside Town Centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: In an effort to prevent sprawling auto-dependent corridors, county directives specify that they will not permit additional commercial and retail development along highways outside Town Centers, driving future business density into designated town cores.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Odenton-Severn community envisions a vibrant, walkable, transit-oriented future centered around the Odenton Town Center and MARC Station, while simultaneously preserving, rehabilitating, and stabilizing affordable housing options in established Severn neighborhoods. Growth is guided by a commitment to expanding multimodal transportation connectivity, delivering inclusive community spaces, and leveraging strong regional economic drivers like Fort George G. Meade to attract diverse employment and retail opportunities.

quotes.text: There has been a long-standing need to increase parking capacity for commuters at the Odenton MARC Station, ideally through redevelopment of the surface parking area to include a parking garage with increased capacity combined with new office, retail, and or residential uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners highlighted a transformative opportunity at the transit station, noting a 'long-standing need to increase parking capacity... ideally through redevelopment of the surface parking area to include a parking garage with increased capacity combined with new office, retail, and or residential uses.'

quotes.text: Relaxing the required mixed-use ratios to improve flexibility for developers while improving opportunities for the private sector to provide community amenities
quotes.briefing_quote: To incentivize well-rounded growth, the updated Master Plan includes 'relaxing the required mixed-use ratios to improve flexibility for developers while improving opportunities for the private sector to provide community amenities.'

quotes.text: Some of the older retail and office establishments need to be updated or revitalized, particularly along MD 175, and their appearance detracts from this gateway corridor and may discourage potential users.
quotes.briefing_quote: County economic development reviews indicate an opportunity to reinvest in primary corridors, pointing out that 'some of the older retail and office establishments need to be updated or revitalized, particularly along MD 175' to improve this key gateway corridor.

quotes.text: In addition to addressing the Countywide need for more affordable housing, this will help to achieve the goal of providing more affordable units near public transit opportunities in the Odenton Town Center as well as near Fort George G. Meade.
quotes.briefing_quote: In alignment with new housing policies, local housing advocates emphasize that these efforts will 'help to achieve the goal of providing more affordable units near public transit opportunities in the Odenton Town Center as well as near Fort George G. Meade.'

quotes.text: The Odenton Town Center would benefit from more employment and retail uses in its Core; however, market trends and competition from other commercial and office developments in West County have made it more difficult to attract these uses in the Town Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning staff noted that despite regional competition, the community 'would benefit from more employment and retail uses in its Core' to solidify its status as a complete, mixed-use hub.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
