quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

community_organizations: Set the Captives Free Outreach, Worship and Education (OWE) Center

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community where residents enjoy a top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, and innovative businesses. The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.
geographic_addresses: Frederick Road & Triadelphia Road, Ellicott City, MD
Broken Land Parkway & Snowden River Parkway, Columbia, MD
Woodland Road & Route 108, Ellicott City, MD
Sanner Road & Johns Hopkins Road, Clarksville, MD
Snowden River Parkway & Oakland Mills Road, Columbia, MD

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Anne Arundel County envisions a future where it embraces its rich Chesapeake culture, heritage, and invaluable ecosystems while directing growth toward smart, green, and equitable development. Under this vision, future development will increasingly focus on mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects on previously developed sites, guiding new investment and redevelopment to older commercial corridors while preserving the unique character of existing low-density neighborhoods, waterfront communities, and agricultural lands.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."

plan_quotes.area_name: Patrick Street Corridor - The City of Frederick
plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Frederick's vision, driven by its CommUNITY 2030 Strategic Plan and 2020 Comprehensive Plan, focuses on sustainable, equitable development across three distinct corridors: Downtown, the Golden Mile, and East Frederick. The community seeks to revitalize underutilized commercial areas and preserve its historic character through selective redevelopment, adaptive reuse, and strategic infill. Key goals include diversifying and increasing housing options (especially affordable and multi-family residential units), enhancing multi-modal transportation systems with shared-use paths, implementing form-based codes to encourage vibrant mixed-use environments, and fostering robust public-private collaborations to ensure high quality of life for all residents.
geographic_addresses: 140 W Patrick Street, Frederick, MD
Old Camp Road & Waverly Drive, Frederick, MD

quotes.text: The amendment eliminated the restriction on the density to make the maximum density for DB zoned properties the same in the CCO as it is outside of the CCO. It also increased the density beyond the maximum density allowed under Section 405 when structured parking is built as part of a development project.
quotes.briefing_quote: A text amendment to the Carroll Creek Overlay District "eliminated the restriction on the density" and allowed increases beyond the maximum permitted density when structured parking is built, opening up new opportunities for high-density downtown housing.

quotes.text: Investment in the construction of 249 new multifamily rental units and 12 condominium units for sale to low to moderate income households.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City's partnerships with affordable housing developers have successfully driven "investment in the construction of 249 new multifamily rental units and 12 condominium units for sale" to low- and moderate-income households.

quotes.text: Improve local connectivity through dedicated bus lanes, new cross easements between shopping centers, and introduction of mixed-use development
quotes.briefing_quote: To support strategic redevelopment along the Golden Mile, the City plans to "improve local connectivity through dedicated bus lanes... and the introduction of mixed-use development."

quotes.text: Sustain the vitality of Downtown Frederick by promoting adaptive reuse/redevelopment of underutilized properties and strategic infill developments
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning documents highlight the goal to "sustain the vitality of Downtown Frederick by promoting adaptive reuse/redevelopment of underutilized properties and strategic infill developments" to meet modern housing and economic needs.

quotes.text: Ensure flexible land use regulations to allow suitable mixtures of residential and non-residential uses within new and existing development
quotes.briefing_quote: The City aims to "ensure flexible land use regulations to allow suitable mixtures of residential and non-residential uses" within both new and existing developments.

quotes.text: Consider creating an Affordable Housing Fund with a dedicated stream of revenue. For example, tax rental units owned by non-City residents at a higher rate and place the difference in the AHF to discourage investors from buying up properties within the City.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City is exploring strategies to support affordable housing, such as "creating an Affordable Housing Fund with a dedicated stream of revenue" to discourage out-of-town investors from buying up properties.

plan_quotes.community_vision: By 2030, the City of Frederick aspires to be a welcoming, progressive, and authentically charming community of over 85,000 residents. The City intends to manage sustainable urban development that balances economic prosperity with housing, employment, and cultural opportunities for everyone. Through active civic engagement, Frederick aims to strengthen its vibrant downtown and diverse, walkable neighborhoods, supported by well-coordinated, multimodal transportation choices that connect residents locally and regionally.

quotes.text: The rise in population has resulted in the developments and investments in newly annexed lands, along with denser and compact infill development in and around the downtown core.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that rapid growth has spurred 'developments and investments in newly annexed lands, along with denser and compact infill development in and around the downtown core' to serve as a catalyst for a vibrant city center.

quotes.text: Except for the Downtown area, the majority of the City’s residential neighborhoods are characterized by lower densities, wider streets, and uniformity in the types of structures and styles. Low-density residential districts drive land consumption rates and generally create the most infrastructure demand.
quotes.briefing_quote: Urban planners noted that, outside of the downtown core, 'the majority of the City’s residential neighborhoods are characterized by lower densities... Low-density residential districts drive land consumption rates and generally create the most infrastructure demand.'

quotes.text: One of the concerns consistently stressed by residents is the segregation of land uses and the lack of nearby supporting retail and service uses. This segregation of land uses contributes to an increase in the length and number of automobile trips.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public workshops, citizens consistently voiced concern regarding 'the segregation of land uses and the lack of nearby supporting retail and service uses,' urging the City to encourage mixed-use neighborhoods to reduce dependency on cars.

quotes.text: The majority of the existing strip centers give little regard for efficiently integrated vehicular and pedestrian access. To provide a more coherent and more attractive environment, future redevelopment along these corridors should be integrated with surrounding businesses and neighborhoods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes that 'the majority of the existing strip centers give little regard for efficiently integrated vehicular and pedestrian access,' recommending that future commercial corridor redevelopments tie seamlessly back into surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: The residential land uses are proposed at greater densities than previously approved by City Comprehensive Plans. The purpose of this is to provide incentives towards infill and redevelopment and to encourage a higher population served by existing services and utilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To leverage existing infrastructure, 'residential land uses are proposed at greater densities than previously approved' to incentivize urban infill and support a growing downtown customer base.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Walkersville envisions preserving its distinctive small-town identity and rural heritage by limiting rapid residential growth and maintaining a permanent agricultural buffer that isolates the town from surrounding urban expansion. The town aims to carefully coordinate future land use with public infrastructure, promoting pedestrian-friendly neighborhood businesses, preserving historic assets, and encouraging limited industrial growth in designated employment corridors to broaden the local tax base while safeguarding natural resources.

quotes.text: Consider zoning standards that would allow neighborhoods with a mix of housing types and sizes that can accommodate a variety of households, including renters and owners.
quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate diverse community needs, the plan recommends that developers and city officials 'consider zoning standards that would allow neighborhoods with a mix of housing types and sizes that can accommodate a variety of households, including renters and owners.'

quotes.text: Seek partners and funding to increase the supply of housing for the senior population, including developments that support aging in place.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address demographic shifts, the plan highlights an opportunity to 'seek partners and funding to increase the supply of housing for the senior population, including developments that support aging in place.'

quotes.text: Permit apartments in Old Town and B-1 Neighborhood Business districts, as well as the R-3 and R-4 Residential districts.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan encourages expanding density in commercial nodes by recommending policies to 'permit apartments in Old Town and Neighborhood Business districts, as well as the R-3 and R-4 Residential districts.'

quotes.text: Review and amend the Zoning Ordinance requirements to permit accessory dwelling units and tiny houses, and develop criteria and conditions for their approval.
quotes.briefing_quote: To encourage creative housing options, the town aims to 'review and amend the Zoning Ordinance requirements to permit accessory dwelling units and tiny houses, and develop criteria and conditions for their approval.'

quotes.text: The LI and LIP district regulations should be reviewed to refocus the districts on wholesaling, warehousing, limited manufacturing and assembly uses, offices, research laboratories and other employment uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: To stimulate local economic development, the plan indicates that 'the Limited Industrial and Limited Industrial Park district regulations should be reviewed to refocus the districts on wholesaling, warehousing, limited manufacturing and assembly uses, offices, research laboratories and other employment uses.'

quotes.text: The B-1 zoning stated purpose and intent is "to encourage the provision of small, safe, attractive and well-located shopping areas for primarily pedestrian use in a manner that will make them compatible assets to the residential environment."
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that the Neighborhood Business zoning intends 'to encourage the provision of small, safe, attractive and well-located shopping areas for primarily pedestrian use' as compatible assets to the neighborhood.

quotes.text: Adaptive reuse of old commercial/industrial structures can be difficult due to lack of flexibility of the zoning code.
quotes.briefing_quote: To clear barriers for historic preservation, the plan observes that 'adaptive reuse of old commercial and industrial structures can be difficult due to lack of flexibility of the zoning code,' signaling a key area for potential zoning updates.

quotes.text: When asked what types of development they would like to see more of in Walkersville, restaurants and neighborhood business were cited most frequently (by nearly 70% and 47% of respondents, respectively).
quotes.briefing_quote: Reflecting local preferences, community survey respondents indicated that 'restaurants and neighborhood business were cited most frequently' as the highly desired commercial additions to the town.

quotes.text: Except for the Downtown area, the majority of the City’s residential neighborhoods are characterized by lower densities, wider streets, and uniformity in the types of structures and styles. quotes.text: One of the concerns consistently stressed by residents is the segregation of land uses and the lack of nearby supporting retail and service uses. This segregation of land uses contributes to an increase in the length and number of automobile trips.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public workshops, citizens consistently voiced concern regarding 'the segregation of land uses and the lack of nearby supporting retail and service uses,' urging the City to encourage mixed-use neighborhoods to reduce dependency on cars.

quotes.text: The majority of the existing strip centers give little regard for efficiently integrated vehicular and pedestrian access. quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes that 'the majority of the existing strip centers give little regard for efficiently integrated vehicular and pedestrian access,' recommending that future commercial corridor redevelopments tie seamlessly back into surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: The residential land uses are proposed at greater densities than previously approved by City Comprehensive Plans. The purpose of this is to provide incentives towards infill and redevelopment and to encourage a higher population served by existing services and utilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To leverage existing infrastructure, 'residential land uses are proposed at greater densities than previously approved' to incentivize urban infill and support a growing downtown customer base.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD
Cowenton Avenue & Pulaski Highway, White Marsh, MD
Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

community_organizations: Set the Captives Free Outreach, Worship and Education (OWE) Center

plan_quotes.community_vision: Arbutus aspires to transition into a vibrant "college town" leveraging its proximity to the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) while carefully protecting the area's historic single-family character and small-town charm. The community aims to capitalize on its strategic role as a logistics and technology hub, revitalizing key commercial corridors like East Drive and Linden Avenue with diverse retail, arts, and mixed-use transit-oriented developments that serve residents and students alike.
geographic_addresses: Waelchi Avenue & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Linden Avenue & Shelbourne Road, Arbutus, MD
Shelbourne Road & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Tom Day & Southwestern Boulevard, Arbutus, MD

quotes.text: The proposed Arbutus Station is a mixed-use development by a local developer at the intersection of Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road. It is within the proposed Sustainable Community boundary and the County's Commercial Revitalization District that can take advantage of the County's revitalization programs if it meets the County revitalization goals and efforts. The project is now submitted for Department's review and approval. The community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: With proposals like Arbutus Station at Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road, "the community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan."

quotes.text: Finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners. Though the community is always looking for prospective homeowners, there is a lack of rental options to attract the UMBC students and programs to benefit both the landlords and student renters. At the same time the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup discussions highlighted the challenge of "finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners," noting that while there is a lack of student rental options, "the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership."

quotes.text: Bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques similar to Ellicott City and Catonsville.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local economic strategies emphasize the desire to "bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques" to the commercial district, modeling success after nearby Ellicott City and Catonsville.

quotes.text: Convene group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: To preserve neighborhood character, the plan recommends convening a "group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community."

quotes.text: Obtain funding and acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs and UMBC students.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address community health and quality of life, stakeholders recommend seeking funding to "acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs" and support the growing student population.

community_organizations: Wilkens Police and Community Relations Organization

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Catonsville-Patapsco community envisions a sustainable, well-connected, and culturally vibrant future. Key aspirations include expanding the local arts ecosystem through the newly designated Catonsville Arts and Entertainment District along Frederick Road, improving active transportation and trail connectivity via groups like Catonsville Rails to Trails, and preserving watershed resources near Patapsco Valley State Park. The community aims to revitalize legacy neighborhoods, address commercial vacancies, and expand quality housing choices—including affordable housing partnerships and accessory dwelling units (ADUs)—while navigating existing low-density zoning constraints that historically limit larger-scale infill development.

quotes.text: Scarcity of undeveloped properties within residential and commercial zones, thereby limiting the potential for larger scale new development or infill
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes a 'scarcity of undeveloped properties within residential and commercial zones, thereby limiting the potential for larger-scale new development or infill,' highlighting the critical importance of strategic infill projects.

quotes.text: Barriers to higher density development (including policies, development process, NIMBYs).
quotes.briefing_quote: The assessment identifies clear 'barriers to higher density development (including policies, development process, NIMBYs)' that must be navigated to successfully introduce multi-family and mixed-use options.

quotes.text: The majority of zoning in the Catonsville SC area is low density residential, that primarily supports single family development. ... The current residential zoning in the majority of the SC Area does not easily support higher density development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning staff emphasized that 'the majority of zoning in the Catonsville Sustainable Community Area is low density residential, which primarily supports single family development' and does not easily accommodate higher density development styles.

quotes.text: Zoning changes occur through the County’s CZMP process... several of these requests for change were denied, though a few were approved to allow for mixed uses along MD 144.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recent comprehensive zoning reviews show progress, noting that while some requests were denied, 'a few were approved to allow for mixed uses along MD 144' to align with main street commercial revitalization goals.

quotes.text: Support the development of new accessory dwelling units (ADUs) within appropriate settings within the SC area through the development process and policy development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community intends to 'support the development of new accessory dwelling units (ADUs) within appropriate settings within the Sustainable Community Area through the development process and policy development' to broaden localized residential choices.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

community_organizations: Arts & Humanities Council of Montgomery County

plan_quotes.community_vision: Langley Park envisions transitioning into a vibrant, transit-oriented gateway that leverages the construction of the Purple Line light rail while preserving its naturally occurring affordable housing and rich cultural diversity. The community seeks to revitalize its commercial districts—especially the International Corridor—through denser, mixed-use development, streetscape beautification, and creative placemaking. Addressing persistent infrastructure and social challenges, the plan aims to improve pedestrian and bicycle safety, modernize aging multifamily rental housing, preserve environmental assets like the Northwest Branch Trail, and elevate the quality of life through enhanced health, language, and youth recreation services.
geographic_addresses: 8300 Adelphi Road, Hyattsville, MD
8910 Riggs Road, Hyattsville, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Langley Park, MD
New Hampshire Avenue & Riggs Road, Langley Park, MD
University Boulevard & Adelphi Road, Adelphi, MD

quotes.text: Support TOD and denser mixed-use development in coordination with the construction of the Purple Line to provide denser retail typologies different from the existing strip retail centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: To leverage incoming transit investments, the plan recommends that developers 'support TOD [Transit-Oriented Development] and denser mixed-use development in coordination with the construction of the Purple Line to provide denser retail typologies different from the existing strip retail centers.'

quotes.text: The housing stock is predominantly aging multi-family apartment units. Most of these units were built in the 1950s, when lead paint and asbestos were used in housing construction. Many of these units have not been substantially upgraded.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community highlights a critical need for modernization, noting that the local 'housing stock is predominantly aging multi-family apartment units' constructed in the 1950s, which creates a prime opportunity to substantially upgrade and improve multifamily conditions.

quotes.text: Increase the number of affordable rental housing units that include 3 and 4 bedrooms to accommodate larger families and prevent overcrowding.
quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate local household structures, community leaders identify a pressing need to 'increase the number of affordable rental housing units that include 3 and 4 bedrooms to accommodate larger families and prevent overcrowding.'

quotes.text: In 2021, the Prince George’s County Planning Department completed the Takoma/Langley Crossroads Planning and Implementation Study, which builds on the 2019 Approved Takoma Langley Sector Plan by developing implementation tools and strategies to support denser, mixed use and walkable development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning frameworks support forward-looking projects, specifically 'developing implementation tools and strategies to support denser, mixed use and walkable development' around key transit nodes.

Prince George’s County-Metro Maryland Habitat for Humanity

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aims to foster a well-planned, livable, and safe community that offers a high quality of life for its growing, aging, and increasingly diverse population. Guided by Thrive Montgomery 2050, the county's vision centers on compact, walkable, and mixed-use development supported by strong pedestrian, bicycle, and transit infrastructure to drive economic competitiveness, environmental resilience, and racial equity.

quotes.text: A third of all County land has zoning that generally only allows detached housing leaving limited land available for medium to high density housing
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "a third of all County land has zoning that generally only allows detached housing," which severely restricts the availability of land for much-needed medium- to high-density residential options.

quotes.text: Too few rental communities that offer family-sized units of three- or more bedrooms.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county identifies a gap in multi-family development, stating there are "too few rental communities that offer family-sized units of three or more bedrooms," presenting an active opportunity for developer focus.

quotes.text: Sustained remote work has increased commercial vacancy rates
quotes.briefing_quote: The county highlights commercial real estate challenges, noting that "sustained remote work has increased commercial vacancy rates," pointing to opportunities for commercial repositioning or adaptive re-use.

quotes.text: Elizabeth Square, located in downtown Silver Spring, is a multi-generational, mixed-income, mixed-use project featuring residential coupled with a state-of-the-art recreation facility and other community amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights successful mixed-use models like Elizabeth Square, describing it as "a multi-generational, mixed-income, mixed-use project featuring residential coupled with a state-of-the-art recreation facility" and civic amenities.

quotes.text: Inadequate supply of affordable housing to address population’s needs and variety of income levels, specifically for elderly, very low-income levels, and people with disabilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: County planning documents address housing gaps, noting an "inadequate supply of affordable housing to address population's needs and variety of income levels," specifically for seniors and residents with disabilities.

quotes.text: Since the last application, we have identified several communities facing such dire, long-standing safety-related interior and exterior building hazards needing immediate repair/replacement, including Hermitage Woods in the Aspen Hill area... built in 1973 this multi-story, apartment-to-condo 37-unit complex units has such extensive structural damage that it is on the verge of being condemned
quotes.briefing_quote: The application emphasizes the urgent need for reinvestment in aging properties, noting several multi-family complexes face "dire, long-standing safety-related interior and exterior building hazards needing immediate repair or replacement."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Garrett County aspires to enhance the quality of life enjoyed by its residents by actively preserving its rural character, farmland, and natural beauty while carefully guiding growth and development. The community seeks to establish a balanced trajectory that expands diverse housing options, supports local businesses and agritourism, plans for modern infrastructure (including universal broadband), and creates high-quality employment opportunities while conserving its abundant open spaces and outdoor recreational assets.

quotes.text: Town Residential (TR) areas provide for higher density, more compact development near incorporated towns, rural villages (such as Bittinger and Swanton), and other places such as McHenry, and Thayerville. Development densities in TR areas are up to eight multi-family dwelling units per acre and approximately four to five single-family dwelling units per acre in areas served by public water and sewer. TR areas can accommodate a mix of housing types, including single family detached, townhouses, and apartments.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better accommodate multi-family options near population centers, the plan designates Town Residential zones to provide for "higher density, more compact development... up to eight multi-family dwelling units per acre" in areas served by public utilities.

quotes.text: TC areas, unlike TR areas, are mixed use areas where a variety of retail, service, and commercial uses can be intermixed with residential uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planners highlight the potential of Town Center zones to create vibrant nodes, describing them as "mixed use areas where a variety of retail, service, and commercial uses can be intermixed with residential uses."

quotes.text: Recommendations were made to, among other things, minimize developable areas, maintain contiguous forests and agricultural lands to the maximum extent possible, cluster new development, preserve viewsheds...
quotes.briefing_quote: To balance low-density development with conservation, the plan recommends measures to "minimize developable areas, maintain contiguous forests and agricultural lands... [and] cluster new development" within rural and resource-sensitive areas.

quotes.text: Concentrated commercial development promotes the economic use of land including sharing facilities such as parking and storm water management.
quotes.briefing_quote: In contrast to linear highway sprawl, the county emphasizes that "concentrated commercial development promotes the economic use of land including sharing facilities" like parking and stormwater infrastructure.

quotes.text: There is a gap in market-rate housing, between fixer-uppers and $250,000 lake homes. It is difficult for first-time homebuyers to own, particularly young couples and young families.
quotes.briefing_quote: Superintendent Barbara Baker identified a critical entry-level housing gap, noting that there is "a gap in market-rate housing, between fixer-uppers and $250,000 lake homes" which prevents young local families from building equity.

quotes.text: According to the Council there is a need for single story 1-bedroom market-rate elderly independent people thus capturing aging retirees.
quotes.briefing_quote: During stakeholder consultations, the Mayor's Council noted that to support the aging population, "there is a need for single-story 1-bedroom market-rate" independent living options to capture and retain active retirees.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Lonaconing envisions a resilient, vibrant community that preserves its unique industrial heritage, including the historic Silk Mill and Iron Furnace, to stimulate economic growth and tourism. The Town aims to revitalize its Central Business District through streetscape and sidewalk improvements, address critical water and stormwater infrastructure deficits, promote green spaces and active trails like the Georges Creek Trail, and support its aging population by fostering new transitional housing options.

quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate its aging population, Lonaconing plans to "solicit developer interest in building high density senior housing on undeveloped properties within Town limits."

quotes.text: Despite some basic needs, retail opportunities in town are still rather limited. The nearest full-service grocery store (Weis) is more than eight miles away in Frostburg.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planning narratives emphasize a commercial deficit, noting that "retail opportunities in town are still rather limited," leaving residents to travel over eight miles to Frostburg for a full-service grocery store.

quotes.text: The historic Main St area has a healthy mix of residential and commercial uses: several small businesses exist including pharmacy, clothing boutique, credit union, Ternent & Sons lumber company, pizza shop, tavern, florist, fuel stations, auto repair, and the Dollar General.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights existing neighborhood assets, noting that "the historic Main Street area has a healthy mix of residential and commercial uses," which provides a solid baseline for downtown revitalization.

quotes.text: There is lack of building land, there is nowhere to build new houses.
quotes.briefing_quote: Residential developers should note that local growth is constrained, as "there is a lack of building land, there is nowhere to build new houses" within current municipal boundaries, making infill redevelopment highly critical.

quotes.text: In the last five years, there have been no infill developments; however, the groundwork has been laid for future infill development, and one multi-family infill housing project is currently under construction, with another planned to begin construction in the next year.

quotes.text: New development and construction is booming - especially single family homes (starting under $200,000) as affordable first-time homes
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planners highlighted that "new development and construction is booming — especially single-family homes (starting under $200,000) as affordable first-time homes," indicating a strong and accessible market for low-density residential builds.

quotes.text: The Nickel building, which has remained vacant since the Au Petit Paris restaurant closed its doors in 2012, has been purchased by a local developer who plans to completely renovate the building to include six separate commercial spaces and luxury apartments on the two upper levels.
quotes.briefing_quote: Demonstrating the viability of downtown adaptive reuse, a local developer purchased the long-vacant Nickel building with plans to "completely renovate the building to include six separate commercial spaces and luxury apartments on the two upper levels."

quotes.text: The Diamond Building, located at 43-53, was recently purchased by Rockville-based developers, who plan to rehabilitate the six main-level commercial spaces and the 9 upper-story dwelling units (the dwelling units have been listed as uninhabitable for at least five years).
quotes.briefing_quote: In a major boost to downtown mixed-use inventory, Rockville-based developers plan to "rehabilitate the six main-level commercial spaces and the nine upper-story dwelling units" of the historic Diamond Building.

quotes.text: Incentivize development of rental apartments and townhomes for younger residents who do not want to own single family homes
quotes.briefing_quote: To better serve the evolving needs of the local workforce, the plan outlines strategies to "incentivize development of rental apartments and townhomes for younger residents who do not want to own single-family homes."

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.

quotes.text: Additionally, newer residential and commercial development near Arundel Mills, Fort Meade, BWI Airport, and in other areas where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Glen Burnie aspires to revitalize its historic Town Center into an attractive, vibrant, and walkable destination. By leveraging flexible zoning overlays, public-private partnerships, and multimodal transportation enhancements, the community aims to stimulate the redevelopment of underutilized commercial corridors while preserving and upgrading its diverse, affordable housing stock to support a younger, growing workforce.

quotes.text: The County’s efforts to secure a private developer to redevelop the large County property at 7409 Baltimore Annapolis Boulevard in the Town Center with new residential and retail uses were not successful and so must begin again.
quotes.briefing_quote: The renewal plan details a key opportunity for mixed-use development, noting that 'The County’s efforts to secure a private developer to redevelop the large County property at 7409 Baltimore Annapolis Boulevard in the Town Center with new residential and retail uses were not successful and so must begin again.'

quotes.text: Due to the lack of vacant land, it is difficult for Glen Burnie to attract newer businesses or office parks since location in Glen Burnie will typically require renovation of an older building or redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the constraints of commercial infill development, the report emphasizes that 'Due to the lack of vacant land, it is difficult for Glen Burnie to attract newer businesses or office parks since location in Glen Burnie will typically require renovation of an older building or redevelopment.'

quotes.text: Legislation was passed in 2020 to establish a Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay within the County’s zoning and development codes. The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To catalyze local investment, the plan highlights that 'The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.'

quotes.text: Additionally, newer residential and commercial development near Arundel Mills, Fort Meade, BWI Airport, and in other areas where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Acknowledging regional market headwinds, the application notes that 'newer residential and commercial development... where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.'

quotes.text: While no major affordable rental developments are planned in Glen Burnie at this time, the County has supported the redevelopment and preservation of existing affordable units when possible.
quotes.briefing_quote: In outlining housing goals, the application specifies that 'While no major affordable rental developments are planned in Glen Burnie at this time, the County has supported the redevelopment and preservation of existing affordable units when possible.'

quotes.text: Due to the lack of vacant land, it is difficult for Glen Burnie to attract newer businesses or office parks since location in Glen Burnie will typically require renovation of an older building or redevelopment.

quotes.text: Legislation was passed in 2020 to establish a Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay within the County’s zoning and development codes. The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To catalyze local investment, the plan highlights that 'The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.'

quotes.text: Additionally, newer residential and commercial development near Arundel Mills, Fort Meade, BWI Airport, and in other areas where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Acknowledging regional market headwinds, the application notes that 'newer residential and commercial development... where unimproved land is still available for development, can make it difficult for older areas such as Glen Burnie to compete in attracting new development or redevelopment.'

quotes.text: While no major affordable rental developments are planned in Glen Burnie at this time, the County has supported the redevelopment and preservation of existing affordable units when possible.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Laurel envisions a sustainable, vibrant, and walkable community that balances economic growth with environmental stewardship. By targeting revitalization within its historical core, expanding green infrastructure, and implementing forward-thinking sustainability initiatives like curbside composting and widespread EV charging, the City seeks to grow responsibly. Laurel aims to deliver a diverse and affordable housing stock, enhance multimodal transit connections (such as transit-oriented development near the MARC station), and foster inclusive public spaces that support a high quality of life for multi-generational residents.

quotes.text: LAUREL MARC - TRANSIT ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT. Located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space. The building is planned in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Transportation.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a premier transit-oriented opportunity at the Laurel MARC station, noting that 'located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space' coordinated alongside state transit partners.

quotes.text: ANDERSON’S CORNER. A mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex known as Avalon Bay (constructed), an approved 55-unit townhouse community entitled Avery Place and a Royal Farms gas station and convenience store.
quotes.briefing_quote: Anderson's Corner serves as a successful template for mixed-density development, showcasing 'a mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex, an approved 55-unit townhouse community... and a Royal Farms' convenience center.

quotes.text: WEST SIDE. A mixed-use community consisting of a 469-unit apartment complex known as Modera at Westside (constructed) and 56-unit townhouse community, which is complete. The site also has other undeveloped parcels for commercial, a hotel and a second phase townhouse development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The West Side master-planned area illustrates the demand for integrated density, featuring 'a 469-unit apartment complex... and a 56-unit townhouse community' alongside undeveloped parcels reserved for commercial space and a hotel.

quotes.text: PATUXENT GREENS GOLF COURSE. The golf course closed in December 2018. The property was approved to be re-developed into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units. The development will also include a clubhouse, swimming pool, hiker/biker trails and other community amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: Following the transition of local recreational lands, the City approved plans for Patuxent Greens 'to be redeveloped into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units' paired with extensive walkable amenities.

quotes.text: Per the City of Laurel Unified Development Code, any multifamily development of 100 dwelling units or more approved after November 23, 2020, shall include a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as work force housing units, a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as moderately priced housing units and a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as age-restricted housing units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To ensure equitable growth, the City's Unified Development Code mandates that large-scale multifamily projects deliver 'a minimum of four percent workforce housing, four percent moderately priced housing, and four percent age-restricted housing.'

quotes.text: The redevelopment of the Main Street area and the retention of commercial uses is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability and attract shoppers.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan underscores that proactive commercial retention 'is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability.'

quotes.text: Encourage a substantial portion of future housing stock to be single-family detached homes, including high-quality custom-built homes. Strategy B: Preserve and restore single-family residences within the Historic Districts.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing strategies focus on preservation and diversity, seeking to 'encourage a substantial portion of future housing stock to be single-family detached homes, including high-quality custom-built homes' while safeguarding historic structures.

quotes.text: Compact, mixed-use, walkable design consistent with existing community character and located near available or planned transit options is encouraged to ensure efficient use of land and transportation resources and preservation and enhancement of natural system, open spaces, recreational area, and historical, cultural, and archeological resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City strongly favors sustainable design frameworks, stating that 'compact, mixed-use, walkable design consistent with existing community character and located near available or planned transit options is encouraged' to optimize resources.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community where residents enjoy a top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, and innovative businesses. The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The North Laurel-Savage community envisions a sustainable, walkable, and vibrant future centered on Route 1 and transit-oriented hubs like the Savage MARC station. quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that while designated activity centers and transit districts are designed for a mix of uses, they "have primarily yielded high-density residential development with limited nonresidential" retail, creating an opportunity for future developers to deliver more balanced commercial and community spaces.

quotes.text: Allow the development of residential and hotels within the transit oriented development areas to support nonresidential uses, such as office, retail, and entertainment, and increased MARC ridership.
quotes.briefing_quote: To build vibrant station areas, local guidelines recommend that planners "allow the development of residential and hotels within the transit oriented development areas to support nonresidential uses" like office, retail, and entertainment.

quotes.text: Allow sufficient residential densities in North Laurel District—defined in HoCo By Design as an area that will build on the existing transit-oriented community with an entertainment focus that both serves the needs of existing and future residents and offers a destination for neighboring communities-- to make a wide range of uses economically viable, including convenience retail and other neighborhood-serving amenities.

quotes.text: Reduction in older, smaller, more affordable single family housing units through demolition and substantial renovations that results in an increased resale value

quotes.text: Aging multi-family housing stock is in need of redevelopment or upgrades. The SC area has 9% of units that were built before 1970 and 73% of units that were built before 2000 according to Howard County’s Housing Opportunities Master Plan.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.

quotes.text: Legislation was passed in 2020 to establish a Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay within the County’s zoning and development codes. quotes.briefing_quote: To catalyze local investment, the plan highlights that 'The overlay encompasses the entire Glen Burnie Sustainable Community area and allows for flexibility in certain development regulations and zoning requirements, as well as financial incentives, to encourage redevelopment of declining and underutilized properties within the area.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: In the coming years, Annapolis aspires to become a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. quotes.text: Infill development has been ongoing in the older sections of Havre de Grace, east of US 40. From calendar years 2017 – 2021, there have been 72 new construction permits issued for infill lots. These included three completed subdivisions: 1). six luxury townhomes with water views, 2). Ivy Hills, a neighborhood of affordable homes with a mix of townhouses and duplexes, 38 of which were constructed during this timeframe, and 3). Habitat for Humanity Susquehanna’s project that included six duplex units and a single-family residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Sustainable Communities renewal report highlights that infill development has been actively ongoing in the older sections east of US Route 40, including 'seventy-two new construction permits issued for infill lots' and 'three completed subdivisions' providing a diverse mix of townhouses, duplexes, and affordable single-family residences.

quotes.text: The City has recognized for years its need for more lodging and has actively encouraged investment for a boutique hotel in Havre de Grace over the past five years. plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: St. Mary's County aims to direct growth into designated development districts and town centers like the Lexington Park Development District and Charlotte Hall, encouraging mixed-use, infill, and medium-to-high-density development. By updating the Comprehensive Plan (St. Mary's 2050) and aligning local zoning ordinances, the county seeks to foster walkable, pedestrian-friendly environments, expand public water and sewer infrastructure, and address constraints from the Patuxent River Naval Air Station's Air Installation Compatible Use Zone (AICUZ) restrictions, ultimately creating a vibrant, resilient, and inclusive community.
geographic_addresses: Chancellors Run Road & Buck Hewitt Road, Lexington Park, MD
Shangri-La Drive & Colony Square, Lexington Park, MD
Three Notch Road & Great Mills Road, Lexington Park, MD
Golden Beach Road & MD 5, Charlotte Hall, MD
North Shangri-La Drive & Three Notch Road, Lexington Park, MD

quotes.text: No new apartment complexes have been developed from 2019-2024. However, upgrades and improvements have been made to the existing complexes. Single Family homes and town home development has occurred across the SC footprint. Lack of incentives to build apartment complexes, met with a desire to see only single-family housing built, has encouraged developers to look elsewhere. High taxes, cost of building materials and land, and additional performance standards and expectations of the Planning Commission has slowed development as well.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning staff noted that while single-family homes and townhomes have expanded, 'no new apartment complexes have been developed from 2019-2024' due to a lack of development incentives, rising material costs, and a strong local preference for single-family housing.

quotes.text: The AICUZ reduces the potential of high-density development, especially due to height restrictions. The County regulations are more restrictive than DOD guidelines require. There is a high upfront cost for development, which creates a barrier to encourage Developers to build affordable housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights an opportunity for regulatory alignment, noting that 'the Air Installation Compatible Use Zone (AICUZ) reduces the potential of high-density development, especially due to height restrictions,' which are currently more restrictive than federal Department of Defense guidelines require.

quotes.text: The Comprehensive Plan directs mixed-use and medium-high-density development in the Lexington Park Development District. Policies discourage strip development and instead promote infill development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county's growth strategy promotes a shift in design, emphasizing that the 'Comprehensive Plan directs mixed-use and medium-high-density development in the Lexington Park Development District' to discourage strip commercial designs in favor of infill development.

quotes.text: The Comprehensive Plan lacks incentives for redevelopment and revitalization efforts... The Air Installation Compatible Use Zone (AICUZ) restricts development along key corridors in Lexington Park, such as the Downtown, Central Subarea, and Southern Subarea that have been identified in the Lexington Park Development District Master Plan. The Comprehensive Plan is unable to encourage higher density at the intersection of Three Notch Rd. and Great Mills Rd due to height restrictions in the AICUZ.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planning analysis shows that 'the Air Installation Compatible Use Zone (AICUZ) restricts development along key corridors in Lexington Park,' hindering the county's ability to encourage higher density at the intersection of Three Notch Road and Great Mills Road.

St. Mary’s Chapter of the NAACP
