quotes.text: A third of all County land has zoning that generally only allows detached housing leaving limited land available for medium to high density housing
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "a third of all County land has zoning that generally only allows detached housing," which severely restricts the availability of land for much-needed medium- to high-density residential options.

quotes.text: Too few rental communities that offer family-sized units of three- or more bedrooms.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county identifies a gap in multi-family development, stating there are "too few rental communities that offer family-sized units of three or more bedrooms," presenting an active opportunity for developer focus.

quotes.text: Sustained remote work has increased commercial vacancy rates
quotes.briefing_quote: The county highlights commercial real estate challenges, noting that "sustained remote work has increased commercial vacancy rates," pointing to opportunities for commercial repositioning or adaptive re-use.

quotes.text: Elizabeth Square, located in downtown Silver Spring, is a multi-generational, mixed-income, mixed-use project featuring residential coupled with a state-of-the-art recreation facility and other community amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights successful mixed-use models like Elizabeth Square, describing it as "a multi-generational, mixed-income, mixed-use project featuring residential coupled with a state-of-the-art recreation facility" and civic amenities.

quotes.text: Inadequate supply of affordable housing to address population’s needs and variety of income levels, specifically for elderly, very low-income levels, and people with disabilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: County planning documents address housing gaps, noting an "inadequate supply of affordable housing to address population's needs and variety of income levels," specifically for seniors and residents with disabilities.

quotes.text: Since the last application, we have identified several communities facing such dire, long-standing safety-related interior and exterior building hazards needing immediate repair/replacement, including Hermitage Woods in the Aspen Hill area... built in 1973 this multi-story, apartment-to-condo 37-unit complex units has such extensive structural damage that it is on the verge of being condemned
quotes.briefing_quote: The application emphasizes the urgent need for reinvestment in aging properties, noting several multi-family complexes face "dire, long-standing safety-related interior and exterior building hazards needing immediate repair or replacement."

quotes.text: Given that most new residential growth in the city will come in the form of multiple unit residential buildings, as apartments or condominiums, and that not all locations are appropriate for mixed-use development, Rockville needs a higher density residential zone.
quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate evolving multi-family housing demands, the plan notes that "most new residential growth in the city will come in the form of multiple unit residential buildings, as apartments or condominiums, and that not all locations are appropriate for mixed-use development, Rockville needs a higher density residential zone."

quotes.text: One way to accommodate more affordable housing options, flexible space for an office or shared family living arrangements, and financial assistance for current homeowners, while maintaining the city’s predominantly residential character, is with accessory apartments and accessory dwelling units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address affordability while maintaining neighborhood fabric, the plan highlights that "one way to accommodate more affordable housing options, flexible space for an office or shared family living arrangements, and financial assistance for current homeowners, while maintaining the city’s predominantly residential character, is with accessory apartments and accessory dwelling units."

quotes.text: Steady additions of commercial and amenity space on the ground floor of new buildings bring the opportunity for new shops and restaurants, supported by new residential units and offices on upper floors. This Plan promotes an intensification of development that encourages an active street scene and vibrant commercial district.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support local businesses and create active downtown corridors, the plan outlines that "steady additions of commercial and amenity space on the ground floor of new buildings bring the opportunity for new shops and restaurants, supported by new residential units and offices on upper floors."

quotes.text: These 'missing middle' housing types, also discussed in the Land Use Element, include: Duplexes; Triplexes; Fourplexes or quads; Sixplexes; Townhouses or rowhouses; Small apartment buildings; and Garden apartments. These housing types are largely missing in American suburbs, including Rockville, in part because land use policies and zoning do not allow their type of construction in single-unit detached residential zones...
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies the need for diversified housing forms, noting that "these 'missing middle' housing types... are largely missing in American suburbs, including Rockville, in part because land use policies and zoning do not allow their type of construction in single-unit detached residential zones."

quotes.text: The most successful office clusters in Montgomery County are part of mixed-use development with a strong sense of place and quality environment. Transit connectivity is increasingly important to office tenants.
quotes.briefing_quote: Citing a countywide office market assessment, the plan underscores that "the most successful office clusters in Montgomery County are part of mixed-use development with a strong sense of place and quality environment. plan_quotes.community_vision: Langley Park envisions transitioning into a vibrant, transit-oriented gateway that leverages the construction of the Purple Line light rail while preserving its naturally occurring affordable housing and rich cultural diversity. The community seeks to revitalize its commercial districts—especially the International Corridor—through denser, mixed-use development, streetscape beautification, and creative placemaking. Addressing persistent infrastructure and social challenges, the plan aims to improve pedestrian and bicycle safety, modernize aging multifamily rental housing, preserve environmental assets like the Northwest Branch Trail, and elevate the quality of life through enhanced health, language, and youth recreation services.

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

quotes.briefing_quote: The application details the unique growth constraints of the municipality, noting that "new development is almost impossible" because the town is entirely surrounded by a National Park, National Cemetery, and agricultural lands.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The vision for the Matthew Henson/Easterwood neighborhood is to transform it into a safe, quiet, and beautiful residential enclave with a variety of housing options and rich community amenities. By building upon existing assets like Easterwood Park and local schools, the plan aspires to rehabilitate vacant rowhouses, introduce affordable handicap-accessible bungalows, and establish mixed-use commercial and residential hubs along key corridors like West North Avenue and Monroe Street. The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Long Reach aspires to revitalize its Village Center, shifting from primary retail to a vibrant mix of arts, culture, community-driven services, and institutional uses. The community envisions achieving sustainable growth by advancing multi-modal 'complete streets' infrastructure, enhancing its neighborhood green spaces, and preserving its diverse housing stock while carefully balancing any new residential density with public facility constraints.

5320 Phelps Luck Drive, Columbia, MD

quotes.text: In 2018, the New Town Preliminary Development Plan (PDP) was increased by 315 units to allow for a mixed-use redevelopment project at the Long Reach Village Center. However, the redevelopment project was hindered by a complex zoning process and the need to acquire multiple properties under different ownership and was unable to overcome these barriers.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning analysis indicates that while the New Town Preliminary Development Plan was expanded by 315 units to enable mixed-use development at the Village Center, 'the redevelopment project was hindered by a complex zoning process and the need to acquire multiple properties under different ownership', highlighting a critical area where public-private coordination can streamline future efforts.

quotes.text: The Housing Commission has expressed interested in redeveloping the Columbia Landing apartment community. Due to existing debt on the property, the Commission would have to significantly increase density to be able to finance the redevelopment. With elementary schools in the area currently overcapacity, the project would likely not be able to proceed for up to 5 years due to the Adequate Public Facilities Ordinance requirements and would need a waiver to proceed.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Housing Commission expressed a strong desire to update local housing, but noted that 'due to existing debt on the property, the Commission would have to significantly increase density to be able to finance the redevelopment', which is currently paused due to local school capacity and Adequate Public Facilities Ordinance requirements.

quotes.text: The Housing Opportunities Master Plan recommends adding affordable units in all new and redevelopment communities, especially if the existing affordable units are not accessible, energy efficient or integrated into market rate communities. However, community feedback within the Long Reach community suggest that Long Reach already has a disproportion share of affordable housing, as compared to the rest of the County.
quotes.briefing_quote: While county plans recommend adding affordable units to all new developments, 'community feedback within the Long Reach community suggests that Long Reach already has a disproportionate share of affordable housing' compared to the rest of the county, indicating a need for a more balanced approach to market-rate and affordable integration.

quotes.text: The most recent subdivision constructed in Long Reach --Arnold’s Corner -- consisted of 18 single-family dwellings with an advertised starting price of $900,000. New Town Zoning, comprising most of Long Reach, does not require Moderately Priced Housing Units (MIHU’s) and they were not constructed as part of this development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan documents that the newest local subdivision, Arnold's Corner, 'consisted of 18 single-family dwellings with an advertised starting price of $900,000' and did not include moderately priced housing units because the underlying New Town zoning does not mandate them.

quotes.text: Market studies have identified opportunities for new/expanded uses in LRVC, including: a shift in use from primary retail to community and institutional uses; an arts theme to complement the Columbia Art Center, potentially to include artist work/sell/exhibit space, studio space, classrooms, and shared production space; and new housing
quotes.briefing_quote: Market evaluations indicate a strong opportunity to reposition commercial space, highlighting 'a shift in use from primary retail to community and institutional uses, an arts theme to complement the Columbia Art Center, and new housing'.

quotes.text: Any Village Center redevelopment plan that includes housing should address the need for additional affordable senior housing and affordable family housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup members and planning guidelines emphasize that 'any Village Center redevelopment plan that includes housing should address the need for additional affordable senior housing and affordable family housing' to promote a diverse, multi-generational neighborhood.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Cherry Hill envisions a holistic, equitable transformation that improves the quality of life, creates pathways out of poverty, and drives economic development without displacing current residents. By building on its rich legacy, new 21st Century schools, and a strong community fabric, Cherry Hill aims to attract high-quality mixed-income housing, cultivate Black-owned small businesses, introduce a community-owned cooperative grocery, and establish vibrant transit-oriented and mixed-use spaces.

quotes.text: All new rental housing should be mixed-income, meaning that it must be accessible to people making all ranges of income (from no income to unrestricted income). Each new development should be 1/3 low-income units, 1/3 workforce units, and 1/3 units for unrestricted income renters where economically feasible.
quotes.briefing_quote: To promote socioeconomic diversity and inclusivity, the plan stresses that 'all new rental housing should be mixed-income... each new development should be 1/3 low-income units, 1/3 workforce units, and 1/3 units for unrestricted income renters where economically feasible.'

quotes.text: Construct 80-100 units of high-quality, mixed-income rental housing in a 4-story building on the Patapsco School Site
quotes.briefing_quote: The steering committee highlighted an immediate infill residential opportunity to 'construct 80-100 units of high-quality, mixed-income rental housing in a 4-story building on the Patapsco School Site' next to the local school.

quotes.text: Many of the existing rowhouses in Cherry Hill are roughly 750—900 SF and have 2-3 bedrooms, with 1 full bathroom. Families today are looking for 3 and 4-bedrooms with at least 2 to 2.5 bathrooms;... Shorter lengths of rowhouses (duplexes, triplexes, and 4-unit buildings) would help to break up the streets and provide green between the buildings.
quotes.briefing_quote: To mitigate out-migration of families seeking larger spaces, the plan highlights a strong demand for developers to build 'larger houses with contemporary floor plans' featuring three to four bedrooms and multiple bathrooms.

quotes.text: Cherry Hill currently does not have the spending required to support a supermarket and would need to capture additional demand from surrounding areas... The best way to address residents' needs for groceries is to implement a phased approach.
quotes.briefing_quote: Acknowledging that the area's current spending power sits below national grocery chain thresholds, the plan recommends that developers 'attract a small, private grocery chain or family-owned franchise' as part of a phased food security approach.

quotes.text: In the future, a mixed-use Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) neighborhood may be possible next to the existing Cherry Hill Light RailLink station... The TOD would also be an ideal location for mixed-income rental housing, which combines financing sources to create housing for a range of incomes, from low-income to market rate.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning team identified a major opportunity to create a 'vibrant mixed-use Transit-Oriented Development neighborhood next to the existing Cherry Hill Light RailLink station' to integrate higher-density housing and local retail.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Reimagine Middle Branch Plan outlines a long-term, community-driven vision to transform 11 miles of neglected shoreline into a world-class system of public parks, trails, and ecological restorations. Centered on justice, equity, diversity, and resilience, the initiative seeks to reconnect historically disinvested South Baltimore neighborhoods to the water, generate local wealth, preserve cultural heritage, and protect critical infrastructure from the impacts of climate change.

S. Hanover Street & Reedbird Avenue, Baltimore, MD

quotes.text: The approved One Westport development plans include a combination of residential and commercial uses, alongside a public waterfront trail and park spaces.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community highlights the opportunity presented by the One Westport project, which "includes a combination of residential and commercial uses, alongside a public waterfront trail and park spaces" to bring vibrant, accessible mixed-use development to the shoreline.

quotes.text: The layout builds on recommendations of the 2020 Cherry Hill Transformation Plan and includes new equitable mixed-use development on vacant land between Hanover and Potee Streets and south of Potee. Echoing the Transformation Plan, a combination of mixed-income housing, healthcare, and a grocery store is recommended.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better serve neighborhood needs, planners recommend "new equitable mixed-use development on vacant land... [including] a combination of mixed-income housing, healthcare, and a grocery store" along the Hanover-Potee Corridor.

quotes.text: The buildings’ bulk and form are envisioned as low to mid-rise and mixed-use: at most three to four stories of residential over a base of commercial-retail or professional services.
quotes.briefing_quote: To maintain visual access to the waterfront, local guidelines suggest that "buildings’ bulk and form are envisioned as low to mid-rise and mixed-use: at most three to four stories of residential over a base of commercial-retail" or professional services.

quotes.text: The Plan recommends establishing a native plant nursery, managed and staffed by South Baltimore residents, to supply park improvement projects and Middle Branch communities with locally grown plants and locally made building materials.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes green economy opportunities by "establishing a native plant nursery, managed and staffed by South Baltimore residents, to supply park improvement projects... with locally grown plants and locally made building materials."

quotes.text: The Plan recommends establishing a storefront marketplace that will offer the opportunity to activate the waterfront by drawing local residents and visitors to purchase culturally authentic goods, art, and foods from an assortment of vendors.
quotes.briefing_quote: To incubate local businesses, the plan envisions "establishing a storefront marketplace that will offer the opportunity to activate the waterfront by drawing local residents and visitors to purchase culturally authentic goods, art, and foods" from a diverse assortment of vendors.

quotes.text: At the north lot, a visible and well-connected site near the base of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial Bridge, the Plan suggests two alternatives – a civic use, such as library or other community facility, or a low-scale commercial development to support the community and the hospital and bring more activity to the waterfront.
quotes.briefing_quote: For underutilized parking areas near MedStar Harbor Hospital, the plan suggests "a civic use, such as [a] library or other community facility, or a low-scale commercial development to support the community and the hospital" while driving active street life.

quotes.text: catalyzing investments in larger, mixed-use or multi-family housing developments with crucial pre-development or gap funding
quotes.briefing_quote: The South Baltimore Community Development Fund is designed to serve as a vital financial tool, "catalyzing investments in larger, mixed-use or multi-family housing developments with crucial pre-development or gap funding" to deliver quality housing options.

quotes.text: The 2020 Cherry Hill Transformation Plan identifies key sites for development in Cherry Hill, as well as locations for new housing, active corridors, and economic initiatives.
quotes.briefing_quote: Reconciling prior neighborhood initiatives, the planning team noted that "the 2020 Cherry Hill Transformation Plan identifies key sites for development in Cherry Hill, as well as locations for new housing, active corridors, and economic initiatives" to ensure coordinate growth.

community_organizations: Boys and Girls Club of Westport
Concerned Citizens for a Better Brooklyn

plan_quotes.community_vision: A Baltimore of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child has opportunities to thrive no matter what zip code they live in, and residents play an essential role in Baltimore’s thriving future. The community aspires to grow through equitable neighborhood development, sustainable transit-oriented design, economic empowerment of local small businesses, environmental and climate justice, and the active preservation of cultural heritage and neighborhood stability.

quotes.text: The Fitzgerald apartment building, located at 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue in Mid-Town Belvedere, is an example of a successful Transit Oriented Development project in Baltimore. Built in 2010, adjacent to the Mt. Royal/MICA Light Rail station, the seven-story building has 275 apartment units and two commercial establishments on the lower level
quotes.briefing_quote: A prime example of successful transit-oriented development is the Fitzgerald apartment building, which stands as a seven-story building with 275 apartment units and ground-floor commercial establishments adjacent to the Light Rail, showcasing how dense, mixed-use infill can thrive in Baltimore.

quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. These areas are relatively rich in the resources needed for quality of life and healthy child development, but as a result of a long practice of exclusion, they currently have limited affordable housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To affirmatively further fair housing, the plan emphasizes that in stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed-income developments to reverse long practices of exclusion.

quotes.text: Replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and the vacant former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, new elementary middle school, two new parks, and a renovated and expanded Chick Webb Recreation Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Perkins Somerset Oldtown Transformation Plan represents a massive revitalization effort, replacing obsolete housing with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, and essential community spaces.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. These are largely stable, highly livable, and resilient communities, but unfortunately, they have historically received little benefit from national and local housing policies that have often failed to support the middle class.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing policy experts highlighted the critical need to support middle neighborhoods, noting that these homes generate wealth over generations for families whose future security is tied to their communities' ongoing success.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore City's vision focuses on reversing population decline, eliminating structural racism, and building economic competitiveness. By integrating investments in housing, transit, arts, and green spaces, the city seeks to stabilize middle-market neighborhoods and transform historically disinvested areas into thriving, equitable communities with ample affordable housing and locally-owned commercial opportunities.
geographic_addresses: 417 E. Fayette Street, Baltimore, MD

Greenmount Avenue & East 20th Street, Baltimore, MD

quotes.text: Despite gains in income, the City continues to experience a shortage of affordable rental and homeownership units particularly for households earning 50% or less of the Area Median Income (AMI) as determined by the U.S. Department of Housing & Urban Development (HUD).
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Sustainable Communities report underscores that despite general income gains, Baltimore "continues to experience a shortage of affordable rental and homeownership units particularly for households earning 50% or less of the Area Median Income."

quotes.text: Each district’s Main Street program has a different strategy for spurring economic activity, but support may include marketing and event planning, financial assistance for design and promotions, architectural services for facade renovations, streetscape improvements, technical support, access to grants, and more to support the City’s eight (8) Main Street Districts.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize local business hubs, Main Street program strategies include offering "financial assistance for design and promotions, architectural services for facade renovations, and streetscape improvements" to draw in new commercial tenants.

quotes.text: Yard 56, a former industrial site redeveloped as a mixed-use development across from Hopkins Bayview.
quotes.briefing_quote: Opportunity Zone initiatives have catalyzed key transformations, such as "Yard 56, a former industrial site redeveloped as a mixed-use development across from Hopkins Bayview."

quotes.text: To provide safe and decent housing and help owners maintain their housing values, the City and Housing Authority dedicate considerable resources to increasing and preserving its supply of affordable housing for both homeowners and renters.
quotes.briefing_quote: Municipal planners indicated that the city aims to "dedicate considerable resources to increasing and preserving its supply of affordable housing for both homeowners and renters" to stabilize residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Vacant lots and buildings are consolidated to create new mixed-income rental and for-sale housing sites. Abandoned industrial sites are repurposed and frequently leverage additional investment.
quotes.briefing_quote: By optimizing municipal land assets, "vacant lots and buildings are consolidated to create new mixed-income rental and for-sale housing sites" that spark wider neighborhood investment.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community where residents enjoy a top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, and innovative businesses. The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.
geographic_addresses: Frederick Road & Triadelphia Road, Ellicott City, MD
Broken Land Parkway & Snowden River Parkway, Columbia, MD
Woodland Road & Route 108, Ellicott City, MD
Sanner Road & Johns Hopkins Road, Clarksville, MD
Snowden River Parkway & Oakland Mills Road, Columbia, MD

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Cherry Hill envisions a holistic, equitable transformation that improves the quality of life, creates pathways out of poverty, and drives economic development without displacing current residents. By building on its rich legacy, new 21st Century schools, and a strong community fabric, Cherry Hill aims to attract high-quality mixed-income housing, cultivate Black-owned small businesses, introduce a community-owned cooperative grocery, and establish vibrant transit-oriented and mixed-use spaces.

Cherry Hill Road & Seabury Road, Baltimore, MD

quotes.text: All new rental housing should be mixed-income, meaning that it must be accessible to people making all ranges of income (from no income to unrestricted income). Each new development should be 1/3 low-income units, 1/3 workforce units, and 1/3 units for unrestricted income renters where economically feasible.
quotes.briefing_quote: To promote socioeconomic diversity and inclusivity, the plan stresses that 'all new rental housing should be mixed-income... each new development should be 1/3 low-income units, 1/3 workforce units, and 1/3 units for unrestricted income renters where economically feasible.'

quotes.text: Construct 80-100 units of high-quality, mixed-income rental housing in a 4-story building on the Patapsco School Site
quotes.briefing_quote: The steering committee highlighted an immediate infill residential opportunity to 'construct 80-100 units of high-quality, mixed-income rental housing in a 4-story building on the Patapsco School Site' next to the local school.

quotes.text: Many of the existing rowhouses in Cherry Hill are roughly 750—900 SF and have 2-3 bedrooms, with 1 full bathroom. Families today are looking for 3 and 4-bedrooms with at least 2 to 2.5 bathrooms;... Shorter lengths of rowhouses (duplexes, triplexes, and 4-unit buildings) would help to break up the streets and provide green between the buildings.
quotes.briefing_quote: To mitigate out-migration of families seeking larger spaces, the plan highlights a strong demand for developers to build 'larger houses with contemporary floor plans' featuring three to four bedrooms and multiple bathrooms.

quotes.text: Cherry Hill currently does not have the spending required to support a supermarket and would need to capture additional demand from surrounding areas... The best way to address residents' needs for groceries is to implement a phased approach.
quotes.briefing_quote: Acknowledging that the area's current spending power sits below national grocery chain thresholds, the plan recommends that developers 'attract a small, private grocery chain or family-owned franchise' as part of a phased food security approach.

quotes.text: In the future, a mixed-use Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) neighborhood may be possible next to the existing Cherry Hill Light RailLink station... The TOD would also be an ideal location for mixed-income rental housing, which combines financing sources to create housing for a range of incomes, from low-income to market rate.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning team identified a major opportunity to create a 'vibrant mixed-use Transit-Oriented Development neighborhood next to the existing Cherry Hill Light RailLink station' to integrate higher-density housing and local retail.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.

quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. quotes.text: Replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and the vacant former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, new elementary middle school, two new parks, and a renovated and expanded Chick Webb Recreation Center.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD

Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. quotes.text: Town Residential (TR) areas provide for higher density, more compact development near incorporated towns, rural villages (such as Bittinger and Swanton), and other places such as McHenry, and Thayerville. Development densities in TR areas are up to eight multi-family dwelling units per acre and approximately four to five single-family dwelling units per acre in areas served by public water and sewer. TR areas can accommodate a mix of housing types, including single family detached, townhouses, and apartments.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better accommodate multi-family options near population centers, the plan designates Town Residential zones to provide for "higher density, more compact development... up to eight multi-family dwelling units per acre" in areas served by public utilities.

quotes.text: TC areas, unlike TR areas, are mixed use areas where a variety of retail, service, and commercial uses can be intermixed with residential uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planners highlight the potential of Town Center zones to create vibrant nodes, describing them as "mixed use areas where a variety of retail, service, and commercial uses can be intermixed with residential uses."

quotes.text: Recommendations were made to, among other things, minimize developable areas, maintain contiguous forests and agricultural lands to the maximum extent possible, cluster new development, preserve viewsheds...
quotes.briefing_quote: To balance low-density development with conservation, the plan recommends measures to "minimize developable areas, maintain contiguous forests and agricultural lands... [and] cluster new development" within rural and resource-sensitive areas.

quotes.text: Concentrated commercial development promotes the economic use of land including sharing facilities such as parking and storm water management.
quotes.briefing_quote: In contrast to linear highway sprawl, the county emphasizes that "concentrated commercial development promotes the economic use of land including sharing facilities" like parking and stormwater infrastructure.

quotes.text: There is a gap in market-rate housing, between fixer-uppers and $250,000 lake homes. It is difficult for first-time homebuyers to own, particularly young couples and young families.
quotes.briefing_quote: Superintendent Barbara Baker identified a critical entry-level housing gap, noting that there is "a gap in market-rate housing, between fixer-uppers and $250,000 lake homes" which prevents young local families from building equity.

quotes.text: According to the Council there is a need for single story 1-bedroom market-rate elderly independent people thus capturing aging retirees.
quotes.briefing_quote: During stakeholder consultations, the Mayor's Council noted that to support the aging population, "there is a need for single-story 1-bedroom market-rate" independent living options to capture and retain active retirees.

TR areas can accommodate a mix of housing types, including single family detached, townhouses, and apartments.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better accommodate multi-family options near population centers, the plan designates Town Residential zones to provide for "higher density, more compact development... up to eight multi-family dwelling units per acre" in areas served by public utilities.

quotes.text: TC areas, unlike TR areas, are mixed use areas where a variety of retail, service, and commercial uses can be intermixed with residential uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planners highlight the potential of Town Center zones to create vibrant nodes, describing them as "mixed use areas where a variety of retail, service, and commercial uses can be intermixed with residential uses."

quotes.text: Recommendations were made to, among other things, minimize developable areas, maintain contiguous forests and agricultural lands to the maximum extent possible, cluster new development, preserve viewsheds...
quotes.briefing_quote: To balance low-density development with conservation, the plan recommends measures to "minimize developable areas, maintain contiguous forests and agricultural lands... [and] cluster new development" within rural and resource-sensitive areas.

quotes.text: Concentrated commercial development promotes the economic use of land including sharing facilities such as parking and storm water management.
quotes.briefing_quote: In contrast to linear highway sprawl, the county emphasizes that "concentrated commercial development promotes the economic use of land including sharing facilities" like parking and stormwater infrastructure.

quotes.text: There is a gap in market-rate housing, between fixer-uppers and $250,000 lake homes. It is difficult for first-time homebuyers to own, particularly young couples and young families.
quotes.briefing_quote: Superintendent Barbara Baker identified a critical entry-level housing gap, noting that there is "a gap in market-rate housing, between fixer-uppers and $250,000 lake homes" which prevents young local families from building equity.

quotes.text: According to the Council there is a need for single story 1-bedroom market-rate elderly independent people thus capturing aging retirees.
quotes.briefing_quote: During stakeholder consultations, the Mayor's Council noted that to support the aging population, "there is a need for single-story 1-bedroom market-rate" independent living options to capture and retain active retirees.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The vision for Harborplace seeks to transform Baltimore’s waterfront into a world-class, inclusive, and resilient destination. By reconnecting the city grid to the water's edge, breaking up monolithic building blocks, and expanding public parklands, the master plan aims to establish a democratic ground plane. It aspires to blend active open spaces with diverse retail, commercial, and high-density residential uses that celebrate Baltimore's local history, entrepreneurship, and cultural identity.

quotes.text: Envision with me … a new Inner Harbor area, where the imagination of man can take advantage of a rare gift of nature to produce an enthralling panorama of office buildings, parks, high-rise apartments, and marinas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Former Baltimore Mayor Theodore Roosevelt McKeldin famously envisioned a future Inner Harbor defined by an "enthralling panorama of office buildings, parks, high-rise apartments, and marinas," highlighting a long-standing aspiration for dynamic, high-density waterfront development.

quotes.text: For the first time in a long time, I really see all the developers and agencies and everybody talking about making sure that these aren't just pockmark projects with wastelands in between — that we're really talking about how we think about connectivity between all these things... Think about an amazing corridor that allows you to eat and drink and live, all the way from President Street all the way down to the stadiums … really a state entertainment district.
quotes.briefing_quote: Developer David Bramble emphasizes the importance of regional connectivity, urging stakeholders to move past isolated developments and design "an amazing corridor that allows you to eat and drink and live... really a state entertainment district."

quotes.text: Enhance Safety By Adding Residential and Active Social Uses
quotes.briefing_quote: During the public engagement sessions, a key theme that emerged from residents was the critical need to "enhance safety by adding residential and active social uses" to make the Inner Harbor a vibrant, 24/7 neighborhood.

quotes.text: Two slender towers move together to frame The Park at Freedom's Port and West Shore Park to create the preeminent waterfront mixed-use destination in Baltimore.
quotes.briefing_quote: The master plan proposes the 303 Light Street development, which introduces "two slender towers [moving] together to frame The Park at Freedom's Port" to deliver between 750 and 900 new residential units and activate the waterfront.

quotes.text: Youth input was heavily focused on two major recommendations: First, many teens and young adults felt unsafe at Harborplace... Second, many felt that there wasn't anything designed for them or geared toward their entertainment... Additionally, many teens and young adults also want to see local, black-owned restaurants and vendors and improved cleanliness and safety.
quotes.briefing_quote: Youth workshop participants highlighted safety concerns and a lack of youth-centric activities, expressing a strong desire for "local, Black-owned restaurants and vendors and improved cleanliness and safety" at the redeveloped Harborplace.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community where residents enjoy a top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, and innovative businesses. The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.
geographic_addresses: Frederick Road & Triadelphia Road, Ellicott City, MD
Broken Land Parkway & Snowden River Parkway, Columbia, MD
Woodland Road & Route 108, Ellicott City, MD
Sanner Road & Johns Hopkins Road, Clarksville, MD
Snowden River Parkway & Oakland Mills Road, Columbia, MD

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The North Laurel-Savage community envisions a sustainable, walkable, and vibrant future centered on Route 1 and transit-oriented hubs like the Savage MARC station. By implementing Complete Streets policies, preserving Historic Savage's unique mill town legacy, expanding affordable and energy-efficient housing options, and fostering commercial and mixed-use redevelopment, the community aims to balance economic growth with environmental conservation along the Patuxent River corridors.
geographic_addresses: 9203 Laurens Way, Laurel, MD
9203 Clovis Place, Laurel, MD
9131 River Hill Road, Laurel, MD
10138 American Pharoah Lane, Laurel, MD
Guilford Road & Mission Road, Jessup, MD
Gorman Road & US Route 1, Laurel, MD

quotes.text: The Corridor Activity Center (CAC) and Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Zoning Districts, while intended to provide a mix of uses, have primarily yielded high-density residential development with limited nonresidential (retail) in some locations
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that while designated activity centers and transit districts are designed for a mix of uses, they "have primarily yielded high-density residential development with limited nonresidential" retail, creating an opportunity for future developers to deliver more balanced commercial and community spaces.

quotes.text: Allow the development of residential and hotels within the transit oriented development areas to support nonresidential uses, such as office, retail, and entertainment, and increased MARC ridership.
quotes.briefing_quote: To build vibrant station areas, local guidelines recommend that planners "allow the development of residential and hotels within the transit oriented development areas to support nonresidential uses" like office, retail, and entertainment.

quotes.text: Allow sufficient residential densities in North Laurel District—defined in HoCo By Design as an area that will build on the existing transit-oriented community with an entertainment focus that both serves the needs of existing and future residents and offers a destination for neighboring communities-- to make a wide range of uses economically viable, including convenience retail and other neighborhood-serving amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To stimulate local economic activity, the plan advocates to "allow sufficient residential densities in North Laurel District... to make a wide range of uses economically viable," including convenience retail and other neighborhood-serving amenities.

quotes.text: Persistent high vacancy rates for ground floor retail in recent mixed-use developments on Route 1
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies a clear need to address "persistent high vacancy rates for ground floor retail in recent mixed-use developments on Route 1" by introducing more flexible zoning and economic incentives.

quotes.text: Reduction in older, smaller, more affordable single family housing units through demolition and substantial renovations that results in an increased resale value

plan_quotes.community_vision: Somerset County envisions a steady, managed trajectory of slow economic and population growth through the year 2010. The community seeks to transition from its traditional, declining resource-based agriculture and fishing economy toward a diversified mix of services, light manufacturing, tourism, and aquaculture. This growth is directed away from valuable farmland and sensitive environments, concentrating instead within designated primary growth corridors and community nodes served by central water and sewer systems to maintain the county's rural character, preserve historical resources, and protect the Chesapeake Bay.

quotes.text: Somerset should begin to encourage townhouses, patio homes and other more affordable types in order to compete with surrounding communities to retain population and tax base. This would introduce a greater proportion of housing at densities of between 5 and 10 DU per acre, thereby conserving land, bringing people closer to village centers and permitting easier access to a concentration of community facilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To improve housing variety and retain younger residents, the 1996 Plan suggests that Somerset 'begin to encourage townhouses, patio homes and other more affordable types in order to compete with surrounding communities,' aiming to achieve housing densities of between 5 and 10 dwelling units per acre.

quotes.text: Higher residential densities in the form of density bonuses should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, where a high quality central water and sewer system is planned.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning narrative notes that 'higher residential densities in the form of density bonuses should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, where a high quality central water and sewer system is planned' to support sustainable infrastructure.

quotes.text: Strict controls should be placed on the subdivision of farms and the spread of strip residential uses along country roads by limiting development in the 'A' zone to minor subdivisions (no more than six lots).
quotes.briefing_quote: To combat unplanned sprawl on rural roadways, the plan outlines that 'strict controls should be placed on the subdivision of farms and the spread of strip residential uses along country roads by limiting development in the agricultural zone to minor subdivisions.'

quotes.text: Planned Unit Developments (PUDs) should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, with a range of community facilities consistent with the development's needs and the location, size and other criteria typically required by the County. In particular, communities with a broad mix of activities, including residential, commercial, employment and recreation should be preferred...
quotes.briefing_quote: Focusing on innovative layout designs, the plan asserts that 'Planned Unit Developments should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, with a range of community facilities consistent with the development's needs.'

quotes.text: Industrial and commercial development should be encouraged to cluster in office parks and employment centers within the Primary Growth Areas as indicated on the Land Use Plan Map (Map 4) They should be well landscaped, buffered from nearby residential areas and should take positive measures to protect sensitive environmental resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: To balance commercial expansion with environmental protection, the plan recommends that 'industrial and commercial development should be encouraged to cluster in office parks and employment centers within the Primary Growth Areas' to safeguard natural resources.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Cultivate investment and hope in the Oliver Neighborhood through creating visible connections between resilient green spaces, activated cultural assets, and vibrant community resources. Oliver aspires to transition from a historically rich but currently underinvested neighborhood characterized by high vacancy into a thriving, safe, and walkable community that balances historic single-family rowhouses with targeted multifamily and mixed-use density, particularly along the Harford Avenue and North Avenue corridors.
geographic_addresses: North Avenue & Broadway, Baltimore, MD
Biddle Street & Broadway, Baltimore, MD
Biddle Street & Ensor Street, Baltimore, MD
North Avenue & Ensor Street, Baltimore, MD
Harford Avenue & Oliver Street, Baltimore, MD
Central Avenue & Hoffman Street, Baltimore, MD

quotes.text: The Family Dollar store site at the corner of Oliver St. and Harford Ave. lies at a critical intersection at the historic heart of the neighborhood. Given this prominent location, we should reimagine the Family Dollar store site in the long-term as a multi-family development consistent with underlying zoning with community-serving retail and active ground floor frontages on the streets, with integrated podium parking underneath
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a prime redevelopment opportunity at the corner of Oliver Street and Harford Avenue, recommending that stakeholders "reimagine the Family Dollar store site in the long-term as a multi-family development consistent with underlying zoning with community-serving retail and active ground floor frontages" to anchor the heart of the community.

quotes.text: Harford Ave. between Federal and Biddle Street, (Mixed-use Residential/Multi-Family Housing/ Commercial) to feature a few mid-rise mixed-use multifamily buildings with ground-floor retail that can support a grocery store or smaller businesses such as coffee shops, apparel, bank, nail salons, etc. with a minimum of 85% of the units being market rate
quotes.briefing_quote: To support local economic viability and house new neighbors, the community visualizes Harford Avenue hosting "mid-rise mixed-use multifamily buildings with ground-floor retail that can support a grocery store or smaller businesses... with a minimum of 85% of the units being market rate."

quotes.text: All single family infill (new construction) should not exceed three stories and, while not yet officially designated as a CHAP district, should generally attempt to align to the design standards presented in the City's CHAP guidelines to best protect the historic character of Oliver.
quotes.briefing_quote: To preserve the aesthetic integrity of the area, the plan requests that "all single family infill (new construction) should not exceed three stories" and should design-align with the Commission for Historical and Architectural Preservation guidelines.

quotes.text: The high concentration of vacant land in this focus area holds Oliver’s best potential to attract multi-family development consistent with underlying zoning into the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the high vacancy along the western boundary, planners note that the area holds "Oliver's best potential to attract multi-family development consistent with underlying zoning into the community" as a mechanism for neighborhood growth.

quotes.text: Current zoning in Oliver makes it challenging for development to be concentrated and responsive to community needs and desires. To support continued investment and development for small businesses and renovations that strengthen the fabric of the community, zoning practices will need to be re-considered.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local development partner ReBUILD Metro pointed out that "current zoning in Oliver makes it challenging for development to be concentrated and responsive to community needs," indicating a vital opportunity for zoning realignment to foster neighborhood-serving storefronts.

quotes.text: I hope that Oliver is a thriving neighborhood. As a native Baltimorean that recently returned to invest in the city, I chose this neighborhood but sometimes have regrets. I love my property but the neighborhood feels stagnant. There doesn’t appear to be a plan, but spotty investment that feels disconnected. Given its location to a major hub like JHH and downtown the neighborhood has potential yet its unrealized.
quotes.briefing_quote: A returning native resident highlighted the gap between hope and reality, stating that while they love their property, "the neighborhood feels stagnant" with disconnected investments, emphasizing that its proximity to downtown and major employment hubs represents major "unrealized potential."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

quotes.text: Expanding the areas where multi-family and apartment development is allowed would increase the availability of development sites and reduce the cost of land per unit. The County and municipalities should review and increase allowable densities where appropriate.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address the housing shortage, the plan notes that "expanding the areas where multi-family and apartment development is allowed" would increase the availability of development sites and reduce land costs per unit.

quotes.text: By reducing the growth of new residential development in agricultural and rural areas... encouraging and directing growth to existing communities and within designated areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county's primary growth management strategy focuses on "reducing the growth of new residential development in agricultural and rural areas" by directing future growth into established communities.

quotes.text: In the Grasonville Village Center, low- and medium-intensity commercial uses are encouraged, along with single-family and multi-family housing. The existing village scale is maintained and enhanced so that this area once again becomes a true village center...
quotes.briefing_quote: For the Grasonville Village Center, the plan outlines an opportunity where "low- and medium-intensity commercial uses are encouraged, along with single-family and multi-family housing" to help reestablish a vibrant village scale.

quotes.text: It is the County's intent that remaining un-allocated sewer capacity should be reserved for commercial uses, directing any new residential development to the incorporated towns that have capacity to accommodate it. Infill development is development that takes place on vacant, undeveloped or underutilized parcels within an area that is already characterized by development...
quotes.briefing_quote: To address infrastructure constraints, the plan stresses the need to "reserve remaining sewer capacity for commercial uses, directing any new residential development to the incorporated towns" that have the capacity to accommodate it.

quotes.text: Many communities are making zoning provisions for 'Missing Middle' housing—housing types with unit sizes and densities between those of single-family and multi-family zones... They include small-lot single-family units, duplexes, triplexes, townhouses, cottage homes, and small multi-family buildings of four to eight units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To provide more diverse and affordable choices, the plan encourages zoning provisions for "'Missing Middle' housing—housing types with unit sizes and densities between those of single-family and multi-family zones".

quotes.text: The Centreville water service map also shows an area designated as W-3 at the intersection of US 301/MD 304. This is an area that has a mixture of commercial, industrial, and municipal uses. In addition, there are some parcels that are currently agricultural. It was suggested that the vacant areas be developed into a County-developed business park.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning framework identifies a strategic opportunity at the intersection of US 301 and MD 304 to develop vacant agricultural parcels into a County-developed business park, supporting a balanced mix of commercial, industrial, and municipal uses.

quotes.text: Both the Town and County Comprehensive Plans call for a mix of residential and commercial land uses on lands in and adjacent to the Town and within the Queenstown Growth Area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Comprehensive strategies for Queenstown emphasize the need to integrate a balanced mix of residential and commercial land uses within the designated growth area to foster vibrant local development.

quotes.text: TRUE commercial apartments – zoning may need to be refined such that the apartments would be ancillary to the commercial, not the other way around.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better manage infrastructure and sewer allocations, the technical committee recommended refining zoning guidelines to encourage true commercial apartments that function strictly as ancillary to commercial developments.

quotes.text: Prohibit any further large-scale residential development. Remove large vacant parcels from the Growth Area – rezone/downzone if required
quotes.briefing_quote: Wastewater capacity limitations have prompted calls to prohibit further large-scale residential developments and potentially rezone or downzone large vacant parcels out of active Growth Areas to protect local infrastructure.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."
