The city envisions sustainable growth centered around transit-oriented, high-quality mixed-use development, green infrastructure, and environmental sustainability, while actively preserving its historic architecture, tree canopy, and socio-economic diversity.

quotes.text: In 2010 the City of Mount Rainier purchased underutilized and abandoned properties and combined them into a parcel on 3200 Rhode Island Avenue and Eastern Avenue, the Washington DC borderline. In 2020 the City sold the property to the IFG Group. Their mixed-use development project consists of 97 condominiums, 11 street-level retail outlets and a 2 level underground parking garage.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a key redevelopment milestone at the Washington D.C. border where the City "purchased underutilized and abandoned properties and combined them into a parcel on 3200 Rhode Island Avenue and Eastern Avenue... [selling] the property to the IFG Group" for a mixed-use project consisting of 97 condominiums and 11 street-level retail outlets.

quotes.text: The Singer Building, a long vacant historic landmark on Rhode Island Ave at Perry Street has been completely renovated by The Menkiti Group and is open for business. The mixed-use development has 12 residential units (fully leased) and 3 new business establishments operating within 10,000 sq. ft. of retail space.
quotes.briefing_quote: Illustrating the success of local adaptive reuse, the plan notes that "The Singer Building, a long vacant historic landmark on Rhode Island Avenue at Perry Street has been completely renovated... [into a] mixed-use development with 12 residential units (fully leased) and 3 new business establishments."

quotes.text: The expansion of housing choice in the Mount Rainier Community is designed to be located in the MUTC where the city currently owns property. This is virtually the only existing area excluding a few lots in the city which are privately owned to building additional housing. The current policy is to create development of high quality without the need to access services by car. In addition, housing will be energy efficient and make use of environmentally sensitive design. Housing will increase from 100-200 units depending upon the configuration of the development according to several developers that the city has consulted with. Workforce housing will consist of approximately 8-10% of the total units.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing future growth, the plan states that the expansion of housing choice is targeted for the Mixed-Use Town Center, noting that "housing will increase from 100-200 units depending upon the configuration of the development" with workforce housing comprising about 8 to 10 percent of the units.

quotes.text: Many vacant commercial properties are privately owned and often these owners are primarily interested in leasing the properties for way above market value rate in anticipation of the speculative influx of Washington DC residents moving into the city based upon our rising housing prices and potential economic boom.
quotes.briefing_quote: Economic development officials noted a significant barrier to commercial retail growth, explaining that "many vacant commercial properties are privately owned and often these owners are primarily interested in leasing the properties for way above market value rate in anticipation of the speculative influx of Washington DC residents."

quotes.text: Vacant and underutilized sites on Rhode Island Avenue give the appearance of a deteriorating commercial environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize the downtown corridor, the plan emphasizes the need to address aesthetic and vacancy challenges, observing that "vacant and underutilized sites on Rhode Island Avenue give the appearance of a deteriorating commercial environment."

quotes.text: Mount Rainier is considered one of the last affordable housing areas in Prince George's County with homes averaging between $200k and $300k. Since property values had previously remained affordable, many homes have not suffered the 'mansionization' trend of 'flippers' doing poor quality renovations and expansions.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting the preservation of neighborhood character, the document notes that Mount Rainier remains "one of the last affordable housing areas in Prince George's County," which has protected many historic homes from the "mansionization" trend of lower-quality flipped expansions.

community_organizations: Mixed Use Town Center Design Review Committee

By focusing development almost exclusively within transit-oriented development zones and commercial corridors near Metro stations, the city aims to foster economic vibrancy and mixed-use density while proactively executing comprehensive strategies to preserve and expand affordable housing so that residents can remain in the community at all stages of life.

quotes.text: Affordability for low-income and moderately low-income has become more challenging as demand for housing in the DC metropolitan area has outpaced the number of building permits approved by local jurisdictions

quotes.text: Private sector investment in land-development, primarily for mixed-use transit-oriented development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planning reviews point to strong 'private sector investment in land-development, primarily for mixed-use transit-oriented development,' demonstrating market momentum surrounding the city's Metro corridors.

By merging adjacent neighborhoods like Carole Highland, Lewisdale, and Adelphi into a single Sustainable Community entity, local leaders aim to revitalize aging single-use commercial retail centers into vibrant mixed-use places, upgrade housing conditions while preserving established single-family residential character, expand multi-modal pedestrian and bicycle connectivity, and implement robust green infrastructure to manage rising stormwater flooding concerns.

quotes.text: WMATA is planning to offer its property at the West Hyattsville Metro Station for redevelopment into a transit-oriented development (TOD). quotes.text: The SC area continues to lack national brand retailers and is limited in several key categories such as sit-down/casual dining, and other lifestyle retailers.

quotes.text: Demographic shifts have created a shortage of affordable housing and caused the conversion of owner-occupied units to overcrowd rentals. Multifamily housing stock is aging, most complexes approaching 50 years.

quotes.text: Notwithstanding the completion of 71 new Townhouses at 'Avondale Ridge', on MD 500 (Queens Chapel Road) in the Avondale Ridge Neighborhood in 2018, the total number housing units in the SC area decreased from 11,487 in 2015 to 10,924 in 2020

quotes.text: Development has been stalled in this area due to an outdated plan that did not truly promote transit-oriented development. A new Transit District Development Plan was adopted by Prince George’s County in 2015 and prospects have improved. A WMATA joint development project was approved for 400 apartment units and 10,000 SF of retail and County owned property across from the Metro station is being sold for mixed-use development.
quotes.briefing_quote: While past development near the Metro station was hindered by outdated zoning, the adoption of a new Transit District Development Plan has unlocked major opportunities, including an approved project featuring "400 apartment units and 10,000 square feet of retail" alongside county-owned property slated for transit-oriented mixed-use development.

quotes.text: The City has approved 10 new multifamily/townhouse projects since 2017 amounting to an increase of 2,626 dwelling units. About a dozen single-family home infill development has occurred. ... Most new development in College Park is redevelopment of commercial corridors and centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: Indicating a strong market preference for higher-density redevelopment in commercial areas, the plan notes that "the City has approved 10 new multifamily/townhouse projects since 2017" representing an addition of 2,626 dwelling units.

quotes.text: Strengthen College Park neighborhoods by reducing the number of single-family homes that are converted to group rental properties by continuing to offer homeownership grant programs, establishing a community land trust, and exploring new programs for housing rehabilitation with Habitat for Humanity Maryland.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community aims to stabilize residential areas, seeking to "strengthen College Park neighborhoods by reducing the number of single-family homes that are converted to group rental properties" through the creation of a community land trust and targeted homeownership programs.

quotes.text: Use recently acquired property on Calvert Road for the development of missing middle housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To promote housing type diversity, community planning goals advise the city to "use recently acquired property on Calvert Road for the development of missing middle housing" as a bridge between low- and high-density neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many long-term businesses have closed or have been relocated due to new development. ARPA assistance was provided to many businesses and has helped, but high rents are making it difficult for local, independent businesses to survive and for other to enter the market.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting a clear opportunity for developers to build affordable storefront spaces, the plan notes that "high rents are making it difficult for local, independent businesses to survive and for others to enter the market" amid ongoing corridor redevelopment.

quotes.text: Route 1 has seen tremendous redevelopment activity since being rezoned from C-S-C (Commercial Shopping Center) to M-U-I (Mixed-Use Infill) in 2001 and is successfully transforming from a strip commercial corridor to a mixed-use boulevard with a series of walkable nodes
quotes.briefing_quote: Due to progressive zoning changes, the US Route 1 corridor is "successfully transforming from a strip commercial corridor to a mixed-use boulevard with a series of walkable nodes" that enhance local economic vibrancy.

community_organizations: College Park Neighborhood Quality of Life Committee
College Park Committee for a Better Environment

Under this vision, future development will increasingly focus on mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects on previously developed sites, guiding new investment and redevelopment to older commercial corridors while preserving the unique character of existing low-density neighborhoods, waterfront communities, and agricultural lands.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."

community_organizations: Community Foundation of Anne Arundel County
Anne Arundel County Trust for Preservation, Inc.
Arts Council of Anne Arundel County Foundation

quotes.text: Like many areas of the county, the SC Area could benefit from a greater variety of housing options. Much of the housing in the SC Area are single-family detached units. A variety of middle density housing would provide additional affordability and choices to match needs.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that the community 'could benefit from a greater variety of housing options,' and that 'a variety of middle density housing would provide additional affordability and choices to match needs.'

quotes.text: Promote and incentivize mixed-use infill development in shopping centers taking advantage of the under-utilized parking lots.
quotes.briefing_quote: To enhance neighborhood vibrancy, the plan recommends to 'promote and incentivize mixed-use infill development in shopping centers taking advantage of under-utilized parking lots.'

quotes.text: A multifamily, medium-density residential development under construction within one-mile radius of Landover Metro Station
quotes.briefing_quote: The report highlights market activity nearby, pointing to a 'multifamily, medium-density residential development under construction within a one-mile radius of Landover Metro Station.'

quotes.text: A mix of housing types exist within the SC Area, including medium density detached homes and duplexes and high-density single-family dwellings such as triplexes and townhomes. Some multi-family apartment complexes are also located in the SC Area.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county's housing assessment notes that 'a mix of housing types exist within the Sustainable Community Area, including medium-density detached homes, duplexes, and high-density single-family dwellings such as triplexes and townhomes.'

quotes.text: Compatible zoning provides the opportunity for the redevelopment of older commercial areas and residential communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planners observed that 'compatible zoning provides the opportunity for the redevelopment of older commercial areas and residential communities' near primary transit assets.

The Town aspires to expand its walking paths, establish vibrant, pedestrian-oriented commercial spaces and dining options, and incorporate diverse housing alternatives like senior living, condominiums, and townhomes through major new developments like Hospital Hill.

quotes.text: The encouragement for new construction and commercial tenancies that provide gathering locations for families and new sit-down dining/meeting spaces primarily comes from the Hospital Hill development but can also be achieved through annexation of Cheverly West.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 renewal application highlighted that the encouragement for new construction and commercial tenancies 'primarily comes from the Hospital Hill development but can also be achieved through annexation of Cheverly West' to establish missing family dining and gathering spaces.

quotes.text: The annexation of Hospital Hill would incorporate assisted living, condos, townhomes, and retirement living opportunities.
quotes.briefing_quote: In planning for inclusive growth, the Town noted that 'the annexation of Hospital Hill would incorporate assisted living, condos, townhomes, and retirement living opportunities.'

quotes.text: Lacking in walkable, pedestrian-oriented commercial experiences... No new opportunities for shopping, dining and community gathering locations due, in part, to lack of commercial spaces that can accommodate new businesses
quotes.briefing_quote: The town recognizes a distinct economic gap, noting that the area is 'lacking in walkable, pedestrian-oriented commercial experiences' with a shortage of available spaces to house new retail or dining options.

quotes.text: There is a lack of buildable land as Cheverly is densely populated with single family homes and areas where there could be potential to build are often preserved for greenspace.
quotes.briefing_quote: In evaluating future development constraints, the application explained that 'Cheverly is densely populated with single family homes' and available unbuilt parcels are prioritized for green space preservation.

quotes.text: The Town of Cheverly did pass an emergency ordinance that created an Emergency Financial Assistance Program. $50,000 was set aside for homeowners and apartment dwellers to receive assistance for late mortgage or rent.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support local housing stability, the Town highlighted that they 'passed an emergency ordinance that created an Emergency Financial Assistance Program,' dedicating $50,000 to assist both homeowners and apartment tenants.

quotes.text: The Town's acreage is 80% residential, 10% commercial and 10% open space.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting the existing land use profile, the application noted that the town's 'acreage is 80% residential, 10% commercial and 10% open space.'

The community aims to sustainably manage its ecological footprint, protect its extensive forest preserves, and revitalize underutilized commercial corridors, while actively advocating for affordable housing and multi-family residential opportunities to create a more walkable, equitable, and vibrant future.

quotes.text: Due to a number of challenges, the City has been unable to increase its inventory of affordable housing since its designation as a Sustainable Community. Prince George’s County lacks incentive programs or affordable housing requirements tied to development like other surrounding counties, and this makes it more difficult to attract developers to Greenbelt to construct an affordable housing product even though the demand for affordable housing remains.
quotes.briefing_quote: City planners highlighted that although "the demand for affordable housing remains," the lack of county-level incentive programs "makes it more difficult to attract developers to Greenbelt to construct an affordable housing product," presenting an open opportunity for collaborative public-private partnerships.

quotes.text: Promote infill development and other redevelopment options for underutilized residential or commercial lots.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Sustainable Communities Action Plan outlines a strategy to "promote infill development and other redevelopment options for underutilized residential or commercial lots," creating clear pathways for adaptive reuse and compact development.

quotes.text: Opportunities for new multi-family residential development
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's housing assessment identifies "opportunities for new multi-family residential development" as a key strength to accommodate growing housing demands near major transit assets.

quotes.text: Oversee the conveyance of indoor recreation space to the City as part of the redevelopment plans of Beltway Plaza.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's active planning goals include a strategy to "oversee the conveyance of indoor recreation space to the City as part of the redevelopment plans" of the Beltway Plaza site, fostering integrated mixed-use environments.

The partner towns aim to leverage their extensive trail networks and historical assets, such as the Anacostia River waterfront, while addressing issues of flooding and pedestrian safety. By fostering an inclusive environment for their diverse, multi-generational populations, the Port Towns aspire to build a thriving local economy through small business support, selective mixed-use redevelopment, and workforce training programs like a localized trade school.

The city envisions sustainable growth centered around transit-oriented, high-quality mixed-use development, green infrastructure, and environmental sustainability, while actively preserving its historic architecture, tree canopy, and socio-economic diversity.

quotes.text: In 2010 the City of Mount Rainier purchased underutilized and abandoned properties and combined them into a parcel on 3200 Rhode Island Avenue and Eastern Avenue, the Washington DC borderline. In 2020 the City sold the property to the IFG Group. Their mixed-use development project consists of 97 condominiums, 11 street-level retail outlets and a 2 level underground parking garage.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a key redevelopment milestone at the Washington D.C. border where the City "purchased underutilized and abandoned properties and combined them into a parcel on 3200 Rhode Island Avenue and Eastern Avenue... [selling] the property to the IFG Group" for a mixed-use project consisting of 97 condominiums and 11 street-level retail outlets.

quotes.text: The Singer Building, a long vacant historic landmark on Rhode Island Ave at Perry Street has been completely renovated by The Menkiti Group and is open for business. The mixed-use development has 12 residential units (fully leased) and 3 new business establishments operating within 10,000 sq. ft. of retail space.
quotes.briefing_quote: Illustrating the success of local adaptive reuse, the plan notes that "The Singer Building, a long vacant historic landmark on Rhode Island Avenue at Perry Street has been completely renovated... [into a] mixed-use development with 12 residential units (fully leased) and 3 new business establishments."

quotes.text: The expansion of housing choice in the Mount Rainier Community is designed to be located in the MUTC where the city currently owns property. This is virtually the only existing area excluding a few lots in the city which are privately owned to building additional housing. The current policy is to create development of high quality without the need to access services by car. In addition, housing will be energy efficient and make use of environmentally sensitive design. Housing will increase from 100-200 units depending upon the configuration of the development according to several developers that the city has consulted with. Workforce housing will consist of approximately 8-10% of the total units.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing future growth, the plan states that the expansion of housing choice is targeted for the Mixed-Use Town Center, noting that "housing will increase from 100-200 units depending upon the configuration of the development" with workforce housing comprising about 8 to 10 percent of the units.

quotes.text: Many vacant commercial properties are privately owned and often these owners are primarily interested in leasing the properties for way above market value rate in anticipation of the speculative influx of Washington DC residents moving into the city based upon our rising housing prices and potential economic boom.
quotes.briefing_quote: Economic development officials noted a significant barrier to commercial retail growth, explaining that "many vacant commercial properties are privately owned and often these owners are primarily interested in leasing the properties for way above market value rate in anticipation of the speculative influx of Washington DC residents."

quotes.text: Vacant and underutilized sites on Rhode Island Avenue give the appearance of a deteriorating commercial environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize the downtown corridor, the plan emphasizes the need to address aesthetic and vacancy challenges, observing that "vacant and underutilized sites on Rhode Island Avenue give the appearance of a deteriorating commercial environment."

quotes.text: Mount Rainier is considered one of the last affordable housing areas in Prince George's County with homes averaging between $200k and $300k. Since property values had previously remained affordable, many homes have not suffered the 'mansionization' trend of 'flippers' doing poor quality renovations and expansions.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting the preservation of neighborhood character, the document notes that Mount Rainier remains "one of the last affordable housing areas in Prince George's County," which has protected many historic homes from the "mansionization" trend of lower-quality flipped expansions.

community_organizations: Mixed Use Town Center Design Review Committee

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Brentwood aspires to become a highly livable, environmentally resilient, and inclusive municipality. By leveraging its designation in the Gateway Arts District, the town aims to stimulate green and creative economic development, particularly through the rehabilitation of commercial facades along US Route 1 and the adaptive reuse of industrial buildings for artist spaces. Simultaneously, Brentwood is pursuing key infrastructure improvements, including a $2.5 million New Town Center project, extensive stormwater management to combat local flooding, pedestrian and bicycle accessibility via Vision Zero initiatives, and programs dedicated to housing affordability, racial equity, and enabling seniors to age in place.
geographic_addresses: 4408 40th St, Brentwood, MD

quotes.text: The Town will relocate the Administrative Support staff and municipal leadership to the old Brentwood Fire Station. A long-term capital campaign, over the past five years, the Town has successfully moved the project forward significantly. A $2.5 million project, architectural and engineering plans have been delivered, construction has continued and overcome significant challenges, cable engineering and landscaping plans have advanced, and residents are able to tour the construction bi-weekly.
quotes.briefing_quote: To centralize municipal services and improve energy efficiency, the Town is moving forward with a $2.5 million "New Town Center project to relocate administrative staff to the historic old Brentwood Fire Station," establishing a centralized hub for community engagement.

quotes.text: Develop and implement a commercial façade program for commercial corridors along Route US 1. Investigate ways to market and leverage the Arts District Designation.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize local business corridors, town strategies emphasize the plan to "develop and implement a commercial façade program for commercial corridors along Route US 1," while actively leveraging the local Arts District designation.

quotes.text: Support local businesses converting existing industrial buildings into artist space. Support interested art-based businesses to facilitate ownership within Town limits.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the unique local economy, town goals aim to "support local businesses converting existing industrial buildings into artist space" and facilitate art-based business ownership within town limits.

quotes.text: Continue outreach efforts to inform residents of programs to help low-income and senior residents to upkeep their property. Provide homeowners, renters, business owners with information on how to plant for and mitigate flooding, stormwater, excess heat, air pollution, and energy efficiency.
quotes.briefing_quote: To ensure residential resilience and support low-income families, the town will "continue outreach efforts to inform residents of programs to help low-income and senior residents to upkeep their property" and adapt to climate challenges.

quotes.text: Advocate for Senior Housing Options and provide funding for current residents to repair, upgrade, and maintain their homes.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the demographic shifts and needs of the aging population, the plan highlights the priority to "advocate for Senior Housing Options and provide funding for current residents to repair, upgrade, and maintain their homes."

quotes.text: Renovation of the current Town Hall into a Police Station and Community Center. Seek grants to assist with the renovations of the Police Station and Community Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: To optimize existing real estate, the municipal strategy targets the "renovation of the current Town Hall into a Police Station and Community Center," seeking state and federal grants to realize this essential community facility.

plan_quotes.community_vision: North Brentwood envisions a vibrant, culturally rich, and resilient future that celebrates its history as the first incorporated African American municipality in Prince George's County. Through the revitalization of the Route 1 corridor and the activation of historic community spaces like Sis's Tavern, the town aims to foster economic growth, support artist and minority-owned businesses, and implement critical green infrastructure to combat chronic flooding. Additionally, the community is focused on preserving its historic character and providing affordable senior housing options to prevent displacement from gentrification.

quotes.briefing_quote: County records show active redevelopment efforts, such as acquiring a vacant laundry facility for "redevelopment and conversion... to a retail, food, and beverage center" alongside new townhome projects.

quotes.text: Continue to work with RDA, RA, and Prince George’s County DHCD to identify key properties within ½ mile of the Metro stations for transit-oriented development housing development/redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup strategies emphasize the value of partnering with regional authorities to "identify key properties within half a mile of the Metro stations for transit-oriented housing development."

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Laurel envisions a sustainable, vibrant, and walkable community that balances economic growth with environmental stewardship. By targeting revitalization within its historical core, expanding green infrastructure, and implementing forward-thinking sustainability initiatives like curbside composting and widespread EV charging, the City seeks to grow responsibly. Laurel aims to deliver a diverse and affordable housing stock, enhance multimodal transit connections (such as transit-oriented development near the MARC station), and foster inclusive public spaces that support a high quality of life for multi-generational residents.

quotes.text: LAUREL MARC - TRANSIT ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT. Located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space. The building is planned in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Transportation.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a premier transit-oriented opportunity at the Laurel MARC station, noting that 'located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space' coordinated alongside state transit partners.

quotes.text: ANDERSON’S CORNER. A mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex known as Avalon Bay (constructed), an approved 55-unit townhouse community entitled Avery Place and a Royal Farms gas station and convenience store.
quotes.briefing_quote: Anderson's Corner serves as a successful template for mixed-density development, showcasing 'a mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex, an approved 55-unit townhouse community... and a Royal Farms' convenience center.

quotes.text: WEST SIDE. A mixed-use community consisting of a 469-unit apartment complex known as Modera at Westside (constructed) and 56-unit townhouse community, which is complete. The site also has other undeveloped parcels for commercial, a hotel and a second phase townhouse development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The West Side master-planned area illustrates the demand for integrated density, featuring 'a 469-unit apartment complex... and a 56-unit townhouse community' alongside undeveloped parcels reserved for commercial space and a hotel.

quotes.text: PATUXENT GREENS GOLF COURSE. The golf course closed in December 2018. The property was approved to be re-developed into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units. The development will also include a clubhouse, swimming pool, hiker/biker trails and other community amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: Following the transition of local recreational lands, the City approved plans for Patuxent Greens 'to be redeveloped into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units' paired with extensive walkable amenities.

quotes.text: Per the City of Laurel Unified Development Code, any multifamily development of 100 dwelling units or more approved after November 23, 2020, shall include a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as work force housing units, a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as moderately priced housing units and a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as age-restricted housing units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To ensure equitable growth, the City's Unified Development Code mandates that large-scale multifamily projects deliver 'a minimum of four percent workforce housing, four percent moderately priced housing, and four percent age-restricted housing.'

quotes.text: The redevelopment of the Main Street area and the retention of commercial uses is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability and attract shoppers.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan underscores that proactive commercial retention 'is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability.'

quotes.text: Encourage a substantial portion of future housing stock to be single-family detached homes, including high-quality custom-built homes. Strategy B: Preserve and restore single-family residences within the Historic Districts.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing strategies focus on preservation and diversity, seeking to 'encourage a substantial portion of future housing stock to be single-family detached homes, including high-quality custom-built homes' while safeguarding historic structures.

quotes.text: Compact, mixed-use, walkable design consistent with existing community character and located near available or planned transit options is encouraged to ensure efficient use of land and transportation resources and preservation and enhancement of natural system, open spaces, recreational area, and historical, cultural, and archeological resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City strongly favors sustainable design frameworks, stating that 'compact, mixed-use, walkable design consistent with existing community character and located near available or planned transit options is encouraged' to optimize resources.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The North Laurel-Savage community envisions a sustainable, walkable, and vibrant future centered on Route 1 and transit-oriented hubs like the Savage MARC station. By implementing Complete Streets policies, preserving Historic Savage's unique mill town legacy, expanding affordable and energy-efficient housing options, and fostering commercial and mixed-use redevelopment, the community aims to balance economic growth with environmental conservation along the Patuxent River corridors.

quotes.text: The Corridor Activity Center (CAC) and Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Zoning Districts, while intended to provide a mix of uses, have primarily yielded high-density residential development with limited nonresidential (retail) in some locations
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that while designated activity centers and transit districts are designed for a mix of uses, they "have primarily yielded high-density residential development with limited nonresidential" retail, creating an opportunity for future developers to deliver more balanced commercial and community spaces.

quotes.text: Allow the development of residential and hotels within the transit oriented development areas to support nonresidential uses, such as office, retail, and entertainment, and increased MARC ridership.
quotes.briefing_quote: To build vibrant station areas, local guidelines recommend that planners "allow the development of residential and hotels within the transit oriented development areas to support nonresidential uses" like office, retail, and entertainment.

quotes.text: Allow sufficient residential densities in North Laurel District—defined in HoCo By Design as an area that will build on the existing transit-oriented community with an entertainment focus that both serves the needs of existing and future residents and offers a destination for neighboring communities-- to make a wide range of uses economically viable, including convenience retail and other neighborhood-serving amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To stimulate local economic activity, the plan advocates to "allow sufficient residential densities in North Laurel District... to make a wide range of uses economically viable," including convenience retail and other neighborhood-serving amenities.

quotes.text: Persistent high vacancy rates for ground floor retail in recent mixed-use developments on Route 1
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies a clear need to address "persistent high vacancy rates for ground floor retail in recent mixed-use developments on Route 1" by introducing more flexible zoning and economic incentives.

quotes.text: Reduction in older, smaller, more affordable single family housing units through demolition and substantial renovations that results in an increased resale value
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing analysis highlights a challenge in entry-level homeownership due to a "reduction in older, smaller, more affordable single family housing units through demolition and substantial renovations" that drive up area housing prices.

quotes.text: Aging multi-family housing stock is in need of redevelopment or upgrades. The SC area has 9% of units that were built before 1970 and 73% of units that were built before 2000 according to Howard County’s Housing Opportunities Master Plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: Data indicates that the local "aging multi-family housing stock is in need of redevelopment or upgrades," with 73 percent of multi-family units in the Sustainable Community Area originally constructed before the year 2000.

quotes.text: As this SC Area’s transit amenities grow, it will be essential for residents, community leaders, municipalities, and agency partners to utilize program funding opportunities to preserve and protect existing stable residential neighborhoods.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Historically characterized as a suburban bedroom community with a majority of residents commuting to surrounding metropolitan areas for work, Bowie is actively steering its trajectory toward sustainable, high-quality development. The city's goals center around expanding local employment options in professional, scientific, and health fields, and building vibrant mixed-use town centers and walkable retail districts. Bowie remains highly committed to environmental stewardship, tracking a major drop in greenhouse gas emissions through green municipal infrastructure, transitioning to renewable energy, and pursuing aggressive trail connectivity to integrate its diverse residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: A recent example was in 2019 with approval of the South Lake development. The 381-acre mixed-use property was annexed by the City in 2019 and will include 555,000 sq. ft. to 620,000 sq. ft. of retail/office uses, three hotels with a total of 375 to 400 rooms/keys and 1360 dwelling units including 325 multifamily apartment units, 128 two-family attached condominium units, 563 townhouse units and 344 single family detached units.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2022 Bowie Sustainable Communities application highlights the massive **South Lake development, a 381-acre mixed-use property** that will bring "555,000 sq. ft. to 620,000 sq. ft. of retail/office uses, three hotels... and 1,360 dwelling units" including multifamily, townhomes, and single-family detached homes to the area.

quotes.text: Melford Village, however, is all much newer, and will include about 25,000 square feet of retail space known as Retail Village West, a 388-unit multi-family housing building known as The Aspen, about 58,000 square feet of retail area known as Retail Village East, another 435 multifamily units along with a clubhouse building known as the Melford Mansions, 249 townhouse units (Melford Townhomes), Tribute Assisted Living, and the Berkleigh with an additional 472 multi-family units.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning documentation showcases the growth of Melford Village, a modern mixed-use node slated to feature retail space, **"multifamily units along with a clubhouse building... 249 townhouse units... and the Berkleigh with an additional 472 multi-family units"** to expand the community's diverse housing and retail options.

quotes.text: Expanding the City's employment base is a core goal of this proposed strategy, and the City may have the potential to attract more professional, scientific, and technical services sector jobs in the County's strong Federal contractor sector, as well as serve as a regional center for health care and social assistance employment, by supporting more traditional office space development.
quotes.briefing_quote: A study for the Economic Development Strategy and Action Plan noted that the City has strong potential to expand its employment base and **"attract more professional, scientific, and technical services sector jobs... by supporting more traditional office space development."**

quotes.text: Outcome 2: Revitalize Old Town Bowie and create new areas for residents to spend time, commune, shop, dine. ... Economic Development and Planning will continue to work on a revitalization plan for the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city is focusing efforts to **"revitalize Old Town Bowie and create new areas for residents to spend time, commune, shop, [and] dine"** through a coordinated economic and physical development plan.

quotes.text: Many homes are older/original Levitt homes from the 1960s and are not energy efficient, causing energy costs to soar for some
quotes.briefing_quote: City staff identified an opportunity to support single-family homeowners, pointing out that **"many homes are older/original Levitt homes from the 1960s and are not energy efficient, causing energy costs to soar"**, signaling a clear need for energy-focused residential rehabilitation.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Laurel envisions a sustainable, vibrant, and walkable community that balances economic growth with environmental stewardship. By targeting revitalization within its historical core, expanding green infrastructure, and implementing forward-thinking sustainability initiatives like curbside composting and widespread EV charging, the City seeks to grow responsibly. Laurel aims to deliver a diverse and affordable housing stock, enhance multimodal transit connections (such as transit-oriented development near the MARC station), and foster inclusive public spaces that support a high quality of life for multi-generational residents.

quotes.text: LAUREL MARC - TRANSIT ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT. Located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space. The building is planned in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Transportation.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a premier transit-oriented opportunity at the Laurel MARC station, noting that 'located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space' coordinated alongside state transit partners.

quotes.text: ANDERSON’S CORNER. A mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex known as Avalon Bay (constructed), an approved 55-unit townhouse community entitled Avery Place and a Royal Farms gas station and convenience store.
quotes.briefing_quote: Anderson's Corner serves as a successful template for mixed-density development, showcasing 'a mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex, an approved 55-unit townhouse community... and a Royal Farms' convenience center.

quotes.text: WEST SIDE. A mixed-use community consisting of a 469-unit apartment complex known as Modera at Westside (constructed) and 56-unit townhouse community, which is complete. The site also has other undeveloped parcels for commercial, a hotel and a second phase townhouse development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The West Side master-planned area illustrates the demand for integrated density, featuring 'a 469-unit apartment complex... and a 56-unit townhouse community' alongside undeveloped parcels reserved for commercial space and a hotel.

quotes.text: PATUXENT GREENS GOLF COURSE. The golf course closed in December 2018. The property was approved to be re-developed into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units. The development will also include a clubhouse, swimming pool, hiker/biker trails and other community amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: Following the transition of local recreational lands, the City approved plans for Patuxent Greens 'to be redeveloped into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units' paired with extensive walkable amenities.

quotes.text: Per the City of Laurel Unified Development Code, any multifamily development of 100 dwelling units or more approved after November 23, 2020, shall include a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as work force housing units, a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as moderately priced housing units and a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as age-restricted housing units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To ensure equitable growth, the City's Unified Development Code mandates that large-scale multifamily projects deliver 'a minimum of four percent workforce housing, four percent moderately priced housing, and four percent age-restricted housing.'

quotes.text: The redevelopment of the Main Street area and the retention of commercial uses is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability and attract shoppers.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan underscores that proactive commercial retention 'is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability.'

quotes.text: Encourage a substantial portion of future housing stock to be single-family detached homes, including high-quality custom-built homes. Strategy B: Preserve and restore single-family residences within the Historic Districts.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing strategies focus on preservation and diversity, seeking to 'encourage a substantial portion of future housing stock to be single-family detached homes, including high-quality custom-built homes' while safeguarding historic structures.

quotes.text: Compact, mixed-use, walkable design consistent with existing community character and located near available or planned transit options is encouraged to ensure efficient use of land and transportation resources and preservation and enhancement of natural system, open spaces, recreational area, and historical, cultural, and archeological resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City strongly favors sustainable design frameworks, stating that 'compact, mixed-use, walkable design consistent with existing community character and located near available or planned transit options is encouraged' to optimize resources.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.

Under this vision, future development will increasingly focus on mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects on previously developed sites, guiding new investment and redevelopment to older commercial corridors while preserving the unique character of existing low-density neighborhoods, waterfront communities, and agricultural lands.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."

By targeting revitalization within its historical core, expanding green infrastructure, and implementing forward-thinking sustainability initiatives like curbside composting and widespread EV charging, the City seeks to grow responsibly. Laurel aims to deliver a diverse and affordable housing stock, enhance multimodal transit connections (such as transit-oriented development near the MARC station), and foster inclusive public spaces that support a high quality of life for multi-generational residents.

quotes.text: LAUREL MARC - TRANSIT ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT. Located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space. The building is planned in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Transportation.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a premier transit-oriented opportunity at the Laurel MARC station, noting that 'located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space' coordinated alongside state transit partners.

quotes.text: ANDERSON’S CORNER. A mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex known as Avalon Bay (constructed), an approved 55-unit townhouse community entitled Avery Place and a Royal Farms gas station and convenience store.
quotes.briefing_quote: Anderson's Corner serves as a successful template for mixed-density development, showcasing 'a mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex, an approved 55-unit townhouse community... and a Royal Farms' convenience center.

quotes.text: WEST SIDE. A mixed-use community consisting of a 469-unit apartment complex known as Modera at Westside (constructed) and 56-unit townhouse community, which is complete. The site also has other undeveloped parcels for commercial, a hotel and a second phase townhouse development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The West Side master-planned area illustrates the demand for integrated density, featuring 'a 469-unit apartment complex... and a 56-unit townhouse community' alongside undeveloped parcels reserved for commercial space and a hotel.

quotes.text: PATUXENT GREENS GOLF COURSE. The golf course closed in December 2018. The property was approved to be re-developed into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units. The development will also include a clubhouse, swimming pool, hiker/biker trails and other community amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: Following the transition of local recreational lands, the City approved plans for Patuxent Greens 'to be redeveloped into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units' paired with extensive walkable amenities.

quotes.text: Per the City of Laurel Unified Development Code, any multifamily development of 100 dwelling units or more approved after November 23, 2020, shall include a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as work force housing units, a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as moderately priced housing units and a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as age-restricted housing units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To ensure equitable growth, the City's Unified Development Code mandates that large-scale multifamily projects deliver 'a minimum of four percent workforce housing, four percent moderately priced housing, and four percent age-restricted housing.'

quotes.text: The redevelopment of the Main Street area and the retention of commercial uses is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability and attract shoppers.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan underscores that proactive commercial retention 'is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability.'

quotes.text: Expanding the City's employment base is a core goal of this proposed strategy, and the City may have the potential to attract more professional, scientific, and technical services sector jobs in the County's strong Federal contractor sector, as well as serve as a regional center for health care and social assistance employment, by supporting more traditional office space development.

quotes.text: In 2010 the City of Mount Rainier purchased underutilized and abandoned properties and combined them into a parcel on 3200 Rhode Island Avenue and Eastern Avenue, the Washington DC borderline. In 2020 the City sold the property to the IFG Group. Their mixed-use development project consists of 97 condominiums, 11 street-level retail outlets and a 2 level underground parking garage.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a key redevelopment milestone at the Washington D.C. border where the City "purchased underutilized and abandoned properties and combined them into a parcel on 3200 Rhode Island Avenue and Eastern Avenue... [selling] the property to the IFG Group" for a mixed-use project consisting of 97 condominiums and 11 street-level retail outlets.

quotes.text: The Singer Building, a long vacant historic landmark on Rhode Island Ave at Perry Street has been completely renovated by The Menkiti Group and is open for business. The mixed-use development has 12 residential units (fully leased) and 3 new business establishments operating within 10,000 sq. ft. of retail space.
quotes.briefing_quote: Illustrating the success of local adaptive reuse, the plan notes that "The Singer Building, a long vacant historic landmark on Rhode Island Avenue at Perry Street has been completely renovated... [into a] mixed-use development with 12 residential units (fully leased) and 3 new business establishments."

quotes.text: The expansion of housing choice in the Mount Rainier Community is designed to be located in the MUTC where the city currently owns property. This is virtually the only existing area excluding a few lots in the city which are privately owned to building additional housing. The current policy is to create development of high quality without the need to access services by car. In addition, housing will be energy efficient and make use of environmentally sensitive design. Housing will increase from 100-200 units depending upon the configuration of the development according to several developers that the city has consulted with. Workforce housing will consist of approximately 8-10% of the total units.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing future growth, the plan states that the expansion of housing choice is targeted for the Mixed-Use Town Center, noting that "housing will increase from 100-200 units depending upon the configuration of the development" with workforce housing comprising about 8 to 10 percent of the units.

quotes.text: Many vacant commercial properties are privately owned and often these owners are primarily interested in leasing the properties for way above market value rate in anticipation of the speculative influx of Washington DC residents moving into the city based upon our rising housing prices and potential economic boom.
quotes.briefing_quote: Economic development officials noted a significant barrier to commercial retail growth, explaining that "many vacant commercial properties are privately owned and often these owners are primarily interested in leasing the properties for way above market value rate in anticipation of the speculative influx of Washington DC residents."

quotes.text: Vacant and underutilized sites on Rhode Island Avenue give the appearance of a deteriorating commercial environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize the downtown corridor, the plan emphasizes the need to address aesthetic and vacancy challenges, observing that "vacant and underutilized sites on Rhode Island Avenue give the appearance of a deteriorating commercial environment."

quotes.text: Mount Rainier is considered one of the last affordable housing areas in Prince George's County with homes averaging between $200k and $300k. Since property values had previously remained affordable, many homes have not suffered the 'mansionization' trend of 'flippers' doing poor quality renovations and expansions.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting the preservation of neighborhood character, the document notes that Mount Rainier remains "one of the last affordable housing areas in Prince George's County," which has protected many historic homes from the "mansionization" trend of lower-quality flipped expansions.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Brentwood aspires to become a highly livable, environmentally resilient, and inclusive municipality. By leveraging its designation in the Gateway Arts District, the town aims to stimulate green and creative economic development, particularly through the rehabilitation of commercial facades along US Route 1 and the adaptive reuse of industrial buildings for artist spaces. Simultaneously, Brentwood is pursuing key infrastructure improvements, including a $2.5 million New Town Center project, extensive stormwater management to combat local flooding, pedestrian and bicycle accessibility via Vision Zero initiatives, and programs dedicated to housing affordability, racial equity, and enabling seniors to age in place.

quotes.text: Due to a number of challenges, the City has been unable to increase its inventory of affordable housing since its designation as a Sustainable Community. Prince George’s County lacks incentive programs or affordable housing requirements tied to development like other surrounding counties, and this makes it more difficult to attract developers to Greenbelt to construct an affordable housing product even though the demand for affordable housing remains.
quotes.briefing_quote: City planners highlighted that although "the demand for affordable housing remains," the lack of county-level incentive programs "makes it more difficult to attract developers to Greenbelt to construct an affordable housing product," presenting an open opportunity for collaborative public-private partnerships.

quotes.text: Promote infill development and other redevelopment options for underutilized residential or commercial lots.

quotes.text: Opportunities for new multi-family residential development
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's housing assessment identifies "opportunities for new multi-family residential development" as a key strength to accommodate growing housing demands near major transit assets.

quotes.text: Oversee the conveyance of indoor recreation space to the City as part of the redevelopment plans of Beltway Plaza.
quotes.briefing_quote: The city's active planning goals include a strategy to "oversee the conveyance of indoor recreation space to the City as part of the redevelopment plans" of the Beltway Plaza site, fostering integrated mixed-use environments.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Laurel envisions a sustainable, vibrant, and walkable community that balances economic growth with environmental stewardship. By targeting revitalization within its historical core, expanding green infrastructure, and implementing forward-thinking sustainability initiatives like curbside composting and widespread EV charging, the City seeks to grow responsibly. Laurel aims to deliver a diverse and affordable housing stock, enhance multimodal transit connections (such as transit-oriented development near the MARC station), and foster inclusive public spaces that support a high quality of life for multi-generational residents.

quotes.text: LAUREL MARC - TRANSIT ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT. Located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space. The building is planned in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Transportation.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a premier transit-oriented opportunity at the Laurel MARC station, noting that 'located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space' coordinated alongside state transit partners.

quotes.text: ANDERSON’S CORNER. A mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex known as Avalon Bay (constructed), an approved 55-unit townhouse community entitled Avery Place and a Royal Farms gas station and convenience store.
quotes.briefing_quote: Anderson's Corner serves as a successful template for mixed-density development, showcasing 'a mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex, an approved 55-unit townhouse community... and a Royal Farms' convenience center.

quotes.text: WEST SIDE. A mixed-use community consisting of a 469-unit apartment complex known as Modera at Westside (constructed) and 56-unit townhouse community, which is complete. The site also has other undeveloped parcels for commercial, a hotel and a second phase townhouse development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The West Side master-planned area illustrates the demand for integrated density, featuring 'a 469-unit apartment complex... and a 56-unit townhouse community' alongside undeveloped parcels reserved for commercial space and a hotel.

quotes.text: PATUXENT GREENS GOLF COURSE. The golf course closed in December 2018. The property was approved to be re-developed into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units. The development will also include a clubhouse, swimming pool, hiker/biker trails and other community amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: Following the transition of local recreational lands, the City approved plans for Patuxent Greens 'to be redeveloped into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units' paired with extensive walkable amenities.

quotes.text: Per the City of Laurel Unified Development Code, any multifamily development of 100 dwelling units or more approved after November 23, 2020, shall include a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as work force housing units, a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as moderately priced housing units and a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as age-restricted housing units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To ensure equitable growth, the City's Unified Development Code mandates that large-scale multifamily projects deliver 'a minimum of four percent workforce housing, four percent moderately priced housing, and four percent age-restricted housing.'

quotes.text: The redevelopment of the Main Street area and the retention of commercial uses is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability and attract shoppers.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan underscores that proactive commercial retention 'is crucial to maintaining an economically strong Main Street; a commercial area where the image, appearance, and environment encourage walkability.'

quotes.text: Encourage a substantial portion of future housing stock to be single-family detached homes, including high-quality custom-built homes. Strategy B: Preserve and restore single-family residences within the Historic Districts.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing strategies focus on preservation and diversity, seeking to 'encourage a substantial portion of future housing stock to be single-family detached homes, including high-quality custom-built homes' while safeguarding historic structures.

quotes.text: Compact, mixed-use, walkable design consistent with existing community character and located near available or planned transit options is encouraged to ensure efficient use of land and transportation resources and preservation and enhancement of natural system, open spaces, recreational area, and historical, cultural, and archeological resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City strongly favors sustainable design frameworks, stating that 'compact, mixed-use, walkable design consistent with existing community character and located near available or planned transit options is encouraged' to optimize resources.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The North Laurel-Savage community envisions a sustainable, walkable, and vibrant future centered on Route 1 and transit-oriented hubs like the Savage MARC station. By implementing Complete Streets policies, preserving Historic Savage's unique mill town legacy, expanding affordable and energy-efficient housing options, and fostering commercial and mixed-use redevelopment, the community aims to balance economic growth with environmental conservation along the Patuxent River corridors.
