Gorman Road & US Route 1, Laurel, MD

quotes.text: The Corridor Activity Center (CAC) and Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Zoning Districts, while intended to provide a mix of uses, have primarily yielded high-density residential development with limited nonresidential (retail) in some locations
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that while designated activity centers and transit districts are designed for a mix of uses, they "have primarily yielded high-density residential development with limited nonresidential" retail, creating an opportunity for future developers to deliver more balanced commercial and community spaces.

quotes.text: Allow the development of residential and hotels within the transit oriented development areas to support nonresidential uses, such as office, retail, and entertainment, and increased MARC ridership.
quotes.briefing_quote: To build vibrant station areas, local guidelines recommend that planners "allow the development of residential and hotels within the transit oriented development areas to support nonresidential uses" like office, retail, and entertainment.

quotes.text: Allow sufficient residential densities in North Laurel District—defined in HoCo By Design as an area that will build on the existing transit-oriented community with an entertainment focus that both serves the needs of existing and future residents and offers a destination for neighboring communities-- to make a wide range of uses economically viable, including convenience retail and other neighborhood-serving amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To stimulate local economic activity, the plan advocates to "allow sufficient residential densities in North Laurel District... to make a wide range of uses economically viable," including convenience retail and other neighborhood-serving amenities.

quotes.text: Persistent high vacancy rates for ground floor retail in recent mixed-use developments on Route 1
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies a clear need to address "persistent high vacancy rates for ground floor retail in recent mixed-use developments on Route 1" by introducing more flexible zoning and economic incentives.

quotes.text: Reduction in older, smaller, more affordable single family housing units through demolition and substantial renovations that results in an increased resale value
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing analysis highlights a challenge in entry-level homeownership due to a "reduction in older, smaller, more affordable single family housing units through demolition and substantial renovations" that drive up area housing prices.

quotes.text: Aging multi-family housing stock is in need of redevelopment or upgrades. The SC area has 9% of units that were built before 1970 and 73% of units that were built before 2000 according to Howard County’s Housing Opportunities Master Plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: Data indicates that the local "aging multi-family housing stock is in need of redevelopment or upgrades," with 73 percent of multi-family units in the Sustainable Community Area originally constructed before the year 2000.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Forest Heights envisions a sustainable future driven by modernized infrastructure, expanded tree canopy, and green stormwater systems. The Town seeks to alleviate resident tax burdens by aggressively expanding its commercial base through strategic annexations and high-impact joint ventures, such as the upcoming "National Harbor 2.0" National View Project, while preserving and enhancing its affordable, well-kept single-family residential character. Additionally, the community aims to build a pedestrian bridge across MD Route 210 to safely connect both sides of the town, ensuring high walkability and strong neighborhood ties.

quotes.text: Town has very little commercial land which places a larger tax burden on its residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local leadership identified a critical fiscal challenge, noting that the "Town has very little commercial land which places a larger tax burden on its residents," underscoring the priority to attract new businesses.

quotes.text: Lack of full-service restaurants and entertainment in the incorporated limits
quotes.briefing_quote: Stakeholders emphasized a major gap in the local market, pointing to a "lack of full-service restaurants and entertainment in the incorporated limits" as an opportunity for commercial development.

quotes.text: Work with local developers for the National View Project to support tax incentives to draw businesses to National View upon its completion which will increase the Town’s tax base exponentially.
quotes.briefing_quote: The town plan details active steps to "work with local developers for the National View Project to support tax incentives to draw businesses," aiming to exponentially increase the municipal tax base upon completion.

quotes.text: Partner with local non-profits to provide affordable renovation services to low-to-moderate income homes.
quotes.briefing_quote: To enhance existing residential areas, the community plans to "partner with local non-profits to provide affordable renovation services to low-to-moderate income homes," ensuring residents can stay in well-maintained housing.

quotes.text: “National Harbor 2.0” National View Project will be built in the next year
quotes.briefing_quote: The document highlights a massive growth driver on the horizon, stating that the "'National Harbor 2.0' National View Project will be built" in the near term.

quotes.text: Greater use of Accessory Dwelling Units, which are smaller housekeeping units located on the same property as a single family home, can be investigated... They are also a way to add dwelling units without drastically changing the character of neighborhoods.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD
Cowenton Avenue & Pulaski Highway, White Marsh, MD
Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community where residents enjoy a top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, and innovative businesses. The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.
geographic_addresses: Frederick Road & Triadelphia Road, Ellicott City, MD
Broken Land Parkway & Snowden River Parkway, Columbia, MD
Woodland Road & Route 108, Ellicott City, MD
Sanner Road & Johns Hopkins Road, Clarksville, MD
Snowden River Parkway & Oakland Mills Road, Columbia, MD

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

community_organizations: Set the Captives Free Outreach, Worship and Education (OWE) Center

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Northwest Gateways community seeks to enhance its overall economic vitality, neighborhood livability, and environmental health by pursuing a vision of improved streetscapes, commercial corridor revitalization, and diverse housing options. By leveraging sustainable community programs and targeted public investments, the area strives to foster commercial growth, address transportation and pedestrian connectivity gaps, and build active, safe, and attractive neighborhoods where families of all backgrounds can thrive.

quotes.text: There is currently an affordable housing proposal within the Pikesville CRD that is requesting rezoning to support multi-family apartments.
quotes.briefing_quote: In the Pikesville Commercial Revitalization District, there is an affordable housing proposal requesting rezoning to support multi-family apartments, showing local momentum for adding density.

quotes.text: There has not been demolition of blighted properties in the area. However, there is an interest from the County to assemble vacant commercial properties on Liberty Rd to assist CDCs in redevelopment. In addition, there is discussion to redevelop the old International House of Pancakes and Bennigan's restaurants located in front of Security Square mall.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county is looking to assemble vacant commercial properties along Liberty Road to assist community development corporations in redevelopment, with further discussions centered on redeveloping the former restaurant sites in front of Security Square Mall.

quotes.text: Expand full spectrum housing for residents at diverse income levels and life stages and for individuals with disabilities by encouraging high quality mixed income, multigenerational developments. Promote Housing Accessibility Modification programs to make housing more accessible. Continue to implement smart growth policies by supporting mixed-use development and Traditional Neighborhood Development in the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning guidelines emphasize the need to encourage high-quality mixed-income, multigenerational developments while supporting smart growth policies such as mixed-use and Traditional Neighborhood Development.

quotes.text: Some homes in Colonial Village have been improved. There are homes in the Pikesville area that have gone through the zoning petition process for additions. This is largely attributed to growing families that require additional space and secondary kitchens due to religious food preparation requirements.
quotes.briefing_quote: In Pikesville, growing families are actively seeking zoning petitions for home additions and secondary kitchens to meet specific cultural and religious food preparation needs.

quotes.text: Lack of quality retail and chain restaurants in the Liberty Rd CRD... Lack of variety of businesses to meet the needs of the community... Abundance of unwanted businesses... Businesses closing and vacant gas stations are an eyesore to the residents
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback highlights a lack of quality retail and restaurant variety along the Liberty Road Commercial Revitalization District, alongside concerns over vacant storefronts and gas stations.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Glassmanor and Oxon Hill communities seek to leverage their close proximity to the District of Columbia and major transit corridors to revitalize older commercial corridors, address stormwater and environmental concerns within the Oxon Run Watershed, and improve pedestrian and bicycle connectivity. Through targeted infill redevelopment, residential property maintenance, and regulatory flexibility introduced by the Prince George's County Zoning Rewrite, the community aims to transition underutilized commercial spaces into vibrant mixed-use developments while preserving and stabilizing its established residential neighborhoods.
geographic_addresses: Southern Avenue & Indian Head Highway, Oxon Hill, MD
Wheeler Road & Iverson Street, Glassmanor, MD
Devitt Road & Maury Place, Oxon Hill, MD
Livingston Road & Oxon Hill Road, Oxon Hill, MD

quotes.text: The SC area is primarily built-out; however, in 2016, construction was initiated for a residential development on Devitt Road and Maury Place. Once completed, the development will consist of 63 townhouses.
quotes.briefing_quote: Although the Sustainable Community area is primarily built-out, infill housing opportunities exist, noting that 'construction was initiated for a residential development on Devitt Road and Maury Place' which will add 63 new townhouses upon completion.

quotes.text: The SC area continues to lack national brand retailers and does not provide offerings in several key categories such as sit-down/casual dining, quality discount clothing stores, and other lifestyle retailers.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community assessments reveal commercial gaps, indicating that the 'area continues to lack national brand retailers' and has a significant need for sit-down or casual dining, quality discount clothing, and lifestyle options.

quotes.text: It is anticipated that the approval of Prince George’s County Zoning Rewrite in 2018 will allow more flexibility to construct mixed-use development projects, promote adaptive reuse and streamline the development review process.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights regulatory advancements, noting that the new Zoning Rewrite is expected to 'allow more flexibility to construct mixed-use development projects, promote adaptive reuse' and ease the development process.

quotes.text: Promote and incentivize mixed-use infill development in shopping centers taking advantage of the under-utilized parking lots.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community actively supports land-use optimization, aiming to 'promote and incentivize mixed-use infill development in shopping centers' by repurposing under-utilized surface parking lots.

community_organizations: University of Maryland Master Gardener Program

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Suitland-Naylor Road Metro Station Area envisions transforming into a vibrant, transit-oriented, and arts-centered community. By leveraging its strategic position on the Metrorail Green Line, the community aims to absorb moderate-to-high-density mixed-use development, rehabilitate aging commercial corridors, improve pedestrian safety and connectivity, and offer diverse housing options, all while fostering social cohesion through public art, community farming, and active public spaces.
geographic_addresses: 3650 St. Barnabas Road, Suitland, MD
4524 Suitland Road, Suitland, MD
4701 Silver Hill Road, Suitland, MD
Suitland Road & Romaine Court, Suitland, MD
Eastern Lane & Romaine Court, Suitland, MD
Branch Avenue & Curtis Drive, Suitland, MD
Branch Avenue & Old Branch Avenue, Suitland, MD

quotes.text: The 25-acre neighborhood will contain a mix of residential, retail, and cultural activities. The development will contain 895 residential apartment housing units and single family attached homes as well as 98,000 sq. ft. of retail. In addition, the development will contain a 50,000 sq. ft. cultural arts and technology center that will showcase local, national, and international public art and performances.
quotes.briefing_quote: Plan authors highlighted that the upcoming "25-acre neighborhood will contain a mix of residential, retail, and cultural activities," integrating 895 apartments, single-family attached homes, and retail space near the Suitland Metro Station.

quotes.text: The purpose of the development is to create affordable, artist-friendly, and social entrepreneur/community change maker housing over the Creative Suitland Arts Center and a commercial food hall/retail space... A four-story, mixed-income, 200-unit multifamily housing development, with 12 artist studio units dedicated to households earning at or below 60% of the area median income (AMI)
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning documents outline the opportunity "to create affordable, artist-friendly, and social entrepreneur/community change maker housing over the Creative Suitland Arts Center and a commercial food hall/retail space," including 200 multifamily units.

quotes.text: Plan 2035 designated the Suitland Metro Station as one of only eight Regional Transit Districts with capacity to absorb moderate to high-density development as well as a mix of office and retail uses and designated the Naylor Road Metro Station as a Local Transit Center with capacity to function as a small-scale, mixed-use center.
quotes.briefing_quote: Under the County's General Plan, the Suitland Metro Station is designated as a Regional Transit District with "capacity to absorb moderate to high-density development as well as a mix of office and retail uses."

quotes.text: Lack of organized business improvement entities to spur improvements. Many properties have fallen into disrepair with aging facades, inconsistent signage, and poorly maintained parking lots
quotes.briefing_quote: Community planners identified a critical need to address commercial corridors, noting a "lack of organized business improvement entities to spur improvements" where many properties suffer from aging facades and inconsistent signage.

quotes.text: In 2021, the Redevelopment Authority of Prince George’s County (RDA) acquired an old 15-unit housing building for demolition and redevelopment into townhomes. In 2022, they acquired and began site preparation for the redevelopment and conversion of a vacant, blighted former coin operated laundry facility to a retail/food and beverage center located on 4524 Suitland Road.
quotes.briefing_quote: County records show active redevelopment efforts, such as acquiring a vacant laundry facility for "redevelopment and conversion... to a retail, food, and beverage center" alongside new townhome projects.

quotes.text: Continue to work with RDA, RA, and Prince George’s County DHCD to identify key properties within ½ mile of the Metro stations for transit-oriented development housing development/redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup strategies emphasize the value of partnering with regional authorities to "identify key properties within half a mile of the Metro stations for transit-oriented housing development."

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Greater Camp Springs-Town of Morningside community envisions transitioning from auto-oriented development to a sustainable, transit-supporting, and vibrant community. Center stage is the Branch Avenue Metro Station area, where the community intends to foster high-density, walkable, mixed-use developments that blend multifamily residential spaces with retail and services. The trajectory emphasizes reducing environmental footprints by restoring local streams like Henson Creek, expanding the tree canopy, and leveraging transit proximity to reduce vehicle emissions while promoting healthy lifestyles.

quotes.text: Explore strategies with WMATA that would incentivize development of the parking lots on either side of the Metro station with a dense mix of commercial and residential uses. More housing will create a demand for more services and retail uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: To maximize transit-oriented development, the plan recommends that stakeholders 'explore strategies with the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority that would incentivize development of the parking lots on either side of the Metro station with a dense mix of commercial and residential uses' to build a solid consumer base for retail.

quotes.text: More than 100 acres on either side of Auth Road and Auth Way leading to the Branch Avenue Metro Station were rezoned from a combination of C-S-C, C-M and I-3 to RTO-L-e (Regional Transit-Oriented - Low Intensity [edge]), which allows a maximum of 60 dwelling units per acre.
quotes.briefing_quote: Paving the way for high-density, transit-supportive housing, the county updated its zoning framework such that 'more than 100 acres on either side of Auth Road and Auth Way were rezoned to Regional Transit-Oriented - Low Intensity [edge], which allows a maximum of 60 dwelling units per acre.'

quotes.text: There is an imbalance between the amount of existing retail space and other land uses that generate demand for retail, which has resulted in more retail space than the area can support.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the retail vacancy rates, planners highlight a key opportunity to adjust local density, noting that 'there is an imbalance between the amount of existing retail space and other land uses,' pointing to a need for more adjacent households to bolster commercial success.

quotes.text: The RSF-65 (Residential, Single-Family) subdivisions are stable with vacant lots available for additional infill housing development.
quotes.briefing_quote: For low-density residential opportunities, the plan notes that 'the Residential, Single-Family subdivisions are stable with vacant lots available for additional infill housing development.'

quotes.text: The 25-acre neighborhood will contain a mix of residential, retail, and cultural activities. The development will contain 895 residential apartment housing units and single family attached homes as well as 98,000 sq. ft. of retail. In addition, the development will contain a 50,000 sq. ft. cultural arts and technology center that will showcase local, national, and international public art and performances.

quotes.text: The purpose of the development is to create affordable, artist-friendly, and social entrepreneur/community change maker housing over the Creative Suitland Arts Center and a commercial food hall/retail space... quotes.text: Plan 2035 designated the Suitland Metro Station as one of only eight Regional Transit Districts with capacity to absorb moderate to high-density development as well as a mix of office and retail uses and designated the Naylor Road Metro Station as a Local Transit Center with capacity to function as a small-scale, mixed-use center.
quotes.briefing_quote: Under the County's General Plan, the Suitland Metro Station is designated as a Regional Transit District with "capacity to absorb moderate to high-density development as well as a mix of office and retail uses."

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of District Heights aims to revitalize its landlocked territory through smart growth strategies focused on the redevelopment of its commercial business district along Marlboro Pike, the preservation of its natural resources, and the creation of mixed-use developments. With a strong commitment to serving its diverse population, the City seeks to expand senior housing options and enhance municipal, recreational, and youth services while fostering walkable, safe, and highly connected neighborhoods.

quotes.text: One of the largest barriers to Smart Growth in the City is the lack of land for major development. The City is landlocked and most of its existing land inventory is developed.
quotes.briefing_quote: Because the City is landlocked with a fully developed land inventory, the primary avenue for smart growth lies in the "redevelopment of underutilized commercial parcels" rather than new greenfield construction.

quotes.text: The City's Smart Growth Strategy to support future opportunities for major development consists of the redevelopment of the commercial business district (CBD), and the preservation of the City's existing housing stock and natural resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: To overcome physical growth limits, the City's strategy centers on "redeveloping the commercial business district while preserving the existing housing stock and natural resources" to create sustainable development.

quotes.text: The City owns the 11-acre property behind the Aldi on Marlboro Pike, slated to become a mixed-use development with a large recreational facility and a senior housing element is proposed on site.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City has identified a key opportunity on an "11-acre municipally owned property behind the Aldi on Marlboro Pike," which is slated for a mixed-use development featuring senior housing and a major recreational facility.

quotes.text: The City's commercial corridor is oversaturated with service-oriented businesses such as beauty salons, barber shops and small convenience stores. There is no active business association, and therefore no real platform to engage business owners in discussion around the City's revitalization goals.
quotes.briefing_quote: Revitalization efforts note that the current commercial corridor is "oversaturated with service-oriented businesses," pointing to a critical need for targeted retail diversification and the establishment of a formal merchants association.

quotes.text: Support and incentivize the forthcoming mixed-use development including senior housing for the St Paul's Town Center site adjacent to Great Eastern Plaza.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Action Plan prioritizes efforts to "support and incentivize the forthcoming mixed-use development," including senior housing, at the St. Paul's Town Center site adjacent to Great Eastern Plaza.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Anne Arundel County envisions a future where it embraces its rich Chesapeake culture, heritage, and invaluable ecosystems while directing growth toward smart, green, and equitable development. Under this vision, future development will increasingly focus on mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects on previously developed sites, guiding new investment and redevelopment to older commercial corridors while preserving the unique character of existing low-density neighborhoods, waterfront communities, and agricultural lands.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

community_organizations: Arts & Humanities Council of Montgomery County

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aims to foster a well-planned, livable, and safe community that offers a high quality of life for its growing, aging, and increasingly diverse population. Guided by Thrive Montgomery 2050, the county's vision centers on compact, walkable, and mixed-use development supported by strong pedestrian, bicycle, and transit infrastructure to drive economic competitiveness, environmental resilience, and racial equity.

quotes.text: A third of all County land has zoning that generally only allows detached housing leaving limited land available for medium to high density housing
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "a third of all County land has zoning that generally only allows detached housing," which severely restricts the availability of land for much-needed medium- to high-density residential options.

quotes.text: Too few rental communities that offer family-sized units of three- or more bedrooms.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county identifies a gap in multi-family development, stating there are "too few rental communities that offer family-sized units of three or more bedrooms," presenting an active opportunity for developer focus.

quotes.text: Sustained remote work has increased commercial vacancy rates
quotes.briefing_quote: The county highlights commercial real estate challenges, noting that "sustained remote work has increased commercial vacancy rates," pointing to opportunities for commercial repositioning or adaptive re-use.

quotes.text: Elizabeth Square, located in downtown Silver Spring, is a multi-generational, mixed-income, mixed-use project featuring residential coupled with a state-of-the-art recreation facility and other community amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights successful mixed-use models like Elizabeth Square, describing it as "a multi-generational, mixed-income, mixed-use project featuring residential coupled with a state-of-the-art recreation facility" and civic amenities.

quotes.text: Inadequate supply of affordable housing to address population’s needs and variety of income levels, specifically for elderly, very low-income levels, and people with disabilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: County planning documents address housing gaps, noting an "inadequate supply of affordable housing to address population's needs and variety of income levels," specifically for seniors and residents with disabilities.

quotes.text: Since the last application, we have identified several communities facing such dire, long-standing safety-related interior and exterior building hazards needing immediate repair/replacement, including Hermitage Woods in the Aspen Hill area... built in 1973 this multi-story, apartment-to-condo 37-unit complex units has such extensive structural damage that it is on the verge of being condemned
quotes.briefing_quote: The application emphasizes the urgent need for reinvestment in aging properties, noting several multi-family complexes face "dire, long-standing safety-related interior and exterior building hazards needing immediate repair or replacement."

quotes.text: A third of all County land has zoning that generally only allows detached housing leaving limited land available for medium to high density housing
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "a third of all County land has zoning that generally only allows detached housing," which severely restricts the availability of land for much-needed medium- to high-density residential options.

quotes.text: Too few rental communities that offer family-sized units of three- or more bedrooms.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county identifies a gap in multi-family development, stating there are "too few rental communities that offer family-sized units of three or more bedrooms," presenting an active opportunity for developer focus.

quotes.text: Sustained remote work has increased commercial vacancy rates
quotes.briefing_quote: The county highlights commercial real estate challenges, noting that "sustained remote work has increased commercial vacancy rates," pointing to opportunities for commercial repositioning or adaptive re-use.

quotes.text: Elizabeth Square, located in downtown Silver Spring, is a multi-generational, mixed-income, mixed-use project featuring residential coupled with a state-of-the-art recreation facility and other community amenities.

quotes.text: Inadequate supply of affordable housing to address population’s needs and variety of income levels, specifically for elderly, very low-income levels, and people with disabilities.

quotes.text: Since the last application, we have identified several communities facing such dire, long-standing safety-related interior and exterior building hazards needing immediate repair/replacement, including Hermitage Woods in the Aspen Hill area... built in 1973 this multi-story, apartment-to-condo 37-unit complex units has such extensive structural damage that it is on the verge of being condemned
quotes.briefing_quote: The application emphasizes the urgent need for reinvestment in aging properties, noting several multi-family complexes face "dire, long-standing safety-related interior and exterior building hazards needing immediate repair or replacement."

The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Brookeville seeks to preserve and foster the values of its Quaker founders—neighborliness, hospitality, industriousness, and charity—by safeguarding its historic 19th-century rural village character. With the completion of the Brookeville Bypass, the Town focuses on reclaiming its streets for local traffic and pedestrians, reconnecting its sidewalk and trail networks, and directing very limited residential and commercial growth in a low-density, highly sensitive manner that respects its cultural landscape.
geographic_addresses: High Street & Market Street, Brookeville, MD
North Street & Market Street, Brookeville, MD
Brighton Dam Road & East Market Street, Brookeville, MD
Georgia Avenue & Brookeville Road, Brookeville, MD

quotes.text: Land use within the Town under this Plan shall continue to be comprised of single-family detached residences at the less intense density of 1 unit per acre of land.
quotes.briefing_quote: To reinforce the town's architectural character, the plan guides future development by noting that 'land use within the Town under this Plan shall continue to be comprised of single-family detached residences at the less intense density of 1 unit per acre of land.'

quotes.text: While maintaining a density of one dwelling unit per acre for developable properties, clustering under the HVR zone allows flexibility in creating an in-fill plan that can be wholly integrated into the Town’s historical pattern of development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners advocate for conservation-minded residential layouts, explaining that 'while maintaining a density of one dwelling unit per acre for developable properties, clustering under the Historic Village Residential zone allows flexibility in creating an in-fill plan that can be wholly integrated into the Town’s historical pattern of development.'

quotes.text: Permitted uses in the HVC zone shall be limited to single-family detached residential and low intensity commercial and professional office uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: To prevent incompatible business growth, the plan states that 'permitted uses in the Historic Village Commercial zone shall be limited to single-family detached residential and low intensity commercial and professional office uses.'

quotes.text: Within the Town itself, the pressure for in-fill development has presented an increased likelihood for congestion and the possibility of compromising the Town’s historic character.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing local physical limitations, the plan observes that 'within the Town itself, the pressure for in-fill development has presented an increased likelihood for congestion and the possibility of compromising the Town’s historic character.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of District Heights aims to revitalize its landlocked territory through smart growth strategies focused on the redevelopment of its commercial business district along Marlboro Pike, the preservation of its natural resources, and the creation of mixed-use developments. With a strong commitment to serving its diverse population, the City seeks to expand senior housing options and enhance municipal, recreational, and youth services while fostering walkable, safe, and highly connected neighborhoods.
geographic_addresses: 2000 Marbury Drive, District Heights, MD
Marlboro Pike, District Heights, MD
District Heights Parkway, District Heights, MD
Kipling Parkway, District Heights, MD

quotes.text: One of the largest barriers to Smart Growth in the City is the lack of land for major development. The City is landlocked and most of its existing land inventory is developed.
quotes.briefing_quote: Because the City is landlocked with a fully developed land inventory, the primary avenue for smart growth lies in the "redevelopment of underutilized commercial parcels" rather than new greenfield construction.

quotes.text: The City's Smart Growth Strategy to support future opportunities for major development consists of the redevelopment of the commercial business district (CBD), and the preservation of the City's existing housing stock and natural resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: To overcome physical growth limits, the City's strategy centers on "redeveloping the commercial business district while preserving the existing housing stock and natural resources" to create sustainable development.

quotes.text: The City owns the 11-acre property behind the Aldi on Marlboro Pike, slated to become a mixed-use development with a large recreational facility and a senior housing element is proposed on site.
quotes.briefing_quote: The City has identified a key opportunity on an "11-acre municipally owned property behind the Aldi on Marlboro Pike," which is slated for a mixed-use development featuring senior housing and a major recreational facility.

quotes.text: The City's commercial corridor is oversaturated with service-oriented businesses such as beauty salons, barber shops and small convenience stores. There is no active business association, and therefore no real platform to engage business owners in discussion around the City's revitalization goals.
quotes.briefing_quote: Revitalization efforts note that the current commercial corridor is "oversaturated with service-oriented businesses," pointing to a critical need for targeted retail diversification and the establishment of a formal merchants association.

quotes.text: Support and incentivize the forthcoming mixed-use development including senior housing for the St Paul's Town Center site adjacent to Great Eastern Plaza.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Action Plan prioritizes efforts to "support and incentivize the forthcoming mixed-use development," including senior housing, at the St. Paul's Town Center site adjacent to Great Eastern Plaza.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Suitland-Naylor Road Metro Station Area envisions transforming into a vibrant, transit-oriented, and arts-centered community. By leveraging its strategic position on the Metrorail Green Line, the community aims to absorb moderate-to-high-density mixed-use development, rehabilitate aging commercial corridors, improve pedestrian safety and connectivity, and offer diverse housing options, all while fostering social cohesion through public art, community farming, and active public spaces.
geographic_addresses: 3650 St. Barnabas Road, Suitland, MD
4524 Suitland Road, Suitland, MD
4701 Silver Hill Road, Suitland, MD
Suitland Road & Romaine Court, Suitland, MD
Eastern Lane & Romaine Court, Suitland, MD
Branch Avenue & Curtis Drive, Suitland, MD
Branch Avenue & Old Branch Avenue, Suitland, MD

quotes.text: The 25-acre neighborhood will contain a mix of residential, retail, and cultural activities. The development will contain 895 residential apartment housing units and single family attached homes as well as 98,000 sq. ft. of retail. In addition, the development will contain a 50,000 sq. ft. cultural arts and technology center that will showcase local, national, and international public art and performances.
quotes.briefing_quote: Plan authors highlighted that the upcoming "25-acre neighborhood will contain a mix of residential, retail, and cultural activities," integrating 895 apartments, single-family attached homes, and retail space near the Suitland Metro Station.

quotes.text: The purpose of the development is to create affordable, artist-friendly, and social entrepreneur/community change maker housing over the Creative Suitland Arts Center and a commercial food hall/retail space... A four-story, mixed-income, 200-unit multifamily housing development, with 12 artist studio units dedicated to households earning at or below 60% of the area median income (AMI)
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning documents outline the opportunity "to create affordable, artist-friendly, and social entrepreneur/community change maker housing over the Creative Suitland Arts Center and a commercial food hall/retail space," including 200 multifamily units.

quotes.text: Plan 2035 designated the Suitland Metro Station as one of only eight Regional Transit Districts with capacity to absorb moderate to high-density development as well as a mix of office and retail uses and designated the Naylor Road Metro Station as a Local Transit Center with capacity to function as a small-scale, mixed-use center.
quotes.briefing_quote: Under the County's General Plan, the Suitland Metro Station is designated as a Regional Transit District with "capacity to absorb moderate to high-density development as well as a mix of office and retail uses."

quotes.text: Lack of organized business improvement entities to spur improvements. Many properties have fallen into disrepair with aging facades, inconsistent signage, and poorly maintained parking lots
quotes.briefing_quote: Community planners identified a critical need to address commercial corridors, noting a "lack of organized business improvement entities to spur improvements" where many properties suffer from aging facades and inconsistent signage.

quotes.text: In 2021, the Redevelopment Authority of Prince George’s County (RDA) acquired an old 15-unit housing building for demolition and redevelopment into townhomes. In 2022, they acquired and began site preparation for the redevelopment and conversion of a vacant, blighted former coin operated laundry facility to a retail/food and beverage center located on 4524 Suitland Road.
quotes.briefing_quote: County records show active redevelopment efforts, such as acquiring a vacant laundry facility for "redevelopment and conversion... to a retail, food, and beverage center" alongside new townhome projects.

quotes.text: Continue to work with RDA, RA, and Prince George’s County DHCD to identify key properties within ½ mile of the Metro stations for transit-oriented development housing development/redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup strategies emphasize the value of partnering with regional authorities to "identify key properties within half a mile of the Metro stations for transit-oriented housing development."

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Greater Chillum community envisions a stable, cohesive, and walkable transit-oriented environment that leverages its proximity to Washington, D.C. and regional transit assets. By merging adjacent neighborhoods like Carole Highland, Lewisdale, and Adelphi into a single Sustainable Community entity, local leaders aim to revitalize aging single-use commercial retail centers into vibrant mixed-use places, upgrade housing conditions while preserving established single-family residential character, expand multi-modal pedestrian and bicycle connectivity, and implement robust green infrastructure to manage rising stormwater flooding concerns.

quotes.text: in 2017, construction was initiated for a mixed-use development at the intersection of Northwest Drive and Toledo Terrace. Once completed, the development will consist of 2,750 dwelling units and 289,480 square feet of commercial space.
quotes.briefing_quote: A major mixed-use development under construction at Northwest Drive and Toledo Terrace is slated to bring 2,750 dwelling units and 289,480 square feet of commercial space within walking distance of transit.

quotes.text: WMATA is planning to offer its property at the West Hyattsville Metro Station for redevelopment into a transit-oriented development (TOD). Privately owned, single-use commercial properties adjacent to this WMATA station property are already zoned for redevelopment at mixed-use transit density.
quotes.briefing_quote: Transit planners highlighted the potential to redevelop the West Hyattsville Metro Station property and adjacent single-use commercial assets into high-density transit-oriented development.

quotes.text: The SC area continues to lack national brand retailers and is limited in several key categories such as sit-down/casual dining, and other lifestyle retailers.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback emphasizes that the Sustainable Community area lacks national brand retailers and remains limited in sit-down or casual dining and other lifestyle retail options.

quotes.text: Demographic shifts have created a shortage of affordable housing and caused the conversion of owner-occupied units to overcrowd rentals. Multifamily housing stock is aging, most complexes approaching 50 years.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community report raises concerns that aging multi-family housing stock and a shortage of affordable choices have triggered the conversion of single-family owner-occupied homes into overcrowded rentals.

quotes.text: Notwithstanding the completion of 71 new Townhouses at 'Avondale Ridge', on MD 500 (Queens Chapel Road) in the Avondale Ridge Neighborhood in 2018, the total number housing units in the SC area decreased from 11,487 in 2015 to 10,924 in 2020
quotes.briefing_quote: Despite the addition of 71 new townhomes at Avondale Ridge, the total housing unit supply in the Sustainable Community area decreased slightly over the five-year period.

quotes.text: Embrace mixed-use redevelopment of failing retail centers and adaptive reuse underutilized buildings.
quotes.briefing_quote: To modernize the local economy, the plan recommends that stakeholders embrace mixed-use redevelopment of failing retail centers and the adaptive reuse of underutilized buildings.

quotes.text: Identify locations for small infill projects such as townhouses that modestly increase residential density.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community strategies support locating small infill projects like townhomes to modestly increase residential density while preserving single-family neighborhoods.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Langley Park envisions transitioning into a vibrant, transit-oriented gateway that leverages the construction of the Purple Line light rail while preserving its naturally occurring affordable housing and rich cultural diversity. The community seeks to revitalize its commercial districts—especially the International Corridor—through denser, mixed-use development, streetscape beautification, and creative placemaking. Addressing persistent infrastructure and social challenges, the plan aims to improve pedestrian and bicycle safety, modernize aging multifamily rental housing, preserve environmental assets like the Northwest Branch Trail, and elevate the quality of life through enhanced health, language, and youth recreation services.

quotes.text: Support TOD and denser mixed-use development in coordination with the construction of the Purple Line to provide denser retail typologies different from the existing strip retail centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: To leverage incoming transit investments, the plan recommends that developers 'support TOD [Transit-Oriented Development] and denser mixed-use development in coordination with the construction of the Purple Line to provide denser retail typologies different from the existing strip retail centers.'

quotes.text: The housing stock is predominantly aging multi-family apartment units. Most of these units were built in the 1950s, when lead paint and asbestos were used in housing construction. Many of these units have not been substantially upgraded.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community highlights a critical need for modernization, noting that the local 'housing stock is predominantly aging multi-family apartment units' constructed in the 1950s, which creates a prime opportunity to substantially upgrade and improve multifamily conditions.

quotes.text: Increase the number of affordable rental housing units that include 3 and 4 bedrooms to accommodate larger families and prevent overcrowding.
quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate local household structures, community leaders identify a pressing need to 'increase the number of affordable rental housing units that include 3 and 4 bedrooms to accommodate larger families and prevent overcrowding.'

quotes.text: In 2021, the Prince George’s County Planning Department completed the Takoma/Langley Crossroads Planning and Implementation Study, which builds on the 2019 Approved Takoma Langley Sector Plan by developing implementation tools and strategies to support denser, mixed use and walkable development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning frameworks support forward-looking projects, specifically 'developing implementation tools and strategies to support denser, mixed use and walkable development' around key transit nodes.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Langley Park envisions transitioning into a vibrant, transit-oriented gateway that leverages the construction of the Purple Line light rail while preserving its naturally occurring affordable housing and rich cultural diversity. The community seeks to revitalize its commercial districts—especially the International Corridor—through denser, mixed-use development, streetscape beautification, and creative placemaking. Addressing persistent infrastructure and social challenges, the plan aims to improve pedestrian and bicycle safety, modernize aging multifamily rental housing, preserve environmental assets like the Northwest Branch Trail, and elevate the quality of life through enhanced health, language, and youth recreation services.

quotes.text: Support TOD and denser mixed-use development in coordination with the construction of the Purple Line to provide denser retail typologies different from the existing strip retail centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: To leverage incoming transit investments, the plan recommends that developers 'support TOD [Transit-Oriented Development] and denser mixed-use development in coordination with the construction of the Purple Line to provide denser retail typologies different from the existing strip retail centers.'

quotes.text: The housing stock is predominantly aging multi-family apartment units. Most of these units were built in the 1950s, when lead paint and asbestos were used in housing construction. Many of these units have not been substantially upgraded.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community highlights a critical need for modernization, noting that the local 'housing stock is predominantly aging multi-family apartment units' constructed in the 1950s, which creates a prime opportunity to substantially upgrade and improve multifamily conditions.

quotes.text: Increase the number of affordable rental housing units that include 3 and 4 bedrooms to accommodate larger families and prevent overcrowding.
quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate local household structures, community leaders identify a pressing need to 'increase the number of affordable rental housing units that include 3 and 4 bedrooms to accommodate larger families and prevent overcrowding.'

quotes.text: In 2021, the Prince George’s County Planning Department completed the Takoma/Langley Crossroads Planning and Implementation Study, which builds on the 2019 Approved Takoma Langley Sector Plan by developing implementation tools and strategies to support denser, mixed use and walkable development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning frameworks support forward-looking projects, specifically 'developing implementation tools and strategies to support denser, mixed use and walkable development' around key transit nodes.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of College Park envisions a diverse, vibrant, connected, and economically successful university community. By partnering with the University of Maryland, the community seeks to stabilize and preserve historic neighborhoods, foster smart growth and transit-oriented development, expand housing diversity, support locally owned businesses, and champion environmental sustainability and climate resilience.

9219 51st Avenue, College Park, MD
