quotes.text: Development has been stalled in this area due to an outdated plan that did not truly promote transit-oriented development. A new Transit District Development Plan was adopted by Prince George’s County in 2015 and prospects have improved. A WMATA joint development project was approved for 400 apartment units and 10,000 SF of retail and County owned property across from the Metro station is being sold for mixed-use development.
quotes.briefing_quote: While past development near the Metro station was hindered by outdated zoning, the adoption of a new Transit District Development Plan has unlocked major opportunities, including an approved project featuring "400 apartment units and 10,000 square feet of retail" alongside county-owned property slated for transit-oriented mixed-use development.

quotes.text: The City has approved 10 new multifamily/townhouse projects since 2017 amounting to an increase of 2,626 dwelling units. About a dozen single-family home infill development has occurred. ... Most new development in College Park is redevelopment of commercial corridors and centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: Indicating a strong market preference for higher-density redevelopment in commercial areas, the plan notes that "the City has approved 10 new multifamily/townhouse projects since 2017" representing an addition of 2,626 dwelling units.

quotes.text: Strengthen College Park neighborhoods by reducing the number of single-family homes that are converted to group rental properties by continuing to offer homeownership grant programs, establishing a community land trust, and exploring new programs for housing rehabilitation with Habitat for Humanity Maryland.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community aims to stabilize residential areas, seeking to "strengthen College Park neighborhoods by reducing the number of single-family homes that are converted to group rental properties" through the creation of a community land trust and targeted homeownership programs.

quotes.text: Use recently acquired property on Calvert Road for the development of missing middle housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To promote housing type diversity, community planning goals advise the city to "use recently acquired property on Calvert Road for the development of missing middle housing" as a bridge between low- and high-density neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many long-term businesses have closed or have been relocated due to new development. ARPA assistance was provided to many businesses and has helped, but high rents are making it difficult for local, independent businesses to survive and for other to enter the market.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting a clear opportunity for developers to build affordable storefront spaces, the plan notes that "high rents are making it difficult for local, independent businesses to survive and for others to enter the market" amid ongoing corridor redevelopment.

quotes.text: Route 1 has seen tremendous redevelopment activity since being rezoned from C-S-C (Commercial Shopping Center) to M-U-I (Mixed-Use Infill) in 2001 and is successfully transforming from a strip commercial corridor to a mixed-use boulevard with a series of walkable nodes
quotes.briefing_quote: Due to progressive zoning changes, the US Route 1 corridor is "successfully transforming from a strip commercial corridor to a mixed-use boulevard with a series of walkable nodes" that enhance local economic vibrancy.

quotes.briefing_quote: Indicating a strong market preference for higher-density redevelopment in commercial areas, the plan notes that "the City has approved 10 new multifamily/townhouse projects since 2017" representing an addition of 2,626 dwelling units.

quotes.text: Strengthen College Park neighborhoods by reducing the number of single-family homes that are converted to group rental properties by continuing to offer homeownership grant programs, establishing a community land trust, and exploring new programs for housing rehabilitation with Habitat for Humanity Maryland.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community aims to stabilize residential areas, seeking to "strengthen College Park neighborhoods by reducing the number of single-family homes that are converted to group rental properties" through the creation of a community land trust and targeted homeownership programs.

quotes.text: Use recently acquired property on Calvert Road for the development of missing middle housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To promote housing type diversity, community planning goals advise the city to "use recently acquired property on Calvert Road for the development of missing middle housing" as a bridge between low- and high-density neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many long-term businesses have closed or have been relocated due to new development. ARPA assistance was provided to many businesses and has helped, but high rents are making it difficult for local, independent businesses to survive and for other to enter the market.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting a clear opportunity for developers to build affordable storefront spaces, the plan notes that "high rents are making it difficult for local, independent businesses to survive and for others to enter the market" amid ongoing corridor redevelopment.

quotes.text: Route 1 has seen tremendous redevelopment activity since being rezoned from C-S-C (Commercial Shopping Center) to M-U-I (Mixed-Use Infill) in 2001 and is successfully transforming from a strip commercial corridor to a mixed-use boulevard with a series of walkable nodes
quotes.briefing_quote: Due to progressive zoning changes, the US Route 1 corridor is "successfully transforming from a strip commercial corridor to a mixed-use boulevard with a series of walkable nodes" that enhance local economic vibrancy.

community_organizations: College Park Neighborhood Quality of Life Committee
College Park Committee for a Better Environment

properties.tract_name: The town-center of Calverton

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

community_organizations: Arts & Humanities Council of Montgomery County

plan_quotes.community_vision: The community of Landover Hills, New Carrollton, and surrounding unincorporated areas seeks to leverage transit-oriented development opportunities from the New Carrollton transit hub and incoming Purple Line light rail. The vision focuses on revitalizing aging commercial corridors and shopping centers through mixed-use infill development and pedestrian streetscape enhancements, while aggressively preserving existing housing affordability and protecting stable residential neighborhoods from displacement.

quotes.text: Encourage mixed-use development at Purple Line Light Rail and Metro stations that includes office development to increase daytime population for local businesses.
quotes.briefing_quote: To capitalize on transit expansion, the plan recommends to "encourage mixed-use development at Purple Line Light Rail and Metro stations that includes office development to increase daytime population for local businesses."

quotes.text: Overpopulated neighborhood businesses and service providers in the SC Area (laundromats, nail salons, liquor stores, gas stations, pawn shops, etc.), and lack of quality restaurants.
quotes.briefing_quote: Stakeholders identified an imbalance in commercial retail variety, noting an "overpopulation of neighborhood businesses and service providers in the Sustainable Community Area... and lack of quality restaurants."

quotes.text: As this SC Area’s transit amenities grow, it will be essential for residents, community leaders, municipalities, and agency partners to utilize program funding opportunities to preserve and protect existing stable residential neighborhoods.
quotes.briefing_quote: As infrastructure expands, the plan notes that "it will be essential for residents, community leaders, municipalities, and agency partners to utilize program funding opportunities to preserve and protect existing stable residential neighborhoods" from displacement and speculative market forces.

quotes.text: Promote and incentivize mixed-use infill development in shopping centers taking advantage of the under-utilized parking lots.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revive stagnant commercial properties, the plan urges local entities to "promote and incentivize mixed-use infill development in shopping centers taking advantage of the under-utilized parking lots."

quotes.text: As noted in the Housing element of this action plan, there are already cases of development in this region that do little to support maintaining affordable and diverse housing options for the existing residential neighborhoods.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community members expressed caution regarding certain new residential builds, noting "there are already cases of development in this region that do little to support maintaining affordable and diverse housing options for the existing residential neighborhoods."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community where residents enjoy a top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, and innovative businesses. The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.
geographic_addresses: Frederick Road & Triadelphia Road, Ellicott City, MD
Broken Land Parkway & Snowden River Parkway, Columbia, MD
Woodland Road & Route 108, Ellicott City, MD
Sanner Road & Johns Hopkins Road, Clarksville, MD
Snowden River Parkway & Oakland Mills Road, Columbia, MD

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD
Cowenton Avenue & Pulaski Highway, White Marsh, MD
Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Catonsville-Patapsco community envisions a sustainable, well-connected, and culturally vibrant future. Key aspirations include expanding the local arts ecosystem through the newly designated Catonsville Arts and Entertainment District along Frederick Road, improving active transportation and trail connectivity via groups like Catonsville Rails to Trails, and preserving watershed resources near Patapsco Valley State Park. The community aims to revitalize legacy neighborhoods, address commercial vacancies, and expand quality housing choices—including affordable housing partnerships and accessory dwelling units (ADUs)—while navigating existing low-density zoning constraints that historically limit larger-scale infill development.

Ingleside Ave & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD

S. Paradise Ave & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD
Mellor Ave & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD
Winters Lane & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD

quotes.text: Scarcity of undeveloped properties within residential and commercial zones, thereby limiting the potential for larger scale new development or infill
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes a 'scarcity of undeveloped properties within residential and commercial zones, thereby limiting the potential for larger-scale new development or infill,' highlighting the critical importance of strategic infill projects.

quotes.text: Barriers to higher density development (including policies, development process, NIMBYs).
quotes.briefing_quote: The assessment identifies clear 'barriers to higher density development (including policies, development process, NIMBYs)' that must be navigated to successfully introduce multi-family and mixed-use options.

quotes.text: The majority of zoning in the Catonsville SC area is low density residential, that primarily supports single family development. ... The current residential zoning in the majority of the SC Area does not easily support higher density development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning staff emphasized that 'the majority of zoning in the Catonsville Sustainable Community Area is low density residential, which primarily supports single family development' and does not easily accommodate higher density development styles.

quotes.text: Zoning changes occur through the County’s CZMP process... several of these requests for change were denied, though a few were approved to allow for mixed uses along MD 144.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recent comprehensive zoning reviews show progress, noting that while some requests were denied, 'a few were approved to allow for mixed uses along MD 144' to align with main street commercial revitalization goals.

quotes.text: Support the development of new accessory dwelling units (ADUs) within appropriate settings within the SC area through the development process and policy development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community intends to 'support the development of new accessory dwelling units (ADUs) within appropriate settings within the Sustainable Community Area through the development process and policy development' to broaden localized residential choices.

quotes.text: The Fitzgerald apartment building, located at 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue in Mid-Town Belvedere, is an example of a successful Transit Oriented Development project in Baltimore. Built in 2010, adjacent to the Mt. Royal/MICA Light Rail station, the seven-story building has 275 apartment units and two commercial establishments on the lower level
quotes.briefing_quote: A prime example of successful transit-oriented development is the Fitzgerald apartment building, which stands as a seven-story building with 275 apartment units and ground-floor commercial establishments adjacent to the Light Rail, showcasing how dense, mixed-use infill can thrive in Baltimore.

quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. These areas are relatively rich in the resources needed for quality of life and healthy child development, but as a result of a long practice of exclusion, they currently have limited affordable housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To affirmatively further fair housing, the plan emphasizes that in stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed-income developments to reverse long practices of exclusion.

quotes.text: Replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and the vacant former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, new elementary middle school, two new parks, and a renovated and expanded Chick Webb Recreation Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Perkins Somerset Oldtown Transformation Plan represents a massive revitalization effort, replacing obsolete housing with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, and essential community spaces.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. quotes.briefing_quote: Housing policy experts highlighted the critical need to support middle neighborhoods, noting that these homes generate wealth over generations for families whose future security is tied to their communities' ongoing success.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD
Cowenton Avenue & Pulaski Highway, White Marsh, MD
Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

community_organizations: Set the Captives Free Outreach, Worship and Education (OWE) Center

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Catonsville-Patapsco community envisions a sustainable, well-connected, and culturally vibrant future. Key aspirations include expanding the local arts ecosystem through the newly designated Catonsville Arts and Entertainment District along Frederick Road, improving active transportation and trail connectivity via groups like Catonsville Rails to Trails, and preserving watershed resources near Patapsco Valley State Park. The community aims to revitalize legacy neighborhoods, address commercial vacancies, and expand quality housing choices—including affordable housing partnerships and accessory dwelling units (ADUs)—while navigating existing low-density zoning constraints that historically limit larger-scale infill development.

Mellor Ave & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD
Winters Lane & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD

quotes.text: Scarcity of undeveloped properties within residential and commercial zones, thereby limiting the potential for larger scale new development or infill
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes a 'scarcity of undeveloped properties within residential and commercial zones, thereby limiting the potential for larger-scale new development or infill,' highlighting the critical importance of strategic infill projects.

quotes.text: Barriers to higher density development (including policies, development process, NIMBYs).
quotes.briefing_quote: The assessment identifies clear 'barriers to higher density development (including policies, development process, NIMBYs)' that must be navigated to successfully introduce multi-family and mixed-use options.

quotes.text: The majority of zoning in the Catonsville SC area is low density residential, that primarily supports single family development. ... The current residential zoning in the majority of the SC Area does not easily support higher density development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning staff emphasized that 'the majority of zoning in the Catonsville Sustainable Community Area is low density residential, which primarily supports single family development' and does not easily accommodate higher density development styles.

quotes.text: Zoning changes occur through the County’s CZMP process... several of these requests for change were denied, though a few were approved to allow for mixed uses along MD 144.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recent comprehensive zoning reviews show progress, noting that while some requests were denied, 'a few were approved to allow for mixed uses along MD 144' to align with main street commercial revitalization goals.

quotes.text: Support the development of new accessory dwelling units (ADUs) within appropriate settings within the SC area through the development process and policy development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community intends to 'support the development of new accessory dwelling units (ADUs) within appropriate settings within the Sustainable Community Area through the development process and policy development' to broaden localized residential choices.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Queen Anne's County aspires to preserve its character as a quintessential rural and agricultural community while managing orderly growth. By directing new commercial, industrial, and residential development to established town centers and designated Growth Areas (Chester, Stevensville, Grasonville, and Kent Narrows) where adequate infrastructure and public facilities exist, the County aims to protect its natural resources, agricultural land base, and waterfront heritage for future generations.
geographic_addresses: Main Street & Castle Marina Road, Chester, MD
Main Street & Chester River Beach Road, Grasonville, MD
Commerce Street & Broadway, Centreville, MD
Main Street & Walnut Street, Church Hill, MD
US 301 & MD 304, Centreville, MD
Del Rhodes Avenue, Queenstown, MD
Church Street & Miller Street, Sudlersville, MD
Main Street, Stevensville, MD
Goldsboro Road, Barclay, MD

quotes.text: Expanding the areas where multi-family and apartment development is allowed would increase the availability of development sites and reduce the cost of land per unit. The County and municipalities should review and increase allowable densities where appropriate.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address the housing shortage, the plan notes that "expanding the areas where multi-family and apartment development is allowed" would increase the availability of development sites and reduce land costs per unit.

quotes.text: By reducing the growth of new residential development in agricultural and rural areas... encouraging and directing growth to existing communities and within designated areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county's primary growth management strategy focuses on "reducing the growth of new residential development in agricultural and rural areas" by directing future growth into established communities.

quotes.text: In the Grasonville Village Center, low- and medium-intensity commercial uses are encouraged, along with single-family and multi-family housing. The existing village scale is maintained and enhanced so that this area once again becomes a true village center...
quotes.briefing_quote: For the Grasonville Village Center, the plan outlines an opportunity where "low- and medium-intensity commercial uses are encouraged, along with single-family and multi-family housing" to help reestablish a vibrant village scale.

quotes.text: It is the County's intent that remaining un-allocated sewer capacity should be reserved for commercial uses, directing any new residential development to the incorporated towns that have capacity to accommodate it. Infill development is development that takes place on vacant, undeveloped or underutilized parcels within an area that is already characterized by development...
quotes.briefing_quote: To address infrastructure constraints, the plan stresses the need to "reserve remaining sewer capacity for commercial uses, directing any new residential development to the incorporated towns" that have the capacity to accommodate it.

quotes.text: Many communities are making zoning provisions for 'Missing Middle' housing—housing types with unit sizes and densities between those of single-family and multi-family zones... They include small-lot single-family units, duplexes, triplexes, townhouses, cottage homes, and small multi-family buildings of four to eight units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To provide more diverse and affordable choices, the plan encourages zoning provisions for "'Missing Middle' housing—housing types with unit sizes and densities between those of single-family and multi-family zones".

quotes.text: The Centreville water service map also shows an area designated as W-3 at the intersection of US 301/MD 304. This is an area that has a mixture of commercial, industrial, and municipal uses. In addition, there are some parcels that are currently agricultural. It was suggested that the vacant areas be developed into a County-developed business park.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning framework identifies a strategic opportunity at the intersection of US 301 and MD 304 to develop vacant agricultural parcels into a County-developed business park, supporting a balanced mix of commercial, industrial, and municipal uses.

quotes.text: Both the Town and County Comprehensive Plans call for a mix of residential and commercial land uses on lands in and adjacent to the Town and within the Queenstown Growth Area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Comprehensive strategies for Queenstown emphasize the need to integrate a balanced mix of residential and commercial land uses within the designated growth area to foster vibrant local development.

quotes.text: TRUE commercial apartments – zoning may need to be refined such that the apartments would be ancillary to the commercial, not the other way around.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better manage infrastructure and sewer allocations, the technical committee recommended refining zoning guidelines to encourage true commercial apartments that function strictly as ancillary to commercial developments.

quotes.text: Prohibit any further large-scale residential development. Remove large vacant parcels from the Growth Area – rezone/downzone if required
quotes.briefing_quote: Wastewater capacity limitations have prompted calls to prohibit further large-scale residential developments and potentially rezone or downzone large vacant parcels out of active Growth Areas to protect local infrastructure.

The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.
geographic_addresses: Frederick Road & Triadelphia Road, Ellicott City, MD
Broken Land Parkway & Snowden River Parkway, Columbia, MD
Woodland Road & Route 108, Ellicott City, MD
Sanner Road & Johns Hopkins Road, Clarksville, MD
Snowden River Parkway & Oakland Mills Road, Columbia, MD

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

properties.tract_name: The town-center of Woodlawn

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD

Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Northwest Gateways community seeks to enhance its overall economic vitality, neighborhood livability, and environmental health by pursuing a vision of improved streetscapes, commercial corridor revitalization, and diverse housing options. By leveraging sustainable community programs and targeted public investments, the area strives to foster commercial growth, address transportation and pedestrian connectivity gaps, and build active, safe, and attractive neighborhoods where families of all backgrounds can thrive.

quotes.text: There is currently an affordable housing proposal within the Pikesville CRD that is requesting rezoning to support multi-family apartments.
quotes.briefing_quote: In the Pikesville Commercial Revitalization District, there is an affordable housing proposal requesting rezoning to support multi-family apartments, showing local momentum for adding density.

quotes.text: There has not been demolition of blighted properties in the area. However, there is an interest from the County to assemble vacant commercial properties on Liberty Rd to assist CDCs in redevelopment. In addition, there is discussion to redevelop the old International House of Pancakes and Bennigan's restaurants located in front of Security Square mall.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county is looking to assemble vacant commercial properties along Liberty Road to assist community development corporations in redevelopment, with further discussions centered on redeveloping the former restaurant sites in front of Security Square Mall.

quotes.text: Expand full spectrum housing for residents at diverse income levels and life stages and for individuals with disabilities by encouraging high quality mixed income, multigenerational developments. Promote Housing Accessibility Modification programs to make housing more accessible. Continue to implement smart growth policies by supporting mixed-use development and Traditional Neighborhood Development in the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning guidelines emphasize the need to encourage high-quality mixed-income, multigenerational developments while supporting smart growth policies such as mixed-use and Traditional Neighborhood Development.

quotes.text: Some homes in Colonial Village have been improved. There are homes in the Pikesville area that have gone through the zoning petition process for additions. This is largely attributed to growing families that require additional space and secondary kitchens due to religious food preparation requirements.
quotes.briefing_quote: In Pikesville, growing families are actively seeking zoning petitions for home additions and secondary kitchens to meet specific cultural and religious food preparation needs.

quotes.text: Lack of quality retail and chain restaurants in the Liberty Rd CRD... Lack of variety of businesses to meet the needs of the community... Abundance of unwanted businesses... Businesses closing and vacant gas stations are an eyesore to the residents
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback highlights a lack of quality retail and restaurant variety along the Liberty Road Commercial Revitalization District, alongside concerns over vacant storefronts and gas stations.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Cumberland aspires to revitalize its urban core by leveraging historic assets, enhancing natural resources like the Great Allegheny Passage, and expanding high-quality housing and economic opportunities. Through collaborative public-private partnerships, the city focuses on eliminating residential blight, upgrading infrastructure, and supporting diverse workforce training to establish a vibrant, supportive environment for both families and profitable businesses.

quotes.text: The city has partnered with developers from outside our area to begin infill housing in the shape of single-family units and multi-unit buildings that will address the needs of low to moderate income families.
quotes.briefing_quote: To expand local housing options, municipal planners reported that 'the city has partnered with developers from outside our area to begin infill housing in the shape of single-family units and multi-unit buildings that will address the needs of low to moderate income families.'

quotes.text: Improvements to upper story buildings downtown for residential and commercial use, the creation of a residential unit while increasing mixed-use business below in the central business district
quotes.briefing_quote: Detailing downtown redevelopment successes, the plan highlights 'improvements to upper-story buildings downtown for residential and commercial use, the creation of a residential unit while increasing mixed-use business below in the central business district.'

quotes.text: The city lost an estimated 1,217 single-family, owner-occupied units. At the same time, there was an increase in the number of single-family rentals in the city, which at least partially reflects that shift in tenure from owner-occupied to renter-occupied units.
quotes.briefing_quote: Analyzing shifting housing patterns, the document notes that 'the city lost an estimated 1,217 single-family, owner-occupied units' alongside a corresponding rise in single-family rental conversions.

quotes.text: This investment in Cumberland's main business district will foster growth of new businesses and provide an opportunity for the existing businesses to capitalize on a refreshed downtown.
quotes.briefing_quote: Describing the goals of the Baltimore Street Revitalization Project, organizers emphasized that 'this investment in Cumberland's main business district will foster growth of new businesses and provide an opportunity for the existing businesses to capitalize on a refreshed downtown.'

quotes.text: The city has a demand for market-rate housing but, unfortunately, we cannot compete with neighboring markets in terms of ROI. Grants that help offset costs or incentivize market-rate housing would be very beneficial in stabilizing our housing market, thus lessening the need for such incentives.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing barriers to housing development, city staff highlighted that 'the city has a demand for market-rate housing but, unfortunately, we cannot compete with neighboring markets in terms of ROI,' indicating a strong need for offsetting development grants.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of La Plata aims to expand its Sustainable Community boundary to 192 acres to encompass and revitalize its downtown core. The vision focuses on transforming the downtown into a walkable, pedestrian-friendly environment with enhanced streetscapes, stronger transit connections, and vibrant mixed-use developments, while relocating heavy industrial uses and anchoring the center with a relocated county library.

305 Queen Anne Street, La Plata, MD

quotes.text: The Neighborhood Commercial Mixed-Use (NCX) Zone was drafted as part of the Town's Comprehensive zoning code review. The adoption of the updated zoning is planned to be in Spring of 2018. This Zone will be applied to areas, some of which may be in the downtown core if determined by the Town Council or as part of the Comprehensive plan update.
quotes.briefing_quote: To incentivize downtown redevelopment, the Town drafted a new "Neighborhood Commercial Mixed-Use (NCX) Zone as part of its Comprehensive zoning code review" to facilitate flexible, growth-oriented zoning.

quotes.text: Strategy B: support mixed-use and Traditional Neighborhood communities and mixed-use Live/Work buildings in the downtown and the TND village center
quotes.briefing_quote: The Town of La Plata seeks to address housing variety by acting to "support mixed-use and Traditional Neighborhood communities and mixed-use Live/Work buildings" in the downtown core.

quotes.text: Strategy E: Promote an attached townhouse product and live/work units amongst home builders, developers, and consumers
quotes.briefing_quote: To diversify local housing options, municipal strategies focus on efforts to "promote an attached townhouse product and live/work units amongst home builders, developers, and consumers."

quotes.text: Strategy D: Foster more restaurant and boutique retail, complementary with existing retail, as new housing is built and more residents move into the town center
quotes.briefing_quote: The Plan recommends that the Town "foster more restaurant and boutique retail, complementary with existing retail" as residential infill progresses in the downtown.

quotes.text: Vehicular congestion, fragmented ownership, and lack of relocation and redevelopment readiness for two significant industrial properties hinder redevelopment prospects.
quotes.briefing_quote: While local planning challenges include "fragmented ownership and lack of relocation readiness for two significant industrial properties," these operational downtown parcels represent a substantial future redevelopment opportunity.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of La Plata seeks to strengthen its downtown core, preserve its historic small-town character, and ensure that new development areas are built on principles of walkability, sustainability, and environmental protection. The town aims to foster flexible planning to support its health care anchor institutions, encourage a more diverse housing stock, and expand its tax base through mixed-use and commercial infill development.
geographic_addresses: Crain Highway & Charles Street, La Plata, MD
MD 225 & Crain Highway, La Plata, MD
Washington Avenue & Baltimore Street, La Plata, MD
Rosewick Road & Crain Highway, La Plata, MD

quotes.text: Create developments with more density to differentiate the downtown from the residential neighborhoods throughout the rest of La Plata.
quotes.briefing_quote: A National Trust for Historic Preservation assessment suggested that the town "create developments with more density to differentiate the downtown from the residential neighborhoods throughout the rest of La Plata."

quotes.text: Rezone parcels to allow for mixed-use redevelopment to move forward.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Urban Land Institute Technical Assistance Panel recommended that the town "rezone parcels to allow for mixed-use redevelopment to move forward" in the downtown area.

quotes.text: Encourage the use of accessory dwelling units (ADUs) as defined in the Zoning Ordinance; this will allow development of ADUs in association with single family detached homes. These will help provide affordable housing options for low to moderate income workers, seniors, and recent college graduates as recommended in the 2009 Comprehensive Plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights an opportunity to "encourage the use of accessory dwelling units (ADUs) in association with single family detached homes" to provide affordable housing options for seniors and young graduates.

quotes.text: The Town should support development proposals and programs that integrate various populations in order to successfully implement mixed-use development in and around the Downtown Core.
quotes.briefing_quote: To build a vibrant and inclusive community, the plan notes that "the Town should support development proposals and programs that integrate various populations in order to successfully implement mixed-use development in and around the Downtown Core."

quotes.text: Ensure that zoning definitions include the concepts of "micro-manufacturing" and "makerspaces" to be permitted in commercial and mixed-use areas. The Town should recognize that a rapidly changing economy does not neatly classify such business opportunities and that their integration into commercial and mixed-use areas brings investment and vitality to targeted sites.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan encourages modern commercial uses, stating the Town should "ensure that zoning definitions include the concepts of micro-manufacturing and makerspaces to be permitted in commercial and mixed-use areas."

quotes.text: There is a lack of diversity in the town’s existing housing stock; having only few multifamily properties makes it difficult to attract younger residents who don’t have a need for large properties but may otherwise have a desire to live in town.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the need for diverse housing options, the plan notes that "having only few multifamily properties makes it difficult to attract younger residents who do not have a need for large properties."

quotes.text: The WURC area consists largely of small and narrowly shaped lots, which has posed a challenge to redevelopment. Parcel acquisition/consolidation is needed.

quotes.text: The downtown-style development planned for the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) and Greenberg Gibbons development has not yet occurred, mainly because these are long term projects that take several years to come to fruition: In addition, there have been several obstacles to creating a downtown in the WURC corridor; including fractured property ownership, inadequate infrastructure, and general lack in investment of the type to spur redevelopment:

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD
Cowenton Avenue & Pulaski Highway, White Marsh, MD
Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The community's vision is to enhance and revitalize the Reisterstown Main Street corridor by preserving its historic character, expanding its public green spaces and trail networks—such as Woodley Avenue Park and the Franklin Woodland Trails—and promoting economic vitality through commercial facade improvements, diverse retail offerings, and vibrant community events, while simultaneously improving pedestrian safety and complete streets connectivity.
geographic_addresses: Woodley Ave, Reisterstown, MD
202 Main Street, Reisterstown, MD
350 Main Street, Reisterstown, MD
Bond Ave & Main St, Reisterstown, MD
Chartley & Main St, Reisterstown, MD

quotes.text: The residential communities within and surrounding the SC Area are predominantly lower density communities with only some mid-rise residential communities. Further diversifying the kinds of housing available could further contribute to increasing the success and vitality of Main Street.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning document emphasizes that further diversifying the kinds of housing available within the surrounding lower-density communities could significantly contribute to increasing the success and vitality of Main Street.

quotes.text: Opportunities for artist and/or live where you work apartments along Main St. Existing apartments over retail establishments are present, but some require renovation.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup members identified significant opportunities to develop artist and live-work apartments along Main Street, noting that existing apartments over retail establishments represent a strong foundation but require thoughtful renovation.

quotes.text: County zoning regulations and codes require updating to reflect the County's current realities and needs. Barriers to higher density development, including zoning and community opposition.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning document highlights the opportunity to update county zoning regulations to better address barriers to higher-density development and align land-use policies with current community realities.

quotes.text: The northern portion of the SC Area does lend itself to infill development opportunities due to the presence of aging strip malls in the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners pointed out that aging strip malls in the northern portion of the Sustainable Community Area present excellent opportunities for supportive infill development.

quotes.text: Identify opportunities for appropriate changes in current zoning to allow for the incorporation of additional residential units into existing residential structures and areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: To expand options, the Action Plan suggests identifying appropriate changes in current zoning to allow additional residential units within existing residential and mixed-use structures.

This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

community_organizations: Set the Captives Free Outreach, Worship and Education (OWE) Center

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Northwest Gateways community seeks to enhance its overall economic vitality, neighborhood livability, and environmental health by pursuing a vision of improved streetscapes, commercial corridor revitalization, and diverse housing options. By leveraging sustainable community programs and targeted public investments, the area strives to foster commercial growth, address transportation and pedestrian connectivity gaps, and build active, safe, and attractive neighborhoods where families of all backgrounds can thrive.

quotes.text: There is currently an affordable housing proposal within the Pikesville CRD that is requesting rezoning to support multi-family apartments.
quotes.briefing_quote: In the Pikesville Commercial Revitalization District, there is an affordable housing proposal requesting rezoning to support multi-family apartments, showing local momentum for adding density.

quotes.text: There has not been demolition of blighted properties in the area. However, there is an interest from the County to assemble vacant commercial properties on Liberty Rd to assist CDCs in redevelopment. In addition, there is discussion to redevelop the old International House of Pancakes and Bennigan's restaurants located in front of Security Square mall.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county is looking to assemble vacant commercial properties along Liberty Road to assist community development corporations in redevelopment, with further discussions centered on redeveloping the former restaurant sites in front of Security Square Mall.

quotes.text: Expand full spectrum housing for residents at diverse income levels and life stages and for individuals with disabilities by encouraging high quality mixed income, multigenerational developments. Promote Housing Accessibility Modification programs to make housing more accessible. Continue to implement smart growth policies by supporting mixed-use development and Traditional Neighborhood Development in the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning guidelines emphasize the need to encourage high-quality mixed-income, multigenerational developments while supporting smart growth policies such as mixed-use and Traditional Neighborhood Development.

quotes.text: Some homes in Colonial Village have been improved. There are homes in the Pikesville area that have gone through the zoning petition process for additions. This is largely attributed to growing families that require additional space and secondary kitchens due to religious food preparation requirements.
quotes.briefing_quote: In Pikesville, growing families are actively seeking zoning petitions for home additions and secondary kitchens to meet specific cultural and religious food preparation needs.

quotes.text: Lack of quality retail and chain restaurants in the Liberty Rd CRD... Lack of variety of businesses to meet the needs of the community... Abundance of unwanted businesses... Businesses closing and vacant gas stations are an eyesore to the residents
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback highlights a lack of quality retail and restaurant variety along the Liberty Road Commercial Revitalization District, alongside concerns over vacant storefronts and gas stations.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

community_organizations: Arts & Humanities Council of Montgomery County
