plan_quotes.community_vision: Somerset County envisions a steady, managed trajectory of slow economic and population growth through the year 2010. The community seeks to transition from its traditional, declining resource-based agriculture and fishing economy toward a diversified mix of services, light manufacturing, tourism, and aquaculture. This growth is directed away from valuable farmland and sensitive environments, concentrating instead within designated primary growth corridors and community nodes served by central water and sewer systems to maintain the county's rural character, preserve historical resources, and protect the Chesapeake Bay.
geographic_addresses: US Route 13 & MD Route 413, Westover, MD
MD Route 362 & US Route 13, Princess Anne, MD
MD Route 362 & Crisfield Lane, Princess Anne, MD
1801 Princess Anne, Princess Anne, MD

quotes.text: Somerset should begin to encourage townhouses, patio homes and other more affordable types in order to compete with surrounding communities to retain population and tax base. This would introduce a greater proportion of housing at densities of between 5 and 10 DU per acre, thereby conserving land, bringing people closer to village centers and permitting easier access to a concentration of community facilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To improve housing variety and retain younger residents, the 1996 Plan suggests that Somerset 'begin to encourage townhouses, patio homes and other more affordable types in order to compete with surrounding communities,' aiming to achieve housing densities of between 5 and 10 dwelling units per acre.

quotes.text: Higher residential densities in the form of density bonuses should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, where a high quality central water and sewer system is planned.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning narrative notes that 'higher residential densities in the form of density bonuses should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, where a high quality central water and sewer system is planned' to support sustainable infrastructure.

quotes.text: Strict controls should be placed on the subdivision of farms and the spread of strip residential uses along country roads by limiting development in the 'A' zone to minor subdivisions (no more than six lots).
quotes.briefing_quote: To combat unplanned sprawl on rural roadways, the plan outlines that 'strict controls should be placed on the subdivision of farms and the spread of strip residential uses along country roads by limiting development in the agricultural zone to minor subdivisions.'

quotes.text: Planned Unit Developments (PUDs) should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, with a range of community facilities consistent with the development's needs and the location, size and other criteria typically required by the County. In particular, communities with a broad mix of activities, including residential, commercial, employment and recreation should be preferred...
quotes.briefing_quote: Focusing on innovative layout designs, the plan asserts that 'Planned Unit Developments should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, with a range of community facilities consistent with the development's needs.'

quotes.text: Industrial and commercial development should be encouraged to cluster in office parks and employment centers within the Primary Growth Areas as indicated on the Land Use Plan Map (Map 4) They should be well landscaped, buffered from nearby residential areas and should take positive measures to protect sensitive environmental resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: To balance commercial expansion with environmental protection, the plan recommends that 'industrial and commercial development should be encouraged to cluster in office parks and employment centers within the Primary Growth Areas' to safeguard natural resources.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Fruitland aims to leverage its steady population growth and strategic location along the U.S. Route 13 corridor to drive economic revitalization and enhance the overall quality of life for its residents. Through the designation of its Sustainable Community Area, Fruitland aspires to transform its historically quiet downtown into a vibrant hub of economic activity using mixed-use development, commercial infill, and housing diversification (including multi-family and affordable options). Concurrently, the city plans to resolve infrastructure and pedestrian safety challenges, expanding sidewalk connectivity, park spaces, and community health services to foster a more connected and resilient community.
geographic_addresses: 401 E. Main Street, Fruitland, MD
U.S. Route 13 & Main Street, Fruitland, MD
Camden Avenue & Main Street, Fruitland, MD

quotes.text: Continue to promote mixed-use projects in the downtown that combine residential with commercial and institutional uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize the core business district, economic strategies highlight the need to "continue to promote mixed-use projects in the downtown that combine residential with commercial and institutional uses."

quotes.text: Explore zoning changes so that multi-family residences can be permitted in appropriate areas
quotes.briefing_quote: To expand housing opportunities for a diverse population, planners recommend that the city "explore zoning changes so that multi-family residences can be permitted in appropriate areas."

quotes.text: Promote the development and redevelopment of commercial and industrial activities along U.S. Route 13.
quotes.briefing_quote: To capture regional economic activity, the plan proposes to "promote the development and redevelopment of commercial and industrial activities along U.S. Route 13."

quotes.text: Rejuvenate older neighborhoods by renovating homes and building attractive new homes to replace deteriorating structures on infill sites.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support housing quality, city guidelines suggest effort to "rejuvenate older neighborhoods by renovating homes and building attractive new homes to replace deteriorating structures on infill sites."

quotes.text: Create an affordable housing trust fund [akin to a Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT)] that can be used to provide incentives for the benefit of the City.
quotes.briefing_quote: To systematically incentivize affordable residential options, the community recommends the city "create an affordable housing trust fund [akin to a Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT)] that can be used to provide incentives for the benefit of the City."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Salisbury is committed to fostering a vibrant, sustainable, and inclusive community by concentrating growth in its urban core, expanding bicycle and pedestrian network infrastructure, and improving water quality. Through proactive municipal programs like the 'Here is Home' initiative, the City seeks to expand and diversify its housing stock, encourage mixed-use vertical development downtown, and create robust support systems for chronically homeless populations, while strengthening local arts, business, and educational opportunities.

quotes.text: The Ross is a redevelopment of 3 existing parcels on W. Main St. in Downtown. The two buildings will consist of 100 apartments and commercial space
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting downtown growth potential, planning documents track 'The Ross,' which is a 'redevelopment of 3 existing parcels on West Main Street in Downtown' consisting of 100 apartments and commercial space.

quotes.text: Selling city-owned properties to developers in order to create mixed-use development
quotes.briefing_quote: To catalyze revitalization, the City has utilized the strength of 'selling city-owned properties to developers in order to create mixed-use development' in the urban core.

quotes.text: Lack of concentration of high-end housing in the urban core
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes a 'lack of concentration of high-end housing in the urban core' as a current weakness, signaling a target opportunity for upscale multi-family projects.

quotes.text: Low return on investment for vertical development
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analyses identified a 'low return on investment for vertical development' as a weakness, suggesting that developers may require targeted local incentives or partnerships to make mid-rise projects viable.

quotes.briefing_quote: To aggressively expand supply, the City instituted the 'Here is Home fee reimbursement program to encourage new housing options within the Sustainable Community Area,' generating entries for over 8,000 potential units.

The village-centers of Sharptown and Mardela Springs

plan_quotes.community_vision: Mardela Springs aspires to preserve its cherished rural, close-knit, and single-family residential character while proactively addressing critical environmental, infrastructure, and redevelopment needs. Key priorities include upgrading deteriorated sidewalks, addressing failing septic systems through a centralized wastewater initiative, and demolishing derelict structures to clear the way for compatible infill development. Economically, the community aims to revitalize existing properties and cluster commercial development near Route 50, ensuring any new growth maintains a pedestrian-friendly, human-scale village atmosphere.
geographic_addresses: 201 Station St., Mardela Springs, MD
Bratten Street & Main Street, Mardela Springs, MD

quotes.text: Preserve the predominant single-family character of the Town
quotes.briefing_quote: To maintain its existing neighborhood context, the community aims to "preserve the predominant single-family character of the Town."

quotes.text: Allow limited residential use in commercial area
quotes.briefing_quote: As a means to encourage improved design and property revitalization, the plan suggests to "allow limited residential use in commercial areas."

quotes.text: Focus on infill development (medium density residential) as well as redevelopment
quotes.briefing_quote: To prevent sprawl and make efficient use of land, the Town seeks to "focus on infill development (medium density residential) as well as redevelopment."

quotes.text: Prohibit commercial strip development and focus on clustered economic development - Restrict retail development to primarily neighborhood-serving character
quotes.briefing_quote: The economic development strategies outline a preference to "prohibit commercial strip development and focus on clustered economic development" while restricting retail to a neighborhood-serving scale.

quotes.text: Focus development on highway commercial areas directly adjacent to Route 50, direct access points to Route 50 should be discouraged
quotes.briefing_quote: For regional business attraction, the plan advises to "focus development on highway commercial areas directly adjacent to Route 50" while discouraging direct access points to manage traffic safety.

community_organizations: Mardela Springs Volunteer Fire Department Ladies Auxiliary

plan_quotes.community_vision: Sharptown is a close-knit, family-oriented, rural "bedroom" community that seeks to preserve its small-town character, scenic riverfront along the Nanticoke River, and rich historic heritage while proactively addressing critical water and sewer infrastructure needs. The community envisions managed smart growth by prioritizing infill development, transforming the vacant former elementary school into a vibrant multi-purpose community center, establishing housing rehabilitation programs, and attracting service-oriented businesses to improve local quality of life.
geographic_addresses: 401 Main Street, Sharptown, MD
Ferry Street, Sharptown, MD
Nanticoke Street & Corporation Road, Sharptown, MD
State Street & Taylor Street, Sharptown, MD
Church Street & Railway Street, Sharptown, MD
Railway Street & School Street, Sharptown, MD

quotes.text: Sharptown has an aging population that will require increased affordable housing options, such as 55 and older residential developments, for aging in place opportunities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support its changing demographics, local leaders note that the town's shifting population will require the development of "increased affordable housing options, such as 55 and older residential developments, for aging in place opportunities."

quotes.text: The town does not have many large parcels available for infill development. New larger-scale developments will likely occur through annexation. There have been three single-family homes constructed on infill lots within the Sustainable Communities boundary.
quotes.briefing_quote: While major expansion may require future annexation due to parcel limitations, the town successfully accommodated "three single-family homes constructed on infill lots within the Sustainable Communities boundary" to support incremental growth.

quotes.text: Sharptown is a small bedroom community which lacks a traditional downtown or main street commercial district. The only new business is the Dollar General constructed in 2018. Although just outside of the Town’s Sustainable Communities boundary, Dollar General serves the entire community as it is within walking distance for most residents. Dollar General provides groceries, healthy food options, and household items for area residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: Despite lacking a traditional main street district, a newly established retailer has proven highly beneficial because it "serves the entire community as it is within walking distance for most residents," filling a critical gap in local food options.

quotes.text: Promote mixed uses and offices to increase service-based business for convenience and job growth
quotes.briefing_quote: To build a resilient local economy, the community action plan advocates for policies that "promote mixed uses and offices to increase service-based business for convenience and job growth" while preserving small-town character.

quotes.text: The most prevalent housing issue in Sharptown is blighted housing which the town plans to begin to address with a request for State Revitalization Funds to initiate a local façade improvement program.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planners identified that the primary domestic concern is physical deterioration, emphasizing an opportunity to utilize state funding to "initiate a local façade improvement program" and upgrade older residential exteriors.

quotes.text: There is a lack of affordable and workforce housing opportunities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a core developmental gap for younger families and local workers, stating that "there is a lack of affordable and workforce housing opportunities" within the existing housing inventory.

properties.tract_name: The village-centers of Pittsville and Willards

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Willards envisions revitalizing its historic core as a walkable, vibrant "bedroom" community while retaining its quiet, small-town character and agricultural heritage. By focusing on smart growth, infill development, and mixed-use projects, the town seeks to address its lack of housing diversity—particularly the need for workforce and senior housing—and to attract compatible commercial enterprises to Main Street without expanding its boundaries through annexation.
geographic_addresses: 7344 Main Street, Willards, MD
Market Street & Main Street, Willards, MD
Main Street & Old Ocean City Road, Willards, MD

quotes.text: Lack of housing diversity, such as apartments, duplexes, and townhomes. Willards has an aging population and will require increased affordable housing options, in particular 55 and older residential developments.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a "lack of housing diversity, such as apartments, duplexes, and townhomes," noting that an aging population will require expanded options, particularly 55 and older developments.

quotes.text: Establish development standards and guidance for planned mixed-use development that comply with the Town's development design objectives.
quotes.briefing_quote: To guide sustainable growth, the community recommends that local officials "establish development standards and guidance for planned mixed-use development" that comply with the town's design objectives.

quotes.text: Expand commercial activity along Main Street (State Hwy 354) with a focus on infill and redevelopment.
quotes.briefing_quote: The action plan aims to "expand commercial activity along Main Street (State Hwy 354) with a focus on infill and redevelopment" to establish a cohesive center.

quotes.text: Waive or reduce fees and infrastructure requirements to facilitate the construction and renovation of affordable housing. Work with Wicomico County to develop and promote employer assisted housing programs. Ensure that regulatory policies align with affordable housing goals. Utilize inclusionary zoning to require a portion of any new development to include a certain amount of affordable housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To foster workforce housing, the town outlines strategies to "waive or reduce fees and infrastructure requirements to facilitate the construction and renovation of affordable housing" and utilize inclusionary zoning.

quotes.text: Attract a developer and tenant to provide fresh and local foods. Allocate funds to perform independent market studies of proposed grocery retail development. Conduct a market study and analyze the competitiveness of a grocer with the recent opening of the new Dollar General.
quotes.briefing_quote: The town desires to "attract a developer and tenant to provide fresh and local foods" and plans to analyze local market dynamics following a recent retail opening.

community_organizations: Town Council for the Town of Willards

plan_quotes.community_vision: Pittsville aspires to preserve its strong rural heritage and small-town character while selectively promoting infill development and diversifying its housing options. By revitalizing its Town Center, establishing a designated Central Business District, and improving utility and pedestrian infrastructure, the Town aims to foster a sustainable, walkable, and vibrant community that supports both multi-generational residents and local businesses.
geographic_addresses: 7505 Pittsville-Gumboro Road, Pittsville, MD

Railroad Avenue & Main Street, Pittsville, MD

quotes.text: Diversification of housing supply beyond single-family residential. Progress Measures: Increased proportion of medium-high density housing options, including duplex, townhouse, multi-family, and cottage units
quotes.briefing_quote: With an eye toward modernizing the local residential landscape, the plan focuses on the diversification of housing supply beyond single-family residential, targeting an "increased proportion of medium-high density housing options, including duplex, townhouse, multi-family, and cottage units."

quotes.text: Adopt infill and redevelopment overlay zone permitting mix-use in Central Business District and Central Residential District
quotes.briefing_quote: To activate underutilized properties, the community intends to adopt an infill and redevelopment overlay zone permitting mixed-use within both the Central Business District and the Central Residential District.

quotes.text: Incentivize commercial infill and redevelopment opportunities and promote new commercial uses in the Town Center, such as a medical or dental practice and a grocery store or fresh foods market
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing gaps in local services, stakeholders recommend to incentivize commercial infill and redevelopment opportunities to attract vital "commercial uses in the Town Center, such as a medical or dental practice and a grocery store or fresh foods market."

quotes.text: Designate a Central Business District to prioritize the development of commercial uses in that district
quotes.briefing_quote: In order to foster local business activity and establish a true sense of place, the Town plans to designate a Central Business District to prioritize the development of commercial uses.

quotes.text: Work with developers to facilitate the construction of housing developments for residents aged 55 years or older
quotes.briefing_quote: To support its aging population, local leaders plan to work with developers to facilitate the construction of housing developments tailored specifically for residents aged 55 years or older.

quotes.text: Seek funding to develop a façade improvement program
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize the appearance of older structures, the plan suggests to seek funding to develop a façade improvement program targeting both historical homes and commercial structures.

community_organizations: Salisbury University’s Business Economic and Community Outreach Network

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Langley Park envisions transitioning into a vibrant, transit-oriented gateway that leverages the construction of the Purple Line light rail while preserving its naturally occurring affordable housing and rich cultural diversity. The community seeks to revitalize its commercial districts—especially the International Corridor—through denser, mixed-use development, streetscape beautification, and creative placemaking. Addressing persistent infrastructure and social challenges, the plan aims to improve pedestrian and bicycle safety, modernize aging multifamily rental housing, preserve environmental assets like the Northwest Branch Trail, and elevate the quality of life through enhanced health, language, and youth recreation services.

quotes.text: Support TOD and denser mixed-use development in coordination with the construction of the Purple Line to provide denser retail typologies different from the existing strip retail centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: To leverage incoming transit investments, the plan recommends that developers 'support TOD [Transit-Oriented Development] and denser mixed-use development in coordination with the construction of the Purple Line to provide denser retail typologies different from the existing strip retail centers.'

quotes.text: The housing stock is predominantly aging multi-family apartment units. Most of these units were built in the 1950s, when lead paint and asbestos were used in housing construction. Many of these units have not been substantially upgraded.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community highlights a critical need for modernization, noting that the local 'housing stock is predominantly aging multi-family apartment units' constructed in the 1950s, which creates a prime opportunity to substantially upgrade and improve multifamily conditions.

quotes.text: Increase the number of affordable rental housing units that include 3 and 4 bedrooms to accommodate larger families and prevent overcrowding.
quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate local household structures, community leaders identify a pressing need to 'increase the number of affordable rental housing units that include 3 and 4 bedrooms to accommodate larger families and prevent overcrowding.'

quotes.text: In 2021, the Prince George’s County Planning Department completed the Takoma/Langley Crossroads Planning and Implementation Study, which builds on the 2019 Approved Takoma Langley Sector Plan by developing implementation tools and strategies to support denser, mixed use and walkable development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning frameworks support forward-looking projects, specifically 'developing implementation tools and strategies to support denser, mixed use and walkable development' around key transit nodes.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

community_organizations: Set the Captives Free Outreach, Worship and Education (OWE) Center

plan_quotes.community_vision: Hampstead aspires to maintain its distinctive small-town charm, safe and family-oriented environment, and rich heritage while actively fostering smart growth and downtown revitalization. By capitalizing on recent major Main Street infrastructure improvements, the Town seeks to eliminate commercial vacancies, encourage adaptive reuse of historic buildings, and introduce a diverse mix of affordable housing options—such as townhomes, single-family starter homes, and senior housing—to accommodate both young families and elderly residents.
geographic_addresses: 1034 S. Carroll Street, Hampstead, MD
Houcksville Road & Main Street, Hampstead, MD
Route 482 & Main Street, Hampstead, MD
Houck Avenue & Main Street, Hampstead, MD
Willow Street & Main Street, Hampstead, MD

quotes.text: Make properties in the downtown district more desirable with the creation of a mixed use overlay zone. This would allow a mixture of residential and commercial use within the same structure.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize the downtown commercial corridor, planning workshops recommended efforts to "make properties in the downtown district more desirable with the creation of a mixed use overlay zone" to allow a dynamic blend of residential and commercial uses within the same building structure.

quotes.text: On the residential side, the Town and the Developers of the Hampstead Overlook project will soon enter the final plan stage for the development. This Planned Unit Development will bring a mix of townhomes and single-family homes to the area which will be attractive and affordable for younger buyers.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting a major opportunity for residential development, the plan notes that a upcoming "Planned Unit Development will bring a mix of townhomes and single-family homes to the area which will be attractive and affordable for younger buyers."

quotes.text: Due to unexpected costs associated with infrastructure improvements necessary for industrial use, the owners of the property filed for a zoning change to R-7,500 Residential. The Town Council approved the request and the property was rezoned in 2016. The property, now known as Hampstead Overlook, is in the planning stages to be developed as a Planned Unit Development. The community would consist of 255 homes, a mix of single family and townhomes, which would be more affordable choices than what is currently available in Hampstead.
quotes.briefing_quote: Following a successful rezoning initiative at the former Florida Rock industrial site, the Town is paving the way for a neighborhood that "would consist of 255 homes, a mix of single family and townhomes, which would be more affordable choices than what is currently available in Hampstead."

quotes.text: Create additional, more affordable private sector housing opportunities for young and elderly residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing shifts in local demographics, community planners emphasized the need to "create additional, more affordable private sector housing opportunities for young and elderly residents" to support both starter homebuyers and seniors wishing to age in place.

quotes.text: Reduce the number of store front vacancies and broaden and diversify the Town’s business, service and residential base.
quotes.briefing_quote: To build on recent streetscape improvements, the Town aims to "reduce the number of store front vacancies and broaden and diversify the Town’s business, service and residential base" by creating a supportive environment for new investments.

quotes.text: Adaptive Reuse of Vacant Buildings. ... Work with the property owners to examine reuse possibilities for the building and the land.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes "adaptive reuse of vacant buildings" and calls on stakeholders to partner with property owners and developers to find modern, viable uses for underutilized downtown properties.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Hampstead is committed to remaining a quintessential American small town in name and character. While primarily a residential community with quiet, well-maintained neighborhoods, the town aims to nurture a thriving, walkable historic downtown core with small-scale businesses. Heavier commercial activities are clustered at the northern and southern nodes, and industrial development is buffered and concentrated in designated zones to maintain economic stability without compromising the town's family-friendly and historic aesthetic.

Shiloh Avenue & Main Street, Hampstead, MD
Houcksville Road & Main Street, Hampstead, MD

quotes.text: The era of large-scale residential growth is largely over.
quotes.briefing_quote: Hampstead Mayor Haven N. Shoemaker, Jr. noted that the "era of large-scale residential growth is largely over," shifting local focus toward strategic infill and infrastructure balancing rather than expansive new subdivisions.

quotes.text: New development and redevelopment of land should be encouraged to incorporate a complementary mix of uses where residential and business uses are combined within a building or within a site.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community workshop participants suggested that "new development and redevelopment of land should be encouraged to incorporate a complementary mix of uses" where residential and business opportunities are combined directly within a building or site.

quotes.text: Where economically feasible, multi-story development and redevelopment should be encouraged to conserve land while recognizing and complementing the Town’s historic character.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planners and stakeholders emphasized that "where economically feasible, multi-story development and redevelopment should be encouraged to conserve land" while respecting and enhancing the historic fabric of the town.

quotes.text: Most of the area within the Town limits currently zoned R-20,000 is recommended for rezoning to R-40,000 and a change to the Residential 'R-40,000' land-use designation. This is because these lots will be served by private septic. It is the Town’s position, and the preference of the Carroll County Health Department, that residential lots served by private septic be at least 40,000 square feet to allow for adequate septic replacement areas and reasonable areas for the dwelling and accessory uses.
quotes.briefing_quote: The comprehensive plan notes that to protect environmental health, "residential lots served by private septic must be at least 40,000 square feet" to allow for sufficient replacement areas, leading to recommendations for lower-density designations on specific unsewered tracts.

quotes.text: To restrict downtown commercial development to businesses that are small in size and scale and that enhance family values and small-town atmosphere.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community expressed a strong desire to "restrict downtown commercial development to businesses that are small in size and scale" to protect the area's native small-town atmosphere and family-centric values.

quotes.text: The R-O District provides areas for residential uses and professional and administrative offices that preserve and enhance the residential character of the area involved. The R-B District provides the opportunity for low-intensity commercial development that is consistent with the general character of a residential neighborhood.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support neighborhood-scale integration, the plan explains that the Residential Business District "provides the opportunity for low-intensity commercial development that is consistent with the general character of a residential neighborhood."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Somerset County envisions a steady, managed trajectory of slow economic and population growth through the year 2010. The community seeks to transition from its traditional, declining resource-based agriculture and fishing economy toward a diversified mix of services, light manufacturing, tourism, and aquaculture. This growth is directed away from valuable farmland and sensitive environments, concentrating instead within designated primary growth corridors and community nodes served by central water and sewer systems to maintain the county's rural character, preserve historical resources, and protect the Chesapeake Bay.
geographic_addresses: US Route 13 & MD Route 413, Westover, MD
MD Route 362 & US Route 13, Princess Anne, MD
MD Route 362 & Crisfield Lane, Princess Anne, MD
1801 Princess Anne, Princess Anne, MD

quotes.text: Somerset should begin to encourage townhouses, patio homes and other more affordable types in order to compete with surrounding communities to retain population and tax base. This would introduce a greater proportion of housing at densities of between 5 and 10 DU per acre, thereby conserving land, bringing people closer to village centers and permitting easier access to a concentration of community facilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To improve housing variety and retain younger residents, the 1996 Plan suggests that Somerset 'begin to encourage townhouses, patio homes and other more affordable types in order to compete with surrounding communities,' aiming to achieve housing densities of between 5 and 10 dwelling units per acre.

quotes.text: Higher residential densities in the form of density bonuses should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, where a high quality central water and sewer system is planned.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning narrative notes that 'higher residential densities in the form of density bonuses should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, where a high quality central water and sewer system is planned' to support sustainable infrastructure.

quotes.text: Strict controls should be placed on the subdivision of farms and the spread of strip residential uses along country roads by limiting development in the 'A' zone to minor subdivisions (no more than six lots).
quotes.briefing_quote: To combat unplanned sprawl on rural roadways, the plan outlines that 'strict controls should be placed on the subdivision of farms and the spread of strip residential uses along country roads by limiting development in the agricultural zone to minor subdivisions.'

quotes.text: Planned Unit Developments (PUDs) should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, with a range of community facilities consistent with the development's needs and the location, size and other criteria typically required by the County. In particular, communities with a broad mix of activities, including residential, commercial, employment and recreation should be preferred...
quotes.briefing_quote: Focusing on innovative layout designs, the plan asserts that 'Planned Unit Developments should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, with a range of community facilities consistent with the development's needs.'

quotes.text: Industrial and commercial development should be encouraged to cluster in office parks and employment centers within the Primary Growth Areas as indicated on the Land Use Plan Map (Map 4) They should be well landscaped, buffered from nearby residential areas and should take positive measures to protect sensitive environmental resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: To balance commercial expansion with environmental protection, the plan recommends that 'industrial and commercial development should be encouraged to cluster in office parks and employment centers within the Primary Growth Areas' to safeguard natural resources.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Princess Anne aspires to foster sustainable economic growth and enhance community vibrancy by leveraging its unique historic assets, scenic location, and strong 'Town and Gown' partnership with the University of Maryland Eastern Shore. The community seeks to revitalize its downtown core through mixed-use development, commercial façade and interior building improvements, and infrastructure modernization. By expanding recreational trails, improving environmental buffers along the Manokin River, and promoting homeownership, Princess Anne aims to cultivate an attractive, walkable, and inclusive environment for residents, students, and visitors alike.
geographic_addresses: 30489 Broad Street, Princess Anne, MD
Somerset Avenue & Prince William Street, Princess Anne, MD
Beckford Avenue & Williams Street, Princess Anne, MD
U.S. Route 13 & University of Maryland Eastern Shore Boulevard, Princess Anne, MD
U.S. Route 13 & Mt. Vernon Road, Princess Anne, MD

quotes.text: Renovation of an older building at the corner of Somerset Avenue and Prince William Street by a private developer, Davis Strategic Development, as part of a public /private partnership with University of Maryland Eastern Shore. The University of Maryland Eastern Shore mascot is "the hawk", so this building is now known as “Hawk’s Corner”. “Hawk’s Corner” provides offices and meeting space on the first floor and apartments on the second floor.
quotes.briefing_quote: Plan authors highlighted the success of a public-private partnership at 'Hawk's Corner' as a model for revitalization, noting that the project 'provides offices and meeting space on the first floor and apartments on the second floor.'

quotes.text: The purpose of the interior renovations is threefold: (1) to provide an incentive for the build-out of commercial and mixed-use space that is vacant; (2) to encourage existing businesses relocate to downtown commercial space; and (3) to upgrade the existing historic building stock.
quotes.briefing_quote: Town administrators outlined that supporting interior renovations serves 'to provide an incentive for the build-out of commercial and mixed-use space that is vacant' while encouraging businesses to relocate to the downtown district.

quotes.text: Recent construction (2021-2022) of 44 moderately priced (approx. $250,000) new single-family dwellings in Somerset Landing subdivision
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights progress in expanding housing options, pointing to the 'recent construction of 44 moderately priced new single-family dwellings in Somerset Landing subdivision' to support homeownership.

quotes.text: Within the Sustainable Community, there have been several rehabilitated housing units (not new) and several new second floor apartments created in the downtown district. There have been seven (7) new second-floor apartments created and over 15 second-floor apartments rehabilitated.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning documents note that within the target area, downtown revitalization has successfully created 'seven new second-floor apartments and over 15 second-floor apartments rehabilitated,' indicating strong potential for further upper-story residential development.

quotes.text: Homeownership continues to be an issue in Princess Anne as, according to the 2016-2020 ACS 5-year estimates, the town is comprised of approximately 65% renter-occupied and 35% owner-occupied housing units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address systemic housing imbalances, municipal leaders emphasized the need to promote homeownership, noting that the community 'is comprised of approximately 65% renter-occupied and 35% owner-occupied housing units.'

plan_quotes.community_vision: The City of Crisfield aspires to build a more resilient, economically vibrant, and livable community by leveraging its unique working waterfront heritage and natural coastal assets. The community's growth strategy centers on addressing persistent tidal and storm flooding, rehabilitating aging infrastructure, revitalizing its downtown business district, and expanding diverse, affordable, and senior housing options to stabilize and grow its population.

quotes.text: There is a lot of potential for infill development to make for a more dense housing market
quotes.briefing_quote: The City of Crisfield's Sustainable Communities Action Plan highlights that there is "a lot of potential for infill development to make for a more dense housing market," offering developers opportunities to revitalize vacant spaces.

quotes.text: Housing shortage, particularly a lack of senior, affordable, workforce, and rental housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planners identified a critical "housing shortage, particularly a lack of senior, affordable, workforce, and rental housing" as a key barrier to community growth and a prime area for development focus.

quotes.text: Work with non-profits and private developers to create new residential and mixed-use developments that offer a variety of housing types, to include affordable, workforce, and senior housing opportunities
quotes.briefing_quote: To support diverse housing options, the city's strategy is to "work with non-profits and private developers to create new residential and mixed-use developments" that provide affordable, workforce, and senior housing.

quotes.text: Many of the buildings that formerly housed seafood processing plants have become vacant, and several sites have been redeveloped into multi-family residential projects (condos)
quotes.briefing_quote: A land-use assessment notes that "many of the buildings that formerly housed seafood processing plants have become vacant, and several sites have been redeveloped into multi-family residential projects" such as condominiums, establishing a successful precedent for industrial-to-residential conversions.

quotes.text: Many commercial buildings are underutilized in the central business district (empty storefronts)
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes downtown vacancies as a clear redevelopment opportunity, stating that "many commercial buildings are underutilized in the central business district" with empty storefronts.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Somerset County envisions a steady, managed trajectory of slow economic and population growth through the year 2010. The community seeks to transition from its traditional, declining resource-based agriculture and fishing economy toward a diversified mix of services, light manufacturing, tourism, and aquaculture. This growth is directed away from valuable farmland and sensitive environments, concentrating instead within designated primary growth corridors and community nodes served by central water and sewer systems to maintain the county's rural character, preserve historical resources, and protect the Chesapeake Bay.

quotes.text: Somerset should begin to encourage townhouses, patio homes and other more affordable types in order to compete with surrounding communities to retain population and tax base. This would introduce a greater proportion of housing at densities of between 5 and 10 DU per acre, thereby conserving land, bringing people closer to village centers and permitting easier access to a concentration of community facilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To improve housing variety and retain younger residents, the 1996 Plan suggests that Somerset 'begin to encourage townhouses, patio homes and other more affordable types in order to compete with surrounding communities,' aiming to achieve housing densities of between 5 and 10 dwelling units per acre.

quotes.text: Higher residential densities in the form of density bonuses should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, where a high quality central water and sewer system is planned.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning narrative notes that 'higher residential densities in the form of density bonuses should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, where a high quality central water and sewer system is planned' to support sustainable infrastructure.

quotes.text: Strict controls should be placed on the subdivision of farms and the spread of strip residential uses along country roads by limiting development in the 'A' zone to minor subdivisions (no more than six lots).
quotes.briefing_quote: To combat unplanned sprawl on rural roadways, the plan outlines that 'strict controls should be placed on the subdivision of farms and the spread of strip residential uses along country roads by limiting development in the agricultural zone to minor subdivisions.'

quotes.text: Planned Unit Developments (PUDs) should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, with a range of community facilities consistent with the development's needs and the location, size and other criteria typically required by the County. In particular, communities with a broad mix of activities, including residential, commercial, employment and recreation should be preferred...
quotes.briefing_quote: Focusing on innovative layout designs, the plan asserts that 'Planned Unit Developments should be encouraged in the Primary Growth Areas, with a range of community facilities consistent with the development's needs.'

quotes.text: Industrial and commercial development should be encouraged to cluster in office parks and employment centers within the Primary Growth Areas as indicated on the Land Use Plan Map (Map 4) They should be well landscaped, buffered from nearby residential areas and should take positive measures to protect sensitive environmental resources.
quotes.briefing_quote: To balance commercial expansion with environmental protection, the plan recommends that 'industrial and commercial development should be encouraged to cluster in office parks and employment centers within the Primary Growth Areas' to safeguard natural resources.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Princess Anne aspires to foster sustainable economic growth and enhance community vibrancy by leveraging its unique historic assets, scenic location, and strong 'Town and Gown' partnership with the University of Maryland Eastern Shore. The community seeks to revitalize its downtown core through mixed-use development, commercial façade and interior building improvements, and infrastructure modernization. By expanding recreational trails, improving environmental buffers along the Manokin River, and promoting homeownership, Princess Anne aims to cultivate an attractive, walkable, and inclusive environment for residents, students, and visitors alike.

quotes.briefing_quote: Town administrators outlined that supporting interior renovations serves 'to provide an incentive for the build-out of commercial and mixed-use space that is vacant' while encouraging businesses to relocate to the downtown district.

quotes.text: Within the Sustainable Community, there have been several rehabilitated housing units (not new) and several new second floor apartments created in the downtown district. There have been seven (7) new second-floor apartments created and over 15 second-floor apartments rehabilitated.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Port Towns Sustainable Communities initiative, representing Bladensburg, Colmar Manor, Cottage City, and Edmonston, envisions a collaborative and resilient future focused on environmental restoration, economic diversification, and equitable housing. The partner towns aim to leverage their extensive trail networks and historical assets, such as the Anacostia River waterfront, while addressing issues of flooding and pedestrian safety. By fostering an inclusive environment for their diverse, multi-generational populations, the Port Towns aspire to build a thriving local economy through small business support, selective mixed-use redevelopment, and workforce training programs like a localized trade school.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Brentwood aspires to become a highly livable, environmentally resilient, and inclusive municipality. By leveraging its designation in the Gateway Arts District, the town aims to stimulate green and creative economic development, particularly through the rehabilitation of commercial facades along US Route 1 and the adaptive reuse of industrial buildings for artist spaces. Simultaneously, Brentwood is pursuing key infrastructure improvements, including a $2.5 million New Town Center project, extensive stormwater management to combat local flooding, pedestrian and bicycle accessibility via Vision Zero initiatives, and programs dedicated to housing affordability, racial equity, and enabling seniors to age in place.

quotes.text: The Town will relocate the Administrative Support staff and municipal leadership to the old Brentwood Fire Station. A long-term capital campaign, over the past five years, the Town has successfully moved the project forward significantly. A $2.5 million project, architectural and engineering plans have been delivered, construction has continued and overcome significant challenges, cable engineering and landscaping plans have advanced, and residents are able to tour the construction bi-weekly.
quotes.briefing_quote: To centralize municipal services and improve energy efficiency, the Town is moving forward with a $2.5 million "New Town Center project to relocate administrative staff to the historic old Brentwood Fire Station," establishing a centralized hub for community engagement.

quotes.text: Develop and implement a commercial façade program for commercial corridors along Route US 1. Investigate ways to market and leverage the Arts District Designation.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize local business corridors, town strategies emphasize the plan to "develop and implement a commercial façade program for commercial corridors along Route US 1," while actively leveraging the local Arts District designation.

quotes.text: Support local businesses converting existing industrial buildings into artist space. Support interested art-based businesses to facilitate ownership within Town limits.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the unique local economy, town goals aim to "support local businesses converting existing industrial buildings into artist space" and facilitate art-based business ownership within town limits.

quotes.text: Continue outreach efforts to inform residents of programs to help low-income and senior residents to upkeep their property. Provide homeowners, renters, business owners with information on how to plant for and mitigate flooding, stormwater, excess heat, air pollution, and energy efficiency.
quotes.briefing_quote: To ensure residential resilience and support low-income families, the town will "continue outreach efforts to inform residents of programs to help low-income and senior residents to upkeep their property" and adapt to climate challenges.

quotes.text: Advocate for Senior Housing Options and provide funding for current residents to repair, upgrade, and maintain their homes.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the demographic shifts and needs of the aging population, the plan highlights the priority to "advocate for Senior Housing Options and provide funding for current residents to repair, upgrade, and maintain their homes."

quotes.text: Renovation of the current Town Hall into a Police Station and Community Center. Seek grants to assist with the renovations of the Police Station and Community Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: To optimize existing real estate, the municipal strategy targets the "renovation of the current Town Hall into a Police Station and Community Center," seeking state and federal grants to realize this essential community facility.

plan_quotes.community_vision: North Brentwood envisions a vibrant, culturally rich, and resilient future that celebrates its history as the first incorporated African American municipality in Prince George's County. Through the revitalization of the Route 1 corridor and the activation of historic community spaces like Sis's Tavern, the town aims to foster economic growth, support artist and minority-owned businesses, and implement critical green infrastructure to combat chronic flooding. Additionally, the community is focused on preserving its historic character and providing affordable senior housing options to prevent displacement from gentrification.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

Simultaneously, Towson seeks to preserve its cultural and historical legacy, particularly in the Historic East Towson neighborhood, while guiding future density through high-quality mixed-use development, commercial revitalization, and proactive affordable housing strategies.
geographic_addresses: 105 W Chesapeake Avenue, Towson, MD
Chesapeake Avenue & Pennsylvania Avenue, Towson, MD
Bosley Avenue, Towson, MD
York Road, Towson, MD

quotes.text: Leveraging $350 million in private/public funding, to include commercial redevelopment and RISE zone designations, the 1.2 million SF mixed-use project focused on redevelopment of 100,000 square feet of restaurant and retail space, 150,000 square feet of Class A office space, 300 student housing units and 250 high rise residential units.
quotes.briefing_quote: The multi-year build-out of Towson Row demonstrates how public-private partnerships can successfully deliver density, "leveraging $350 million in private/public funding, to include commercial redevelopment... [to build] 300 student housing units and 250 high rise residential units" alongside commercial space.

quotes.text: Encourage mixed-use housing options that combine commercial and office spaces with residential units in order to create a more dynamic environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: To cultivate a more vibrant downtown core, county planning staff emphasized the need to "encourage mixed-use housing options that combine commercial and office spaces with residential units" in order to create a more dynamic environment.

quotes.text: Maintain the Downtown Towson (DT) zoning overlay and identify additional zoning changes to encourage the development of high-quality, mixed-use development in the Sustainable Community area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To spur modern redevelopment, the updated plan recommends that the county "maintain the Downtown Towson zoning overlay and identify additional zoning changes" to encourage high-quality, mixed-use development within the Sustainable Community Area.

quotes.text: Provide suitable incentives for key redevelopments of aging commercial and multi-family properties in Towson.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing the need to modernize the existing built environment, the plan calls on the county to "provide suitable incentives for key redevelopments of aging commercial and multi-family properties".

quotes.text: Office vacancies, driven by the pandemic, work-from-home, and other trends, increased sharply: from roughly 6% in the prior period to approximately 18% currently.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning document highlights a significant commercial challenge, noting that "office vacancies, driven by the pandemic, work-from-home, and other trends, increased sharply: from roughly 6% in the prior period to approximately 18% currently".

quotes.text: The County has made efforts to promote the creation and preservation of affordable housing within areas of opportunity, but the progress made within Towson has not kept pace with the existing need.
quotes.briefing_quote: While county initiatives have targeted housing equity, planners acknowledged that "progress made within Towson has not kept pace with the existing need" for creating and preserving affordable housing within high-opportunity areas.

quotes.text: Seek to prevent further commercial encroachment in Historic East Towson through appropriate planning consideration of future land use and zoning regulations
quotes.briefing_quote: To protect the neighborhood's unique residential heritage, the plan highlights a directive to "seek to prevent further commercial encroachment in Historic East Towson" through appropriate planning consideration of future land use and zoning regulations.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Waldorf aspires to transform its high-density, urban core through transit-oriented, mixed-use redevelopment, prioritizing downtown-style development within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor. The community focuses on accelerating infill development, expanding pedestrian and bicycle connectivity, increasing the supply and diversity of affordable housing, and implementing aggressive infrastructure upgrades to address stormwater and environmental needs.

quotes.text: There has been increased interest in developing high-density, multi-family residential in the WURC.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county highlighted that there has been "increased interest in developing high-density, multi-family residential" within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor, signaling a strong market opportunity for transit-oriented growth.

quotes.text: The WURC area consists largely of small and narrowly shaped lots, which has posed a challenge to redevelopment. Parcel acquisition/consolidation is needed.
quotes.briefing_quote: To facilitate larger scale infill projects, planners noted that "the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor area consists largely of small and narrowly shaped lots, which has posed a challenge to redevelopment," indicating that "parcel acquisition and consolidation is needed."

quotes.text: The downtown-style development planned for the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) and Greenberg Gibbons development has not yet occurred, mainly because these are long term projects that take several years to come to fruition: In addition, there have been several obstacles to creating a downtown in the WURC corridor; including fractured property ownership, inadequate infrastructure, and general lack in investment of the type to spur redevelopment:
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines the challenges of long-term development, noting that "obstacles to creating a downtown in the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor" have historically included fractured property ownership and inadequate infrastructure, which the county is actively working to resolve.

quotes.text: The Greenberg Gibbons Company is in the approvals process for a Phase I development of a mixed- use project in 2022 that will comprise residential, assisted living, lodging and hospitality, office and retail/entertainment elements in Waldorf.
quotes.briefing_quote: Indicating high-density mixed-use progress, developers noted that "the Greenberg Gibbons Company is in the approvals process for a Phase I development of a mixed-use project that will comprise residential, assisted living, lodging and hospitality, office, and retail/entertainment elements" in Waldorf.

quotes.text: In 2018 the county, with the assistance of an American Planning Association- sponsored Community Planning Assistance Team, conducted a study to assess the county's housing needs and provide recommendations for strategies to increase housing diversity, supply and affordability:
quotes.briefing_quote: With an eye toward equitable residential development, the county collaborated with a "Community Planning Assistance Team to assess housing needs and provide recommendations for strategies to increase housing diversity, supply and affordability."
