quotes.text: The Fitzgerald apartment building, located at 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue in Mid-Town Belvedere, is an example of a successful Transit Oriented Development project in Baltimore. Built in 2010, adjacent to the Mt. Royal/MICA Light Rail station, the seven-story building has 275 apartment units and two commercial establishments on the lower level
quotes.briefing_quote: A prime example of successful transit-oriented development is the Fitzgerald apartment building, which stands as a seven-story building with 275 apartment units and ground-floor commercial establishments adjacent to the Light Rail, showcasing how dense, mixed-use infill can thrive in Baltimore.

quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. These areas are relatively rich in the resources needed for quality of life and healthy child development, but as a result of a long practice of exclusion, they currently have limited affordable housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To affirmatively further fair housing, the plan emphasizes that in stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed-income developments to reverse long practices of exclusion.

quotes.text: Replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and the vacant former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, new elementary middle school, two new parks, and a renovated and expanded Chick Webb Recreation Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Perkins Somerset Oldtown Transformation Plan represents a massive revitalization effort, replacing obsolete housing with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, and essential community spaces.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. These are largely stable, highly livable, and resilient communities, but unfortunately, they have historically received little benefit from national and local housing policies that have often failed to support the middle class.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing policy experts highlighted the critical need to support middle neighborhoods, noting that these homes generate wealth over generations for families whose future security is tied to their communities' ongoing success.

quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Sustainable Communities report underscores that despite general income gains, Baltimore "continues to experience a shortage of affordable rental and homeownership units particularly for households earning 50% or less of the Area Median Income."

quotes.text: To provide safe and decent housing and help owners maintain their housing values, the City and Housing Authority dedicate considerable resources to increasing and preserving its supply of affordable housing for both homeowners and renters.
quotes.briefing_quote: Municipal planners indicated that the city aims to "dedicate considerable resources to increasing and preserving its supply of affordable housing for both homeowners and renters" to stabilize residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Vacant lots and buildings are consolidated to create new mixed-income rental and for-sale housing sites. Abandoned industrial sites are repurposed and frequently leverage additional investment.

quotes.text: Expand full spectrum housing for residents at diverse income levels and life stages and for individuals with disabilities by encouraging high quality mixed income, multigenerational developments. Continue to implement smart growth policies by supporting mixed-use development and Traditional Neighborhood Development in the area.

quotes.text: Some homes in Colonial Village have been improved. There are homes in the Pikesville area that have gone through the zoning petition process for additions. quotes.briefing_quote: In Pikesville, growing families are actively seeking zoning petitions for home additions and secondary kitchens to meet specific cultural and religious food preparation needs.

quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate growth, the community aims to 'develop high-density residential opportunity within the Sustainable Communities Area' by identifying eligible parcels and creating flexible zoning tools.

quotes.text: One of the primary ways of increasing housing options for seniors is by designating a property or community as age restricted. The market is not providing units (infill or otherwise) with restrictions that decrease the attractiveness of property or limit a property’s sales potential.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the housing needs of older residents is a key concern, as 'the market is not providing units (infill or otherwise) with restrictions' tailored to seniors, highlighting a need for targeted developmental incentives.

quotes.text: Sustainable Communities Area includes different commercial, residential, and mixed-use zones
quotes.briefing_quote: A key spatial planning strength is that the 'Sustainable Communities Area includes different commercial, residential, and mixed-use zones,' offering versatile infill opportunities.

quotes.text: Innovative commercial building interior renovations program leverages significant private investment in unused or underused buildings
quotes.briefing_quote: The City highlights that its 'innovative commercial building interior renovations program leverages significant private investment' in vacant or underutilized properties.

quotes.text: The City perceives a gap in funding opportunities for property owners who are willing to make aesthetically correct improvements or repairs to the exterior of their buildings but are unwilling to meet the financial and bureaucratic burden of the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards.

quotes.text: Past zoning has segregated the most affordable housing and therefore low-income residents in certain parts of the Sustainable Communities Area
quotes.briefing_quote: Looking forward, the plan notes a historical weakness where 'past zoning has segregated the most affordable housing' in specific areas, prompting a desire for more integrated housing opportunities.

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

By leveraging sustainable community programs and targeted public investments, the area strives to foster commercial growth, address transportation and pedestrian connectivity gaps, and build active, safe, and attractive neighborhoods where families of all backgrounds can thrive.

quotes.text: There is currently an affordable housing proposal within the Pikesville CRD that is requesting rezoning to support multi-family apartments.
quotes.briefing_quote: In the Pikesville Commercial Revitalization District, there is an affordable housing proposal requesting rezoning to support multi-family apartments, showing local momentum for adding density.

quotes.text: There has not been demolition of blighted properties in the area. However, there is an interest from the County to assemble vacant commercial properties on Liberty Rd to assist CDCs in redevelopment. In addition, there is discussion to redevelop the old International House of Pancakes and Bennigan's restaurants located in front of Security Square mall.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county is looking to assemble vacant commercial properties along Liberty Road to assist community development corporations in redevelopment, with further discussions centered on redeveloping the former restaurant sites in front of Security Square Mall.

quotes.text: Expand full spectrum housing for residents at diverse income levels and life stages and for individuals with disabilities by encouraging high quality mixed income, multigenerational developments. Promote Housing Accessibility Modification programs to make housing more accessible. Continue to implement smart growth policies by supporting mixed-use development and Traditional Neighborhood Development in the area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning guidelines emphasize the need to encourage high-quality mixed-income, multigenerational developments while supporting smart growth policies such as mixed-use and Traditional Neighborhood Development.

quotes.text: Some homes in Colonial Village have been improved. There are homes in the Pikesville area that have gone through the zoning petition process for additions. This is largely attributed to growing families that require additional space and secondary kitchens due to religious food preparation requirements.
quotes.briefing_quote: In Pikesville, growing families are actively seeking zoning petitions for home additions and secondary kitchens to meet specific cultural and religious food preparation needs.

quotes.text: Lack of quality retail and chain restaurants in the Liberty Rd CRD... Lack of variety of businesses to meet the needs of the community... Abundance of unwanted businesses... Businesses closing and vacant gas stations are an eyesore to the residents
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback highlights a lack of quality retail and restaurant variety along the Liberty Road Commercial Revitalization District, alongside concerns over vacant storefronts and gas stations.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.

quotes.text: Given that most new residential growth in the city will come in the form of multiple unit residential buildings, as apartments or condominiums, and that not all locations are appropriate for mixed-use development, Rockville needs a higher density residential zone.

quotes.text: One way to accommodate more affordable housing options, flexible space for an office or shared family living arrangements, and financial assistance for current homeowners, while maintaining the city’s predominantly residential character, is with accessory apartments and accessory dwelling units.

quotes.text: Steady additions of commercial and amenity space on the ground floor of new buildings bring the opportunity for new shops and restaurants, supported by new residential units and offices on upper floors. quotes.text: These 'missing middle' housing types, also discussed in the Land Use Element, include: Duplexes; Triplexes; Fourplexes or quads; Sixplexes; Townhouses or rowhouses; Small apartment buildings; and Garden apartments. quotes.text: The most successful office clusters in Montgomery County are part of mixed-use development with a strong sense of place and quality environment. Transit connectivity is increasingly important to office tenants.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: By 2040, Thurmont envisions becoming a vibrant community with an active, economically resilient downtown where both historic and new buildings support successful businesses and housing. The Town intends to pursue steady, balanced growth that preserves its scenic natural setting at the foot of the Catoctin Mountains, maintaining its cozy, small-town atmosphere while establishing an interconnected system of parks, trails, and clean, modern industries.
geographic_addresses: Main Street & Church Street, Thurmont, MD
Main Street & Water Street, Thurmont, MD
Frederick Road & Water Street, Thurmont, MD
Apples Church Road & Graceham Road, Thurmont, MD

quotes.text: The TB district effectively prohibits the mixing of residential uses with commercial uses and thus prevents building owners from adapting to market conditions that favor residential.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize the commercial center, the plan highlights the opportunity to update local regulations, noting that the traditional 'Town Business' district 'effectively prohibits the mixing of residential uses with commercial uses,' and suggests that flexible zoning will allow building owners to adapt to market conditions that favor residential integration.

quotes.text: The Zoning Ordinance effectively prohibits the creation of most housing types that could meet the needs and preference of people who would like to live in or near a historic downtown. It also prevents the conversion of long vacant storefronts into needed housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the need for diverse downtown housing options, observing that previous zoning rules 'effectively prohibit the creation of most housing types' and recommending that allowing the conversion of long vacant storefronts into needed housing will help meet the preferences of residents wanting to live in the historic center.

quotes.text: Some intensification of existing areas may be feasible but additional space for modern light industrial and office employment is necessary to capitalize again on regional economic development.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support fiscal health and job growth, the plan states that while existing spaces can be intensified, 'additional space for modern light industrial and office employment is necessary to capitalize again on regional economic development' and secure the town's long-term economic resilience.

quotes.text: Open lands in and around the Town could be developed as conventional single-use residential subdivisions or in ways that distinguish them as excellent neighborhoods unique to Thurmont. Left to chance, land development seldom organizes itself into coherent extensions of existing or historic patterns.
quotes.briefing_quote: Rather than allowing conventional subdivisions, the plan calls for deliberate coordination, warning that 'left to chance, land development seldom organizes itself into coherent extensions of existing or historic patterns' and highlighting the opportunity to design exceptional, integrated neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Within and near Downtown, mixed-use development is encouraged as well as a broad array of land uses including the commercial uses that exist there today and a variety of housing types such as apartment and condominium buildings, senior housing, and townhouses.
quotes.briefing_quote: Promoting a dynamic central core, the plan notes that 'mixed-use development is encouraged as well as a broad array of land uses' including apartments, townhouses, and senior housing, which will enhance downtown vitality while preserving its historic commercial character.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Thurmont aspires to remain a family-oriented, highly walkable, and environmentally conscious community that preserves its historic 'Gateway to the Mountains' charm. The town seeks to methodically manage residential growth through cluster zoning, revitalize its downtown commercial core (including mixed-use adaptive reuse and becoming a designated Arts and Entertainment District), and address critical service gaps such as senior housing and local healthcare facilities.
geographic_addresses: 615 East Main Street, Thurmont, MD
East Main Street & Water Street, Thurmont, MD
Frederick Road & Thurmont Boulevard, Thurmont, MD
Radio Lane & Eyler Road, Thurmont, MD

quotes.text: The Hammaker Hills development has been constructed with the "clustering" effect that became an ordinance in 2019. Single family homes built on less land with little or no maintenance is very attractive to a younger home buyer. The rest of the land is in turn donated to the town for green space.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planners highlighted a successful shift in residential development, noting that 'The Hammaker Hills development has been constructed with the "clustering" effect... Single family homes built on less land with little or no maintenance is very attractive to a younger home buyer,' demonstrating a viable path toward low-maintenance homeownership.

quotes.text: Thurmont continues to have lack of senior or senior assisted living housing available along with smaller home (cottage type) size homes for those just starting out and/or seniors.
quotes.briefing_quote: Plan authors identified a critical local gap, stating that 'Thurmont continues to have lack of senior or senior assisted living housing available along with smaller home (cottage type) size homes for those just starting out and/or seniors.'

quotes.text: To recapture this building as a focal point for Main Street. ... A first floor as commercial business(es) within the next two years and living quarters above within the next three years.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize a key historic landmark downtown, the plan outlines an opportunity 'To recapture this building as a focal point for Main Street' by establishing 'a first floor as commercial business(es)... and living quarters above' within the next three years.

quotes.text: Review the Zoning Ordinance to ensure that smaller housing options are allowed that fit well within the Town’s existing neighborhoods, which will allow seniors to age in place and fit the affordable housing needs.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the need to 'Review the Zoning Ordinance to ensure that smaller housing options are allowed that fit well within the Town’s existing neighborhoods, which will allow seniors to age in place and fit the affordable housing needs.'

quotes.text: Adopting architectural and building design guidelines that will guide both infill development and redevelopment within the proposed Downtown Development District... Avoid formulaic building design and franchise architecture, signage, and new buildings or site layouts that impair rather than complement the Town’s historic character and natural setting.
quotes.briefing_quote: To retain visual identity, town planners recommend 'adopting architectural and building design guidelines' to 'avoid formulaic building design and franchise architecture... that impair rather than complement the Town’s historic character and natural setting.'

quotes.text: No new housing units have been built in the Sustainable Community designated area at this time, but developments are being reviewed for the addition of a mixed housing and commercial development, which would be a mix of single family and townhomes.

quotes.text: MXD Zone is newly adopted and being used on the Beck Property - allows opportunity for mixed residential and commercial development... GreeneTree Development - Town houses, villas, single family homes, commercial element.

quotes.text: Use the Master Plan process to encourage adding housing for seniors... Use the Master Plan process to encourage adding housing for emerging adulthood professionals.

quotes.text: Water capacity does not yield a complete buildout of all infill development- Town will need additional sources of water to develop infill properties.

quotes.text: Mixed-Use Development (MXD) and (MXU-CC) are two new zoning options for the Town. Neither has been officially approved for development, but the land owners are working through process.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: Some intensification of existing areas may be feasible but additional space for modern light industrial and office employment is necessary to capitalize again on regional economic development.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support fiscal health and job growth, the plan states that while existing spaces can be intensified, 'additional space for modern light industrial and office employment is necessary to capitalize again on regional economic development' and secure the town's long-term economic resilience.

quotes.text: Open lands in and around the Town could be developed as conventional single-use residential subdivisions or in ways that distinguish them as excellent neighborhoods unique to Thurmont. Left to chance, land development seldom organizes itself into coherent extensions of existing or historic patterns.
quotes.briefing_quote: Rather than allowing conventional subdivisions, the plan calls for deliberate coordination, warning that 'left to chance, land development seldom organizes itself into coherent extensions of existing or historic patterns' and highlighting the opportunity to design exceptional, integrated neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Within and near Downtown, mixed-use development is encouraged as well as a broad array of land uses including the commercial uses that exist there today and a variety of housing types such as apartment and condominium buildings, senior housing, and townhouses.
quotes.briefing_quote: Promoting a dynamic central core, the plan notes that 'mixed-use development is encouraged as well as a broad array of land uses' including apartments, townhouses, and senior housing, which will enhance downtown vitality while preserving its historic commercial character.

plan_quotes.community_vision: To revitalize and redevelop the former Fort Ritchie Army Base and the surrounding Cascade area into a vibrant, walkable, 'live, work, and play' community. plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

quotes.text: Expanding the areas where multi-family and apartment development is allowed would increase the availability of development sites and reduce the cost of land per unit. The County and municipalities should review and increase allowable densities where appropriate.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address the housing shortage, the plan notes that "expanding the areas where multi-family and apartment development is allowed" would increase the availability of development sites and reduce land costs per unit.

quotes.text: By reducing the growth of new residential development in agricultural and rural areas... encouraging and directing growth to existing communities and within designated areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county's primary growth management strategy focuses on "reducing the growth of new residential development in agricultural and rural areas" by directing future growth into established communities.

quotes.text: In the Grasonville Village Center, low- and medium-intensity commercial uses are encouraged, along with single-family and multi-family housing. The existing village scale is maintained and enhanced so that this area once again becomes a true village center...
quotes.briefing_quote: For the Grasonville Village Center, the plan outlines an opportunity where "low- and medium-intensity commercial uses are encouraged, along with single-family and multi-family housing" to help reestablish a vibrant village scale.

quotes.text: It is the County's intent that remaining un-allocated sewer capacity should be reserved for commercial uses, directing any new residential development to the incorporated towns that have capacity to accommodate it. Infill development is development that takes place on vacant, undeveloped or underutilized parcels within an area that is already characterized by development...
quotes.briefing_quote: To address infrastructure constraints, the plan stresses the need to "reserve remaining sewer capacity for commercial uses, directing any new residential development to the incorporated towns" that have the capacity to accommodate it.

quotes.text: Many communities are making zoning provisions for 'Missing Middle' housing—housing types with unit sizes and densities between those of single-family and multi-family zones... They include small-lot single-family units, duplexes, triplexes, townhouses, cottage homes, and small multi-family buildings of four to eight units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To provide more diverse and affordable choices, the plan encourages zoning provisions for "'Missing Middle' housing—housing types with unit sizes and densities between those of single-family and multi-family zones".

quotes.text: The Centreville water service map also shows an area designated as W-3 at the intersection of US 301/MD 304. This is an area that has a mixture of commercial, industrial, and municipal uses. In addition, there are some parcels that are currently agricultural. It was suggested that the vacant areas be developed into a County-developed business park.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning framework identifies a strategic opportunity at the intersection of US 301 and MD 304 to develop vacant agricultural parcels into a County-developed business park, supporting a balanced mix of commercial, industrial, and municipal uses.

quotes.text: Both the Town and County Comprehensive Plans call for a mix of residential and commercial land uses on lands in and adjacent to the Town and within the Queenstown Growth Area.
quotes.briefing_quote: Comprehensive strategies for Queenstown emphasize the need to integrate a balanced mix of residential and commercial land uses within the designated growth area to foster vibrant local development.

quotes.text: TRUE commercial apartments – zoning may need to be refined such that the apartments would be ancillary to the commercial, not the other way around.
quotes.briefing_quote: To better manage infrastructure and sewer allocations, the technical committee recommended refining zoning guidelines to encourage true commercial apartments that function strictly as ancillary to commercial developments.

quotes.text: Prohibit any further large-scale residential development. Remove large vacant parcels from the Growth Area – rezone/downzone if required
quotes.briefing_quote: Wastewater capacity limitations have prompted calls to prohibit further large-scale residential developments and potentially rezone or downzone large vacant parcels out of active Growth Areas to protect local infrastructure.

quotes.text: Development has been stalled in this area due to an outdated plan that did not truly promote transit-oriented development. A new Transit District Development Plan was adopted by Prince George’s County in 2015 and prospects have improved. A WMATA joint development project was approved for 400 apartment units and 10,000 SF of retail and County owned property across from the Metro station is being sold for mixed-use development.
quotes.briefing_quote: While past development near the Metro station was hindered by outdated zoning, the adoption of a new Transit District Development Plan has unlocked major opportunities, including an approved project featuring "400 apartment units and 10,000 square feet of retail" alongside county-owned property slated for transit-oriented mixed-use development.

quotes.text: The City has approved 10 new multifamily/townhouse projects since 2017 amounting to an increase of 2,626 dwelling units. About a dozen single-family home infill development has occurred. ... Most new development in College Park is redevelopment of commercial corridors and centers.
quotes.briefing_quote: Indicating a strong market preference for higher-density redevelopment in commercial areas, the plan notes that "the City has approved 10 new multifamily/townhouse projects since 2017" representing an addition of 2,626 dwelling units.

quotes.text: Strengthen College Park neighborhoods by reducing the number of single-family homes that are converted to group rental properties by continuing to offer homeownership grant programs, establishing a community land trust, and exploring new programs for housing rehabilitation with Habitat for Humanity Maryland.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community aims to stabilize residential areas, seeking to "strengthen College Park neighborhoods by reducing the number of single-family homes that are converted to group rental properties" through the creation of a community land trust and targeted homeownership programs.

quotes.text: Use recently acquired property on Calvert Road for the development of missing middle housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To promote housing type diversity, community planning goals advise the city to "use recently acquired property on Calvert Road for the development of missing middle housing" as a bridge between low- and high-density neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many long-term businesses have closed or have been relocated due to new development. ARPA assistance was provided to many businesses and has helped, but high rents are making it difficult for local, independent businesses to survive and for other to enter the market.
quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting a clear opportunity for developers to build affordable storefront spaces, the plan notes that "high rents are making it difficult for local, independent businesses to survive and for others to enter the market" amid ongoing corridor redevelopment.

quotes.text: Route 1 has seen tremendous redevelopment activity since being rezoned from C-S-C (Commercial Shopping Center) to M-U-I (Mixed-Use Infill) in 2001 and is successfully transforming from a strip commercial corridor to a mixed-use boulevard with a series of walkable nodes
quotes.briefing_quote: Due to progressive zoning changes, the US Route 1 corridor is "successfully transforming from a strip commercial corridor to a mixed-use boulevard with a series of walkable nodes" that enhance local economic vibrancy.

community_organizations: College Park Neighborhood Quality of Life Committee
College Park Committee for a Better Environment

properties.tract_name: The suburb of Sparrows Point

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Greater Dundalk/Sparrows Point community envisions a multi-year revitalization strategy focused on increasing economic vitality, expanding environmental resilience, and improving community livability. By leveraging its powerful industrial and deep-water assets like Tradepoint Atlantic and the Port of Baltimore, the community aims to create permanent jobs, expand workforce training, and enhance housing quality. The vision focuses on revitalizing historic commercial corridors like the Historic Dundalk Town Center, preserving waterfront assets, and providing a range of high-quality, affordable housing to support first-time homebuyers and aging-in-place seniors.
geographic_addresses: 2500 Sparrows Point Road, Dundalk, MD
3447 Dundalk Avenue, Dundalk, MD

quotes.text: Identify potential zoning changes to encourage the development of high-quality, mixed-use development along major corridors in the Dundalk area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To stimulate corridor revitalization, the plan outlines the need to "identify potential zoning changes to encourage the development of high-quality, mixed-use development along major corridors in the Dundalk area."

quotes.text: Barriers to high density, high-quality development (policies, development approval processes)
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planning assessments highlighted regulatory hurdles, noting "barriers to high density, high-quality development" resulting from current policies and development approval processes.

quotes.text: Expand the supply of quality affordable housing for families, first time homebuyers, and disabled and elderly households
quotes.briefing_quote: A primary objective is to "expand the supply of quality affordable housing for families, first time homebuyers, and disabled and elderly households" to support the shifting demographic profile.

quotes.text: Limited flexibility in residential zoning to allow for appropriate small-scale commercial uses to serve the needs of more remote communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes an opportunity to update current frameworks to address "limited flexibility in residential zoning to allow for appropriate small-scale commercial uses to serve the needs of more remote communities."

quotes.text: Develop strategies to identify and actively attract business types that are desired by the community in portions of Dundalk, such as grocery stores, cafes or coffee shops, and restaurants
quotes.briefing_quote: To fill commercial gaps, the workgroup recommended that the County "develop strategies to identify and actively attract business types that are desired by the community in portions of Dundalk, such as grocery stores, cafes or coffee shops, and restaurants."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD
Cowenton Avenue & Pulaski Highway, White Marsh, MD
Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

The town aims to upgrade its critical water and sewer infrastructure to accommodate future infill development, provide a diverse range of housing options (including workforce and senior housing), and attract commercial activities along the U.S. Route 50 corridor, all while maintaining its unique small-town character.

quotes.text: Explore zoning changes so that multi-family residences can be permitted in appropriate areas
quotes.briefing_quote: To expand housing diversity, town coordinators suggested that Hebron "explore zoning changes so that multi-family residences can be permitted in appropriate areas."

quotes.text: Promote new commercial activities in the Town Center such as small shops, drug store, variety store, service station, as well as institutional uses
quotes.briefing_quote: To bolster the local economy, the plan advocates to "promote new commercial activities in the Town Center such as small shops, drug store, variety store, service station, as well as institutional uses."

quotes.text: Of the Town's 554 undeveloped acres, 511 acres, which are outside of the Sustainable Community area, are included in the Planned Neighborhood category intended for development as new large-scale mixed-use projects that are linked with and made an integral part of the existing Town area
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that 511 acres are designated for future growth "intended for development as new large-scale mixed-use projects that are linked with and made an integral part of the existing Town area."

quotes.text: Encourage the development of senior restricted housing to meet the demands of Hebron's aging population
quotes.briefing_quote: To support residents wishing to age in place, local planners recommended the town "encourage the development of senior restricted housing to meet the demands of Hebron's aging population."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Salisbury is committed to fostering a vibrant, sustainable, and inclusive community by concentrating growth in its urban core, expanding bicycle and pedestrian network infrastructure, and improving water quality. Through proactive municipal programs like the 'Here is Home' initiative, the City seeks to expand and diversify its housing stock, encourage mixed-use vertical development downtown, and create robust support systems for chronically homeless populations, while strengthening local arts, business, and educational opportunities.

quotes.briefing_quote: Highlighting downtown growth potential, planning documents track 'The Ross,' which is a 'redevelopment of 3 existing parcels on West Main Street in Downtown' consisting of 100 apartments and commercial space.

quotes.text: Selling city-owned properties to developers in order to create mixed-use development
quotes.briefing_quote: To catalyze revitalization, the City has utilized the strength of 'selling city-owned properties to developers in order to create mixed-use development' in the urban core.

quotes.text: Lack of concentration of high-end housing in the urban core
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes a 'lack of concentration of high-end housing in the urban core' as a current weakness, signaling a target opportunity for upscale multi-family projects.

quotes.text: Low return on investment for vertical development
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analyses identified a 'low return on investment for vertical development' as a weakness, suggesting that developers may require targeted local incentives or partnerships to make mid-rise projects viable.

quotes.text: Here is Home fee reimbursement program to encourage new housing options within the SC Area. The program has 67 residential projects equaling 8,049 housing units entered in the program that closed February 28, 2022
quotes.briefing_quote: To aggressively expand supply, the City instituted the 'Here is Home fee reimbursement program to encourage new housing options within the Sustainable Community Area,' generating entries for over 8,000 potential units.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community where residents enjoy a top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, and innovative businesses. The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.
geographic_addresses: Frederick Road & Triadelphia Road, Ellicott City, MD
Broken Land Parkway & Snowden River Parkway, Columbia, MD
Woodland Road & Route 108, Ellicott City, MD
Sanner Road & Johns Hopkins Road, Clarksville, MD
Snowden River Parkway & Oakland Mills Road, Columbia, MD

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Long Reach aspires to revitalize its Village Center, shifting from primary retail to a vibrant mix of arts, culture, community-driven services, and institutional uses. The community envisions achieving sustainable growth by advancing multi-modal 'complete streets' infrastructure, enhancing its neighborhood green spaces, and preserving its diverse housing stock while carefully balancing any new residential density with public facility constraints.
geographic_addresses: Tamar Drive & Flamepool Way, Columbia, MD
Tamar Drive & Snowden River Parkway, Columbia, MD
Oakland Mills Road & Old Montgomery Road, Columbia, MD
Hayshed Lane & Tamar Drive, Columbia, MD
Phelps Luck Drive & Tamar Drive, Columbia, MD
5320 Phelps Luck Drive, Columbia, MD

quotes.text: In 2018, the New Town Preliminary Development Plan (PDP) was increased by 315 units to allow for a mixed-use redevelopment project at the Long Reach Village Center. However, the redevelopment project was hindered by a complex zoning process and the need to acquire multiple properties under different ownership and was unable to overcome these barriers.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning analysis indicates that while the New Town Preliminary Development Plan was expanded by 315 units to enable mixed-use development at the Village Center, 'the redevelopment project was hindered by a complex zoning process and the need to acquire multiple properties under different ownership', highlighting a critical area where public-private coordination can streamline future efforts.

quotes.text: The Housing Commission has expressed interested in redeveloping the Columbia Landing apartment community. Due to existing debt on the property, the Commission would have to significantly increase density to be able to finance the redevelopment. With elementary schools in the area currently overcapacity, the project would likely not be able to proceed for up to 5 years due to the Adequate Public Facilities Ordinance requirements and would need a waiver to proceed.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Housing Commission expressed a strong desire to update local housing, but noted that 'due to existing debt on the property, the Commission would have to significantly increase density to be able to finance the redevelopment', which is currently paused due to local school capacity and Adequate Public Facilities Ordinance requirements.

quotes.text: The Housing Opportunities Master Plan recommends adding affordable units in all new and redevelopment communities, especially if the existing affordable units are not accessible, energy efficient or integrated into market rate communities. However, community feedback within the Long Reach community suggest that Long Reach already has a disproportion share of affordable housing, as compared to the rest of the County.
quotes.briefing_quote: While county plans recommend adding affordable units to all new developments, 'community feedback within the Long Reach community suggests that Long Reach already has a disproportionate share of affordable housing' compared to the rest of the county, indicating a need for a more balanced approach to market-rate and affordable integration.

quotes.text: The most recent subdivision constructed in Long Reach --Arnold’s Corner -- consisted of 18 single-family dwellings with an advertised starting price of $900,000. New Town Zoning, comprising most of Long Reach, does not require Moderately Priced Housing Units (MIHU’s) and they were not constructed as part of this development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan documents that the newest local subdivision, Arnold's Corner, 'consisted of 18 single-family dwellings with an advertised starting price of $900,000' and did not include moderately priced housing units because the underlying New Town zoning does not mandate them.

quotes.text: Market studies have identified opportunities for new/expanded uses in LRVC, including: a shift in use from primary retail to community and institutional uses; an arts theme to complement the Columbia Art Center, potentially to include artist work/sell/exhibit space, studio space, classrooms, and shared production space; and new housing
quotes.briefing_quote: Market evaluations indicate a strong opportunity to reposition commercial space, highlighting 'a shift in use from primary retail to community and institutional uses, an arts theme to complement the Columbia Art Center, and new housing'.

quotes.text: Any Village Center redevelopment plan that includes housing should address the need for additional affordable senior housing and affordable family housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup members and planning guidelines emphasize that 'any Village Center redevelopment plan that includes housing should address the need for additional affordable senior housing and affordable family housing' to promote a diverse, multi-generational neighborhood.

community_organizations: Community Action Council of Howard County

plan_quotes.community_vision: By 2030, the City of Frederick aspires to be a welcoming, progressive, and authentically charming community of over 85,000 residents. The City intends to manage sustainable urban development that balances economic prosperity with housing, employment, and cultural opportunities for everyone. Through active civic engagement, Frederick aims to strengthen its vibrant downtown and diverse, walkable neighborhoods, supported by well-coordinated, multimodal transportation choices that connect residents locally and regionally.

quotes.text: The rise in population has resulted in the developments and investments in newly annexed lands, along with denser and compact infill development in and around the downtown core.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that rapid growth has spurred 'developments and investments in newly annexed lands, along with denser and compact infill development in and around the downtown core' to serve as a catalyst for a vibrant city center.

quotes.text: Except for the Downtown area, the majority of the City’s residential neighborhoods are characterized by lower densities, wider streets, and uniformity in the types of structures and styles. Low-density residential districts drive land consumption rates and generally create the most infrastructure demand.
quotes.briefing_quote: Urban planners noted that, outside of the downtown core, 'the majority of the City’s residential neighborhoods are characterized by lower densities... Low-density residential districts drive land consumption rates and generally create the most infrastructure demand.'

quotes.text: One of the concerns consistently stressed by residents is the segregation of land uses and the lack of nearby supporting retail and service uses. This segregation of land uses contributes to an increase in the length and number of automobile trips.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public workshops, citizens consistently voiced concern regarding 'the segregation of land uses and the lack of nearby supporting retail and service uses,' urging the City to encourage mixed-use neighborhoods to reduce dependency on cars.

quotes.text: The majority of the existing strip centers give little regard for efficiently integrated vehicular and pedestrian access. To provide a more coherent and more attractive environment, future redevelopment along these corridors should be integrated with surrounding businesses and neighborhoods.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes that 'the majority of the existing strip centers give little regard for efficiently integrated vehicular and pedestrian access,' recommending that future commercial corridor redevelopments tie seamlessly back into surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: The residential land uses are proposed at greater densities than previously approved by City Comprehensive Plans. The purpose of this is to provide incentives towards infill and redevelopment and to encourage a higher population served by existing services and utilities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To leverage existing infrastructure, 'residential land uses are proposed at greater densities than previously approved' to incentivize urban infill and support a growing downtown customer base.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Arbutus aspires to transition into a vibrant "college town" leveraging its proximity to the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) while carefully protecting the area's historic single-family character and small-town charm. The community aims to capitalize on its strategic role as a logistics and technology hub, revitalizing key commercial corridors like East Drive and Linden Avenue with diverse retail, arts, and mixed-use transit-oriented developments that serve residents and students alike.
geographic_addresses: Waelchi Avenue & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Linden Avenue & Shelbourne Road, Arbutus, MD
Shelbourne Road & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Tom Day & Southwestern Boulevard, Arbutus, MD

quotes.text: The proposed Arbutus Station is a mixed-use development by a local developer at the intersection of Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road. It is within the proposed Sustainable Community boundary and the County's Commercial Revitalization District that can take advantage of the County's revitalization programs if it meets the County revitalization goals and efforts. The project is now submitted for Department's review and approval. The community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: With proposals like Arbutus Station at Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road, "the community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan."

quotes.text: Finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners. Though the community is always looking for prospective homeowners, there is a lack of rental options to attract the UMBC students and programs to benefit both the landlords and student renters. At the same time the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup discussions highlighted the challenge of "finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners," noting that while there is a lack of student rental options, "the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership."
