The vision focuses on revitalizing historic commercial corridors like the Historic Dundalk Town Center, preserving waterfront assets, and providing a range of high-quality, affordable housing to support first-time homebuyers and aging-in-place seniors.
geographic_addresses: 2500 Sparrows Point Road, Dundalk, MD
3447 Dundalk Avenue, Dundalk, MD

quotes.text: Identify potential zoning changes to encourage the development of high-quality, mixed-use development along major corridors in the Dundalk area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To stimulate corridor revitalization, the plan outlines the need to "identify potential zoning changes to encourage the development of high-quality, mixed-use development along major corridors in the Dundalk area."

quotes.text: Barriers to high density, high-quality development (policies, development approval processes)
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planning assessments highlighted regulatory hurdles, noting "barriers to high density, high-quality development" resulting from current policies and development approval processes.

quotes.text: Expand the supply of quality affordable housing for families, first time homebuyers, and disabled and elderly households
quotes.briefing_quote: A primary objective is to "expand the supply of quality affordable housing for families, first time homebuyers, and disabled and elderly households" to support the shifting demographic profile.

quotes.text: Limited flexibility in residential zoning to allow for appropriate small-scale commercial uses to serve the needs of more remote communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes an opportunity to update current frameworks to address "limited flexibility in residential zoning to allow for appropriate small-scale commercial uses to serve the needs of more remote communities."

quotes.text: Develop strategies to identify and actively attract business types that are desired by the community in portions of Dundalk, such as grocery stores, cafes or coffee shops, and restaurants
quotes.briefing_quote: To fill commercial gaps, the workgroup recommended that the County "develop strategies to identify and actively attract business types that are desired by the community in portions of Dundalk, such as grocery stores, cafes or coffee shops, and restaurants."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD
Cowenton Avenue & Pulaski Highway, White Marsh, MD
Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

quotes.text: The redevelopment plan for O'Donnell Heights has been designed as a mixed-use community that includes a range of civic, retail, flex space, and residential uses that will provide a mix of incomes and benefit the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2020 Revitalization Plan establishes that the O'Donnell Heights site will be designed as a mixed-use community that includes a range of civic, retail, flex space, and residential uses to ensure economic diversity and provide direct community benefit.

quotes.text: This area is envisioned to include a variety of townhouses and stacked flats, largely rental with the potential for market-rate, for-sale units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate diverse housing needs, future redevelopment blocks are envisioned to include a variety of townhouses and stacked flats, largely rental with the potential for market-rate, for-sale units.

quotes.text: Holabird Avenue has the opportunity to become a vibrant main street that supports the commercial uses that front along it.
quotes.briefing_quote: Consultants and local business owners emphasize that Holabird Avenue has the opportunity to become a vibrant main street that supports the commercial uses that front along it through streetscape enhancements and consolidated curb cuts.

quotes.text: Building off of the retail amenities along Holabird Avenue, this site is well positioned for uses that require significant parking and provide the community access to fresh foods and essential household items. A small-format grocery and convenience store are ideal tenants for this location.
quotes.briefing_quote: To resolve the food desert challenge, the plan highlights that the vacant Broening Highway site is well positioned for uses that require significant parking and provide the community access to fresh foods and essential household items, making a small-format grocery store an ideal tenant.

quotes.text: As a larger site, the shopping center has the opportunity to integrate a new small-format grocery with adequate parking.
quotes.briefing_quote: At the intersection of O'Donnell Street and Dundalk Avenue, the community identified that the shopping center has the opportunity to integrate a new small-format grocery to upgrade the local retail experience.

plan_quotes.community_vision: A Baltimore of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child has opportunities to thrive no matter what zip code they live in, and residents play an essential role in Baltimore’s thriving future. The community aspires to grow through equitable neighborhood development, sustainable transit-oriented design, economic empowerment of local small businesses, environmental and climate justice, and the active preservation of cultural heritage and neighborhood stability.

145 South Calverton Road, Baltimore, MD

quotes.text: The Fitzgerald apartment building, located at 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue in Mid-Town Belvedere, is an example of a successful Transit Oriented Development project in Baltimore. Built in 2010, adjacent to the Mt. Royal/MICA Light Rail station, the seven-story building has 275 apartment units and two commercial establishments on the lower level
quotes.briefing_quote: A prime example of successful transit-oriented development is the Fitzgerald apartment building, which stands as a seven-story building with 275 apartment units and ground-floor commercial establishments adjacent to the Light Rail, showcasing how dense, mixed-use infill can thrive in Baltimore.

quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. These areas are relatively rich in the resources needed for quality of life and healthy child development, but as a result of a long practice of exclusion, they currently have limited affordable housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To affirmatively further fair housing, the plan emphasizes that in stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed-income developments to reverse long practices of exclusion.

quotes.text: Replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and the vacant former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, new elementary middle school, two new parks, and a renovated and expanded Chick Webb Recreation Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Perkins Somerset Oldtown Transformation Plan represents a massive revitalization effort, replacing obsolete housing with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, and essential community spaces.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. These are largely stable, highly livable, and resilient communities, but unfortunately, they have historically received little benefit from national and local housing policies that have often failed to support the middle class.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing policy experts highlighted the critical need to support middle neighborhoods, noting that these homes generate wealth over generations for families whose future security is tied to their communities' ongoing success.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore City's vision focuses on reversing population decline, eliminating structural racism, and building economic competitiveness. By integrating investments in housing, transit, arts, and green spaces, the city seeks to stabilize middle-market neighborhoods and transform historically disinvested areas into thriving, equitable communities with ample affordable housing and locally-owned commercial opportunities.

quotes.text: Despite gains in income, the City continues to experience a shortage of affordable rental and homeownership units particularly for households earning 50% or less of the Area Median Income (AMI) as determined by the U.S. Department of Housing & Urban Development (HUD).
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Sustainable Communities report underscores that despite general income gains, Baltimore "continues to experience a shortage of affordable rental and homeownership units particularly for households earning 50% or less of the Area Median Income."

quotes.text: Each district’s Main Street program has a different strategy for spurring economic activity, but support may include marketing and event planning, financial assistance for design and promotions, architectural services for facade renovations, streetscape improvements, technical support, access to grants, and more to support the City’s eight (8) Main Street Districts.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize local business hubs, Main Street program strategies include offering "financial assistance for design and promotions, architectural services for facade renovations, and streetscape improvements" to draw in new commercial tenants.

quotes.text: Yard 56, a former industrial site redeveloped as a mixed-use development across from Hopkins Bayview.
quotes.briefing_quote: Opportunity Zone initiatives have catalyzed key transformations, such as "Yard 56, a former industrial site redeveloped as a mixed-use development across from Hopkins Bayview."

quotes.text: To provide safe and decent housing and help owners maintain their housing values, the City and Housing Authority dedicate considerable resources to increasing and preserving its supply of affordable housing for both homeowners and renters.
quotes.briefing_quote: Municipal planners indicated that the city aims to "dedicate considerable resources to increasing and preserving its supply of affordable housing for both homeowners and renters" to stabilize residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Vacant lots and buildings are consolidated to create new mixed-income rental and for-sale housing sites. Abandoned industrial sites are repurposed and frequently leverage additional investment.
quotes.briefing_quote: By optimizing municipal land assets, "vacant lots and buildings are consolidated to create new mixed-income rental and for-sale housing sites" that spark wider neighborhood investment.

quotes.text: This area is envisioned to include a variety of townhouses and stacked flats, largely rental with the potential for market-rate, for-sale units.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

quotes.text: The Fitzgerald apartment building, located at 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue in Mid-Town Belvedere, is an example of a successful Transit Oriented Development project in Baltimore. quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. quotes.briefing_quote: To affirmatively further fair housing, the plan emphasizes that in stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed-income developments to reverse long practices of exclusion.

quotes.text: Replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and the vacant former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, new elementary middle school, two new parks, and a renovated and expanded Chick Webb Recreation Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Perkins Somerset Oldtown Transformation Plan represents a massive revitalization effort, replacing obsolete housing with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, and essential community spaces.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. The vision focuses on revitalizing historic commercial corridors like the Historic Dundalk Town Center, preserving waterfront assets, and providing a range of high-quality, affordable housing to support first-time homebuyers and aging-in-place seniors.
geographic_addresses: 2500 Sparrows Point Road, Dundalk, MD
3447 Dundalk Avenue, Dundalk, MD

quotes.text: Identify potential zoning changes to encourage the development of high-quality, mixed-use development along major corridors in the Dundalk area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To stimulate corridor revitalization, the plan outlines the need to "identify potential zoning changes to encourage the development of high-quality, mixed-use development along major corridors in the Dundalk area."

quotes.text: Barriers to high density, high-quality development (policies, development approval processes)
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planning assessments highlighted regulatory hurdles, noting "barriers to high density, high-quality development" resulting from current policies and development approval processes.

quotes.text: Expand the supply of quality affordable housing for families, first time homebuyers, and disabled and elderly households
quotes.briefing_quote: A primary objective is to "expand the supply of quality affordable housing for families, first time homebuyers, and disabled and elderly households" to support the shifting demographic profile.

quotes.text: Limited flexibility in residential zoning to allow for appropriate small-scale commercial uses to serve the needs of more remote communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes an opportunity to update current frameworks to address "limited flexibility in residential zoning to allow for appropriate small-scale commercial uses to serve the needs of more remote communities."

quotes.text: Develop strategies to identify and actively attract business types that are desired by the community in portions of Dundalk, such as grocery stores, cafes or coffee shops, and restaurants
quotes.briefing_quote: To fill commercial gaps, the workgroup recommended that the County "develop strategies to identify and actively attract business types that are desired by the community in portions of Dundalk, such as grocery stores, cafes or coffee shops, and restaurants."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD
Cowenton Avenue & Pulaski Highway, White Marsh, MD
Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Arbutus aspires to transition into a vibrant "college town" leveraging its proximity to the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) while carefully protecting the area's historic single-family character and small-town charm. The community aims to capitalize on its strategic role as a logistics and technology hub, revitalizing key commercial corridors like East Drive and Linden Avenue with diverse retail, arts, and mixed-use transit-oriented developments that serve residents and students alike.
geographic_addresses: Waelchi Avenue & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Linden Avenue & Shelbourne Road, Arbutus, MD
Shelbourne Road & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Tom Day & Southwestern Boulevard, Arbutus, MD

quotes.text: The proposed Arbutus Station is a mixed-use development by a local developer at the intersection of Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road. It is within the proposed Sustainable Community boundary and the County's Commercial Revitalization District that can take advantage of the County's revitalization programs if it meets the County revitalization goals and efforts. The project is now submitted for Department's review and approval. The community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: With proposals like Arbutus Station at Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road, "the community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan."

quotes.text: Finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners. Though the community is always looking for prospective homeowners, there is a lack of rental options to attract the UMBC students and programs to benefit both the landlords and student renters. At the same time the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup discussions highlighted the challenge of "finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners," noting that while there is a lack of student rental options, "the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership."

quotes.text: Bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques similar to Ellicott City and Catonsville.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local economic strategies emphasize the desire to "bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques" to the commercial district, modeling success after nearby Ellicott City and Catonsville.

quotes.text: Convene group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: To preserve neighborhood character, the plan recommends convening a "group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community."

quotes.text: Obtain funding and acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs and UMBC students.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address community health and quality of life, stakeholders recommend seeking funding to "acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs" and support the growing student population.

community_organizations: Wilkens Police and Community Relations Organization

plan_quotes.community_vision: Cherry Hill envisions a holistic, equitable transformation that improves the quality of life, creates pathways out of poverty, and drives economic development without displacing current residents. By building on its rich legacy, new 21st Century schools, and a strong community fabric, Cherry Hill aims to attract high-quality mixed-income housing, cultivate Black-owned small businesses, introduce a community-owned cooperative grocery, and establish vibrant transit-oriented and mixed-use spaces.
geographic_addresses: Cherry Hill Road & Terra Firma Road, Baltimore, MD
Cherry Hill Road & Seabury Road, Baltimore, MD
Cherry Hill Road & Round Road, Baltimore, MD

Waterview Avenue & Cherry Hill Road, Baltimore, MD

quotes.text: All new rental housing should be mixed-income, meaning that it must be accessible to people making all ranges of income (from no income to unrestricted income). Each new development should be 1/3 low-income units, 1/3 workforce units, and 1/3 units for unrestricted income renters where economically feasible.
quotes.briefing_quote: To promote socioeconomic diversity and inclusivity, the plan stresses that 'all new rental housing should be mixed-income... each new development should be 1/3 low-income units, 1/3 workforce units, and 1/3 units for unrestricted income renters where economically feasible.'

quotes.text: Construct 80-100 units of high-quality, mixed-income rental housing in a 4-story building on the Patapsco School Site
quotes.briefing_quote: The steering committee highlighted an immediate infill residential opportunity to 'construct 80-100 units of high-quality, mixed-income rental housing in a 4-story building on the Patapsco School Site' next to the local school.

quotes.text: Many of the existing rowhouses in Cherry Hill are roughly 750—900 SF and have 2-3 bedrooms, with 1 full bathroom. Families today are looking for 3 and 4-bedrooms with at least 2 to 2.5 bathrooms;... Shorter lengths of rowhouses (duplexes, triplexes, and 4-unit buildings) would help to break up the streets and provide green between the buildings.
quotes.briefing_quote: To mitigate out-migration of families seeking larger spaces, the plan highlights a strong demand for developers to build 'larger houses with contemporary floor plans' featuring three to four bedrooms and multiple bathrooms.

quotes.text: Cherry Hill currently does not have the spending required to support a supermarket and would need to capture additional demand from surrounding areas... The best way to address residents' needs for groceries is to implement a phased approach.
quotes.briefing_quote: Acknowledging that the area's current spending power sits below national grocery chain thresholds, the plan recommends that developers 'attract a small, private grocery chain or family-owned franchise' as part of a phased food security approach.

quotes.text: In the future, a mixed-use Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) neighborhood may be possible next to the existing Cherry Hill Light RailLink station... The TOD would also be an ideal location for mixed-income rental housing, which combines financing sources to create housing for a range of incomes, from low-income to market rate.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning team identified a major opportunity to create a 'vibrant mixed-use Transit-Oriented Development neighborhood next to the existing Cherry Hill Light RailLink station' to integrate higher-density housing and local retail.

Pro Bono Resources Center of Maryland (PBRC)

plan_quotes.community_vision: A Baltimore of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child has opportunities to thrive no matter what zip code they live in, and residents play an essential role in Baltimore’s thriving future. The community aspires to grow through equitable neighborhood development, sustainable transit-oriented design, economic empowerment of local small businesses, environmental and climate justice, and the active preservation of cultural heritage and neighborhood stability.
geographic_addresses: 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue, Baltimore, MD
145 South Calverton Road, Baltimore, MD
1401 East Monument Street, Baltimore, MD
1601 East Lombard Street, Baltimore, MD

quotes.text: The Fitzgerald apartment building, located at 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue in Mid-Town Belvedere, is an example of a successful Transit Oriented Development project in Baltimore. Built in 2010, adjacent to the Mt. Royal/MICA Light Rail station, the seven-story building has 275 apartment units and two commercial establishments on the lower level
quotes.briefing_quote: A prime example of successful transit-oriented development is the Fitzgerald apartment building, which stands as a seven-story building with 275 apartment units and ground-floor commercial establishments adjacent to the Light Rail, showcasing how dense, mixed-use infill can thrive in Baltimore.

quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. These areas are relatively rich in the resources needed for quality of life and healthy child development, but as a result of a long practice of exclusion, they currently have limited affordable housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To affirmatively further fair housing, the plan emphasizes that in stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed-income developments to reverse long practices of exclusion.

quotes.text: Replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and the vacant former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, new elementary middle school, two new parks, and a renovated and expanded Chick Webb Recreation Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Perkins Somerset Oldtown Transformation Plan represents a massive revitalization effort, replacing obsolete housing with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, and essential community spaces.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. These are largely stable, highly livable, and resilient communities, but unfortunately, they have historically received little benefit from national and local housing policies that have often failed to support the middle class.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing policy experts highlighted the critical need to support middle neighborhoods, noting that these homes generate wealth over generations for families whose future security is tied to their communities' ongoing success.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore City's vision focuses on reversing population decline, eliminating structural racism, and building economic competitiveness. By integrating investments in housing, transit, arts, and green spaces, the city seeks to stabilize middle-market neighborhoods and transform historically disinvested areas into thriving, equitable communities with ample affordable housing and locally-owned commercial opportunities.

quotes.text: Despite gains in income, the City continues to experience a shortage of affordable rental and homeownership units particularly for households earning 50% or less of the Area Median Income (AMI) as determined by the U.S. Department of Housing & Urban Development (HUD).
quotes.briefing_quote: The 2023 Sustainable Communities report underscores that despite general income gains, Baltimore "continues to experience a shortage of affordable rental and homeownership units particularly for households earning 50% or less of the Area Median Income."

quotes.text: Each district’s Main Street program has a different strategy for spurring economic activity, but support may include marketing and event planning, financial assistance for design and promotions, architectural services for facade renovations, streetscape improvements, technical support, access to grants, and more to support the City’s eight (8) Main Street Districts.
quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize local business hubs, Main Street program strategies include offering "financial assistance for design and promotions, architectural services for facade renovations, and streetscape improvements" to draw in new commercial tenants.

quotes.text: Yard 56, a former industrial site redeveloped as a mixed-use development across from Hopkins Bayview.
quotes.briefing_quote: Opportunity Zone initiatives have catalyzed key transformations, such as "Yard 56, a former industrial site redeveloped as a mixed-use development across from Hopkins Bayview."

quotes.text: To provide safe and decent housing and help owners maintain their housing values, the City and Housing Authority dedicate considerable resources to increasing and preserving its supply of affordable housing for both homeowners and renters.
quotes.briefing_quote: Municipal planners indicated that the city aims to "dedicate considerable resources to increasing and preserving its supply of affordable housing for both homeowners and renters" to stabilize residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Vacant lots and buildings are consolidated to create new mixed-income rental and for-sale housing sites. Abandoned industrial sites are repurposed and frequently leverage additional investment.
quotes.briefing_quote: By optimizing municipal land assets, "vacant lots and buildings are consolidated to create new mixed-income rental and for-sale housing sites" that spark wider neighborhood investment.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community where residents enjoy a top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, and innovative businesses. The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.
geographic_addresses: Frederick Road & Triadelphia Road, Ellicott City, MD
Broken Land Parkway & Snowden River Parkway, Columbia, MD
Woodland Road & Route 108, Ellicott City, MD
Sanner Road & Johns Hopkins Road, Clarksville, MD
Snowden River Parkway & Oakland Mills Road, Columbia, MD

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

quotes.text: The Warfield Complex is a de-accessioned 140-acre portion of the historic Springfield State Hospital, lying at the Town's eastern boundary... The Town and Warfield Development Corporation purchased the site from the state and then sold it to an LLC as an ongoing economic development project, intended to become a major job center by reusing the historic buildings as offices and commercial establishments.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights the 140-acre historic Warfield Complex as a major opportunity for reuse, noting that the ongoing redevelopment is "intended to become a major job center by reusing the historic buildings as offices and commercial establishments" alongside residential integration.

quotes.text: Near completion of the Parkside at Warfield housing development. Once complete, this project will have created 145+ new townhouse style homes to help meet the growing demand of residential housing in the Sykesville area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address growing local housing demands, the town celebrated the "creation of 145+ new townhouse style homes" in the Parkside at Warfield development, expanding the local housing options.

quotes.text: The Planned Employment Center (PEC) zone was created to facilitate the growth of a whole new development in Sykesville at the historic Warfield property. This zone is intended to create a new business district within the Sykesville limits and allow for a multitude of mixed uses including retail and residential.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Town established a Planned Employment Center zone at the historic Warfield property, designed to "create a new business district... and allow for a multitude of mixed uses including retail and residential."

quotes.text: Downtown zoning needs updating to reflect the high-density development currently found there and encourage more economically feasible development
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies a key regulatory opportunity, stating that "downtown zoning needs updating to reflect the high-density development currently found there and encourage more economically feasible development."

quotes.text: Explore the provision of Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) to create smaller, independent, residential dwelling units located on the same lot as a single-family home.
quotes.briefing_quote: To diversify housing types on existing land, the Town aims to "explore the provision of Accessory Dwelling Units to create smaller, independent, residential dwelling units located on the same lot as a single-family home."

quotes.text: Promote the construction and conversion of existing housing into attached or multi-unit housing to provide more selection by offering smaller efficiency units at a lower price point.
quotes.briefing_quote: To expand affordable options on built-out land, the Town proposes to "promote the construction and conversion of existing housing into attached or multi-unit housing" to offer smaller, cost-effective efficiency units.

quotes.text: Infill at the old carriage house location on Main Street to create additional retail and residential space in the Downtown area.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan showcases successful historic infill development, pointing to the "old carriage house location on Main Street to create additional retail and residential space in the Downtown area."

quotes.text: The developers of the historic Warfield property are unsatisfied with the zoning text for the Planned Employment Center that they agreed to build and progress on certain aspects of the project are stalled while the issues get worked out.
quotes.briefing_quote: While the Warfield site holds immense promise, developers have noted that "progress on certain aspects of the project are stalled while issues get worked out" regarding the Planned Employment Center zoning text, highlighting an opportunity for collaborative zoning refinements.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Town of Sykesville envisions a sustainable, vibrant, and accessible future that honors its rich historic heritage while fostering smart economic growth. By enhancing the historic Downtown and Main Street as a high-quality small-town center, executing successful mixed-use redevelopments like the Warfield Complex, expanding multi-modal trails and sidewalk connectivity, and maintaining robust environmental stewardship, Sykesville aspires to cultivate an inclusive, highly connected, and economically resilient community for residents and visitors alike.

quotes.text: Generally, however, this Plan recognizes that the Town should consider flexibility on future land development submissions to ultimately achieve a mixed-use development which can be defined more specifically during the Town's potential zoning rewrite.

quotes.text: The need for mixed-use development is supported by a Town commissioned economic and fiscal impact study of the Warfield development. The 2020 Sage Policy Group study shows demand for market-rate housing, driven by the Millennial generation that is shifting from apartments to owner-occupied housing as they begin to form families.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local economic study emphasized the opportunity for new housing types, showing "demand for market-rate housing, driven by the Millennial generation that is shifting from apartments to owner-occupied housing" as they grow and form families.

quotes.text: Given the built-out nature of Sykesville, allowing ADUs offers an opportunity for the addition of smaller efficiency units that are more affordable in nature than detached single family homes.
quotes.briefing_quote: Addressing the limited space for expansion, planning narratives suggest that "allowing Accessory Dwelling Units offers an opportunity for the addition of smaller efficiency units that are more affordable in nature" than traditional single-family homes.

quotes.text: To facilitate the development of a diverse housing stock, new or redeveloped residential projects should include low-income housing defined as housing units in which the sale or lease of the dwelling is limited to households earning up to 120% of median income.
quotes.briefing_quote: To foster an inclusive environment, the plan recommends that "new or redeveloped residential projects should include low-income housing" to sustain options for people of all incomes.

quotes.text: Promoting the construction and conversion of housing to 1-unit attached and 2 or more units would provide more housing selection by offering smaller efficiency units that may be offered at a lower price point.
quotes.briefing_quote: To expand housing choices, the plan encourages "promoting the construction and conversion of housing to 1-unit attached and 2 or more units" to provide lower-cost efficiency options.

quotes.text: As new retail storefronts and second floor efficiency housing units expand along Sandosky Road, the distance between the hilltop and Downtown becomes much shorter.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community plans suggest that integrating "new retail storefronts and second floor efficiency housing units expand along Sandosky Road" will physically and socially bridge the hilltop area with Downtown.

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.
quotes.briefing_quote: Community feedback strongly prioritized the need to "protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment" by limiting new development within existing residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan outlines a key policy to "work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization."

quotes.text: The Corridor Activity Center (CAC) and Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Zoning Districts, while intended to provide a mix of uses, have primarily yielded high-density residential development with limited nonresidential (retail) in some locations
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that while designated activity centers and transit districts are designed for a mix of uses, they "have primarily yielded high-density residential development with limited nonresidential" retail, creating an opportunity for future developers to deliver more balanced commercial and community spaces.

quotes.text: Allow the development of residential and hotels within the transit oriented development areas to support nonresidential uses, such as office, retail, and entertainment, and increased MARC ridership.
quotes.briefing_quote: To build vibrant station areas, local guidelines recommend that planners "allow the development of residential and hotels within the transit oriented development areas to support nonresidential uses" like office, retail, and entertainment.

quotes.text: Allow sufficient residential densities in North Laurel District—defined in HoCo By Design as an area that will build on the existing transit-oriented community with an entertainment focus that both serves the needs of existing and future residents and offers a destination for neighboring communities-- to make a wide range of uses economically viable, including convenience retail and other neighborhood-serving amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To stimulate local economic activity, the plan advocates to "allow sufficient residential densities in North Laurel District... to make a wide range of uses economically viable," including convenience retail and other neighborhood-serving amenities.

quotes.text: Persistent high vacancy rates for ground floor retail in recent mixed-use developments on Route 1
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies a clear need to address "persistent high vacancy rates for ground floor retail in recent mixed-use developments on Route 1" by introducing more flexible zoning and economic incentives.

quotes.text: Reduction in older, smaller, more affordable single family housing units through demolition and substantial renovations that results in an increased resale value
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing analysis highlights a challenge in entry-level homeownership due to a "reduction in older, smaller, more affordable single family housing units through demolition and substantial renovations" that drive up area housing prices.

quotes.text: Aging multi-family housing stock is in need of redevelopment or upgrades. The SC area has 9% of units that were built before 1970 and 73% of units that were built before 2000 according to Howard County’s Housing Opportunities Master Plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: Data indicates that the local "aging multi-family housing stock is in need of redevelopment or upgrades," with 73 percent of multi-family units in the Sustainable Community Area originally constructed before the year 2000.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

quotes.text: There is currently an affordable housing proposal within the Pikesville CRD that is requesting rezoning to support multi-family apartments.

quotes.text: There has not been demolition of blighted properties in the area. However, there is an interest from the County to assemble vacant commercial properties on Liberty Rd to assist CDCs in redevelopment. In addition, there is discussion to redevelop the old International House of Pancakes and Bennigan's restaurants located in front of Security Square mall.
quotes.briefing_quote: The county is looking to assemble vacant commercial properties along Liberty Road to assist community development corporations in redevelopment, with further discussions centered on redeveloping the former restaurant sites in front of Security Square Mall.

quotes.text: Expand full spectrum housing for residents at diverse income levels and life stages and for individuals with disabilities by encouraging high quality mixed income, multigenerational developments. Promote Housing Accessibility Modification programs to make housing more accessible. quotes.briefing_quote: Planning guidelines emphasize the need to encourage high-quality mixed-income, multigenerational developments while supporting smart growth policies such as mixed-use and Traditional Neighborhood Development.

quotes.text: Some homes in Colonial Village have been improved. There are homes in the Pikesville area that have gone through the zoning petition process for additions. quotes.text: Lack of quality retail and chain restaurants in the Liberty Rd CRD... Lack of variety of businesses to meet the needs of the community... Abundance of unwanted businesses... Businesses closing and vacant gas stations are an eyesore to the residents

plan_quotes.community_vision: Howard County is a welcoming and inclusive community where residents enjoy a top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, and innovative businesses. The collective vision is to accommodate future growth through compact, sustainable redevelopment in targeted activity centers while protecting the County's agricultural heritage, historic communities, and natural resources.

quotes.text: The FLUM focuses new growth into redevelopment areas, which account for approximately 1.5% of the County's already-developed land. This approach addresses high demand for housing and commercial growth.
quotes.briefing_quote: To sustainably manage growth, the plan targets redevelopment on just 1.5% of the County's developed land to balance housing and commercial demands.

quotes.text: Pedestrian safety must be improved—I keep seeing pedestrians walking down the middle of Broken Land or Snowden because there’s no reasonable public transit or walking paths for them to safely get where they’re going.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local workshop participant emphasized that pedestrian safety must be improved on Broken Land Parkway and Snowden River Parkway by providing better walking paths and transit options.

quotes.text: Boosting commercial-base development is one of the most promising strategies to help rebalance the expenditure needs and fiscal resources. The County should continue to build on its current strengths in developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to promote, retain, and expand its commercial base.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Spending Affordability Advisory Committee emphasized that boosting commercial-base development is critical to balancing the County's long-term fiscal resources.

quotes.text: The concept of missing middle housing is referenced throughout the Plan. It is a housing strategy that is intended to create more diverse housing opportunities for our increasingly socioeconomically diverse County.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan promotes missing middle housing to create more diverse housing opportunities that remain compatible in scale with surrounding neighborhoods.

quotes.text: Many developed areas of Howard County are zoned for single-family detached homes. Some of these neighborhoods include homes on larger lots that could, under existing zoning regulations, be further subdivided into one or more additional lots to accommodate a separate home (or homes) of similar size alongside the existing residence.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan identifies potential for modest single-family infill, noting some neighborhoods could be further subdivided under existing zoning to add homes of similar size.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Catonsville-Patapsco community envisions a sustainable, well-connected, and culturally vibrant future. Key aspirations include expanding the local arts ecosystem through the newly designated Catonsville Arts and Entertainment District along Frederick Road, improving active transportation and trail connectivity via groups like Catonsville Rails to Trails, and preserving watershed resources near Patapsco Valley State Park. The community aims to revitalize legacy neighborhoods, address commercial vacancies, and expand quality housing choices—including affordable housing partnerships and accessory dwelling units (ADUs)—while navigating existing low-density zoning constraints that historically limit larger-scale infill development.
geographic_addresses: Ingleside Ave & Edmondson Ave, Catonsville, MD
Ingleside Ave & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD

S. Paradise Ave & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD
Mellor Ave & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD
Winters Lane & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD

quotes.text: Scarcity of undeveloped properties within residential and commercial zones, thereby limiting the potential for larger scale new development or infill
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes a 'scarcity of undeveloped properties within residential and commercial zones, thereby limiting the potential for larger-scale new development or infill,' highlighting the critical importance of strategic infill projects.

quotes.text: Barriers to higher density development (including policies, development process, NIMBYs).
quotes.briefing_quote: The assessment identifies clear 'barriers to higher density development (including policies, development process, NIMBYs)' that must be navigated to successfully introduce multi-family and mixed-use options.

quotes.text: The majority of zoning in the Catonsville SC area is low density residential, that primarily supports single family development. ... The current residential zoning in the majority of the SC Area does not easily support higher density development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning staff emphasized that 'the majority of zoning in the Catonsville Sustainable Community Area is low density residential, which primarily supports single family development' and does not easily accommodate higher density development styles.

quotes.text: Zoning changes occur through the County’s CZMP process... several of these requests for change were denied, though a few were approved to allow for mixed uses along MD 144.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recent comprehensive zoning reviews show progress, noting that while some requests were denied, 'a few were approved to allow for mixed uses along MD 144' to align with main street commercial revitalization goals.

quotes.text: Support the development of new accessory dwelling units (ADUs) within appropriate settings within the SC area through the development process and policy development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community intends to 'support the development of new accessory dwelling units (ADUs) within appropriate settings within the Sustainable Community Area through the development process and policy development' to broaden localized residential choices.

community_organizations: Catonsville, Arbutus, and Edmondson-Westview Recreation Councils

plan_quotes.community_vision: Ellicott City aspires to preserve its unique historic character and environmental setting while systematically mitigating severe flood risks along its core watershed. The community seeks to revitalize its historic Main Street and West End through creative economic development, adaptive reuse of public assets like the historic courthouse, and environmentally sustainable infill developments like mixed-income housing, balancing heritage preservation with modern climate resilience.

3430 Court House Drive, Ellicott City, MD
Fels Lane & Main Street, Ellicott City, MD

quotes.text: Explore opportunities for in-town residential uses within the walkable core. Residential use is essential for an authentic and vibrant walkable community.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes that planning officials should "explore opportunities for in-town residential uses within the walkable core" because "residential use is essential for an authentic and vibrant walkable community."

quotes.text: Burgess Mill Station II is one of the largest infill developments in the SC area. The Burgess Mill project added a 53-home mixed-income apartment option for prospective residents on the south side of Ellicott Mills Drive and the Station II just around the corner off Fels Lane.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights successful local housing models, noting that "Burgess Mill Station II is one of the largest infill developments in the Sustainable Community area," which successfully "added a 53-home mixed-income apartment option for prospective residents."

quotes.text: Housing affordability remains a challenge in the sustainable community and across the region. Steep elevations and lack of available land for greenfield development limits future infill development opportunities.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recognizing geographic and regulatory constraints, the plan notes that "housing affordability remains a challenge" in Ellicott City, where "steep elevations and lack of available land for greenfield development limits future infill development opportunities"—presenting a critical opportunity for creative, well-designed pocket developments.

quotes.text: The Department of Public Works has petitioned the Zoning Board to rezone the now-vacant Historic Courthouse and associated properties from Historic Office (HO) to Historic Commercial (HC) to encourage a range of possible reuse opportunities.
quotes.briefing_quote: To spur economic vitality, the plan details that the county petitioned to "rezone the now-vacant Historic Courthouse and associated properties from Historic Office to Historic Commercial" to actively encourage a flexible range of possible adaptive reuse opportunities.

quotes.text: While a variety of uses could be considered for the property, they should be determined as part of the disposition process, based upon market conditions and feasibility. Proposed uses should be complementary to the Main Street business community, and the form of new structures should be sensitive to the historic district. The process to create the ECMP included unique hotel/accommodations, apartments, office space and/or business incubator space.
quotes.briefing_quote: For the redevelopment of the prominent Courthouse site, the plan advises that "proposed uses should be complementary to the Main Street business community, and the form of new structures should be sensitive to the historic district," with prior community planning processes for the Ellicott City Watershed Master Plan identifying "unique hotel/accommodations, apartments, office space and/or business incubator space" as desired options.

quotes.text: Explore the opportunity for a food hall or creative food establishment within the core, as the market study indicates that opportunities for food-related retail is significant.
quotes.briefing_quote: In seeking to expand the district's retail mix, planning documents urge developers to "explore the opportunity for a food hall or creative food establishment within the core," driven by market research indicating that "opportunities for food-related retail is significant."

plan_quotes.community_vision: Anne Arundel County envisions a future where it embraces its rich Chesapeake culture, heritage, and invaluable ecosystems while directing growth toward smart, green, and equitable development. Under this vision, future development will increasingly focus on mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects on previously developed sites, guiding new investment and redevelopment to older commercial corridors while preserving the unique character of existing low-density neighborhoods, waterfront communities, and agricultural lands.

B&A Blvd & 8th Avenue, Glen Burnie, MD

quotes.text: Development will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites. Development projects will incorporate resilient, sustainable design that demonstrates efficient use of available resources and services throughout the County. Smart growth will be encouraged in areas with existing infrastructure and redevelopment directed to older commercial corridors.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community's vision emphasizes that future development "will increasingly be mixed-use, mixed-income, and transit-oriented projects in previously developed sites" with smart growth directed toward older commercial corridors and existing infrastructure.

quotes.text: To date, 63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings. Current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land in the County. To provide a greater choice of housing for everyone throughout the County, strategies should be developed to address housing inequity and promote diversity in our communities.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes that "63 percent of houses in Anne Arundel County are single-family detached dwellings" and "current zoning allows multifamily apartments and condominiums in only 8 percent of the land," highlighting a major opportunity to develop diversified housing strategies to address inequity.

quotes.text: Redevelopment and Revitalization: Redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: During public forums, community members expressed a strong preference to "redevelop vacant and underutilized properties, like struggling malls, shopping centers, and offices rather than expanding development into undeveloped properties and rural areas."

quotes.text: Increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live and offer amenities like restaurants, shopping, and recreation
quotes.briefing_quote: Market analysis identifies a major opportunity in the "increased market demand for mixed-use developments that provide opportunities to work near where you live" and offer integrated community amenities.

quotes.text: Limit Development in Existing Residential Neighborhoods: Protect the physical character and respect the limitations of infrastructure, public services, and natural environment.

quotes.text: Work with developers to provide the full spectrum of rental and ownership housing choices for all incomes, ages, and abilities, especially in areas designated for increased density and revitalization.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.
