plan_quotes.community_vision: Arbutus aspires to transition into a vibrant "college town" leveraging its proximity to the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) while carefully protecting the area's historic single-family character and small-town charm. The community aims to capitalize on its strategic role as a logistics and technology hub, revitalizing key commercial corridors like East Drive and Linden Avenue with diverse retail, arts, and mixed-use transit-oriented developments that serve residents and students alike.
geographic_addresses: Waelchi Avenue & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Linden Avenue & Shelbourne Road, Arbutus, MD
Shelbourne Road & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Tom Day & Southwestern Boulevard, Arbutus, MD

quotes.text: The proposed Arbutus Station is a mixed-use development by a local developer at the intersection of Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road. It is within the proposed Sustainable Community boundary and the County's Commercial Revitalization District that can take advantage of the County's revitalization programs if it meets the County revitalization goals and efforts. The project is now submitted for Department's review and approval. The community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: With proposals like Arbutus Station at Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road, "the community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan."

quotes.text: Finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners. Though the community is always looking for prospective homeowners, there is a lack of rental options to attract the UMBC students and programs to benefit both the landlords and student renters. At the same time the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup discussions highlighted the challenge of "finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners," noting that while there is a lack of student rental options, "the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership."

quotes.text: Bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques similar to Ellicott City and Catonsville.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local economic strategies emphasize the desire to "bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques" to the commercial district, modeling success after nearby Ellicott City and Catonsville.

quotes.text: Convene group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: To preserve neighborhood character, the plan recommends convening a "group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community."

quotes.text: Obtain funding and acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs and UMBC students.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address community health and quality of life, stakeholders recommend seeking funding to "acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs" and support the growing student population.

community_organizations: Wilkens Police and Community Relations Organization

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Catonsville-Patapsco community envisions a sustainable, well-connected, and culturally vibrant future. Key aspirations include expanding the local arts ecosystem through the newly designated Catonsville Arts and Entertainment District along Frederick Road, improving active transportation and trail connectivity via groups like Catonsville Rails to Trails, and preserving watershed resources near Patapsco Valley State Park. The community aims to revitalize legacy neighborhoods, address commercial vacancies, and expand quality housing choices—including affordable housing partnerships and accessory dwelling units (ADUs)—while navigating existing low-density zoning constraints that historically limit larger-scale infill development.
geographic_addresses: Ingleside Ave & Edmondson Ave, Catonsville, MD
Ingleside Ave & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD
Maidens Choice Lane & Kenwood Ave, Catonsville, MD
S. Paradise Ave & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD
Mellor Ave & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD
Winters Lane & Frederick Rd, Catonsville, MD

quotes.text: Scarcity of undeveloped properties within residential and commercial zones, thereby limiting the potential for larger scale new development or infill
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan notes a 'scarcity of undeveloped properties within residential and commercial zones, thereby limiting the potential for larger-scale new development or infill,' highlighting the critical importance of strategic infill projects.

quotes.text: Barriers to higher density development (including policies, development process, NIMBYs).
quotes.briefing_quote: The assessment identifies clear 'barriers to higher density development (including policies, development process, NIMBYs)' that must be navigated to successfully introduce multi-family and mixed-use options.

quotes.text: The majority of zoning in the Catonsville SC area is low density residential, that primarily supports single family development. ... The current residential zoning in the majority of the SC Area does not easily support higher density development.
quotes.briefing_quote: Planning staff emphasized that 'the majority of zoning in the Catonsville Sustainable Community Area is low density residential, which primarily supports single family development' and does not easily accommodate higher density development styles.

quotes.text: Zoning changes occur through the County’s CZMP process... several of these requests for change were denied, though a few were approved to allow for mixed uses along MD 144.
quotes.briefing_quote: Recent comprehensive zoning reviews show progress, noting that while some requests were denied, 'a few were approved to allow for mixed uses along MD 144' to align with main street commercial revitalization goals.

quotes.text: Support the development of new accessory dwelling units (ADUs) within appropriate settings within the SC area through the development process and policy development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The community intends to 'support the development of new accessory dwelling units (ADUs) within appropriate settings within the Sustainable Community Area through the development process and policy development' to broaden localized residential choices.

quotes.text: It is the County's intent that remaining un-allocated sewer capacity should be reserved for commercial uses, directing any new residential development to the incorporated towns that have capacity to accommodate it. quotes.text: Harford Ave. between Federal and Biddle Street, (Mixed-use Residential/Multi-Family Housing/ Commercial) to feature a few mid-rise mixed-use multifamily buildings with ground-floor retail that can support a grocery store or smaller businesses such as coffee shops, apparel, bank, nail salons, etc. with a minimum of 85% of the units being market rate

quotes.text: All single family infill (new construction) should not exceed three stories and, while not yet officially designated as a CHAP district, should generally attempt to align to the design standards presented in the City's CHAP guidelines to best protect the historic character of Oliver.

quotes.text: The high concentration of vacant land in this focus area holds Oliver’s best potential to attract multi-family development consistent with underlying zoning into the community.

quotes.text: Current zoning in Oliver makes it challenging for development to be concentrated and responsive to community needs and desires. To support continued investment and development for small businesses and renovations that strengthen the fabric of the community, zoning practices will need to be re-considered.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local development partner ReBUILD Metro pointed out that "current zoning in Oliver makes it challenging for development to be concentrated and responsive to community needs," indicating a vital opportunity for zoning realignment to foster neighborhood-serving storefronts.

quotes.text: I hope that Oliver is a thriving neighborhood. As a native Baltimorean that recently returned to invest in the city, I chose this neighborhood but sometimes have regrets. I love my property but the neighborhood feels stagnant. There doesn’t appear to be a plan, but spotty investment that feels disconnected. Given its location to a major hub like JHH and downtown the neighborhood has potential yet its unrealized.
quotes.briefing_quote: A returning native resident highlighted the gap between hope and reality, stating that while they love their property, "the neighborhood feels stagnant" with disconnected investments, emphasizing that its proximity to downtown and major employment hubs represents major "unrealized potential."

Laurel aims to deliver a diverse and affordable housing stock, enhance multimodal transit connections (such as transit-oriented development near the MARC station), and foster inclusive public spaces that support a high quality of life for multi-generational residents.

quotes.text: LAUREL MARC - TRANSIT ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT. Located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space. The building is planned in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Transportation.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights a premier transit-oriented opportunity at the Laurel MARC station, noting that 'located at Main Street and U.S. Route One Northbound, the development will consist of a multifamily building, with limited retail space' coordinated alongside state transit partners.

quotes.text: ANDERSON’S CORNER. A mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex known as Avalon Bay (constructed), an approved 55-unit townhouse community entitled Avery Place and a Royal Farms gas station and convenience store.
quotes.briefing_quote: Anderson's Corner serves as a successful template for mixed-density development, showcasing 'a mixed-use community consisting of a 344-unit apartment complex, an approved 55-unit townhouse community... and a Royal Farms' convenience center.

quotes.text: WEST SIDE. A mixed-use community consisting of a 469-unit apartment complex known as Modera at Westside (constructed) and 56-unit townhouse community, which is complete. The site also has other undeveloped parcels for commercial, a hotel and a second phase townhouse development.
quotes.briefing_quote: The West Side master-planned area illustrates the demand for integrated density, featuring 'a 469-unit apartment complex... and a 56-unit townhouse community' alongside undeveloped parcels reserved for commercial space and a hotel.

quotes.text: PATUXENT GREENS GOLF COURSE. The golf course closed in December 2018. The property was approved to be re-developed into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units. The development will also include a clubhouse, swimming pool, hiker/biker trails and other community amenities.
quotes.briefing_quote: Following the transition of local recreational lands, the City approved plans for Patuxent Greens 'to be redeveloped into a residential community consisting of 389 single-family and townhouse dwelling units' paired with extensive walkable amenities.

quotes.text: Per the City of Laurel Unified Development Code, any multifamily development of 100 dwelling units or more approved after November 23, 2020, shall include a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as work force housing units, a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as moderately priced housing units and a minimum of four (4) percent of the total number of apartments as age-restricted housing units.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to transition from a suburban bedroom community into an interconnected, economically competitive, and racially integrated jurisdiction. The county's vision centers on compact, corridor-focused development that fosters walkable 'Complete Communities' and '15-minute living' while preserving its Agricultural Reserve. The plan prioritizes addressing historical racial and economic inequities, improving environmental resilience, and integrating design, arts, and culture into the daily lives of all residents.
geographic_addresses: 2425 Reedie Drive, Wheaton, MD
Connecticut Avenue & Manor Road, Kensington, MD
University Boulevard & New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD
Seven Locks Road & River Road, Bethesda, MD

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: Can't take my ladder on the Purple Line.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local working-class resident cautioned planners about transit-focused changes, stating, 'Can’t take my ladder on the Purple Line,' illustrating the critical need to preserve vehicle-accessible corridors and parking for service providers.

community_organizations: Arts & Humanities Council of Montgomery County

quotes.text: Given that most new residential growth in the city will come in the form of multiple unit residential buildings, as apartments or condominiums, and that not all locations are appropriate for mixed-use development, Rockville needs a higher density residential zone.
quotes.briefing_quote: To accommodate evolving multi-family housing demands, the plan notes that "most new residential growth in the city will come in the form of multiple unit residential buildings, as apartments or condominiums, and that not all locations are appropriate for mixed-use development, Rockville needs a higher density residential zone."

quotes.text: One way to accommodate more affordable housing options, flexible space for an office or shared family living arrangements, and financial assistance for current homeowners, while maintaining the city’s predominantly residential character, is with accessory apartments and accessory dwelling units.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address affordability while maintaining neighborhood fabric, the plan highlights that "one way to accommodate more affordable housing options, flexible space for an office or shared family living arrangements, and financial assistance for current homeowners, while maintaining the city’s predominantly residential character, is with accessory apartments and accessory dwelling units."

quotes.text: Steady additions of commercial and amenity space on the ground floor of new buildings bring the opportunity for new shops and restaurants, supported by new residential units and offices on upper floors. quotes.text: In 2010 the City of Mount Rainier purchased underutilized and abandoned properties and combined them into a parcel on 3200 Rhode Island Avenue and Eastern Avenue, the Washington DC borderline. quotes.text: The Singer Building, a long vacant historic landmark on Rhode Island Ave at Perry Street has been completely renovated by The Menkiti Group and is open for business. The mixed-use development has 12 residential units (fully leased) and 3 new business establishments operating within 10,000 sq. ft. of retail space.

[into a] mixed-use development with 12 residential units (fully leased) and 3 new business establishments."

quotes.text: The expansion of housing choice in the Mount Rainier Community is designed to be located in the MUTC where the city currently owns property. quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan highlights that dedicating more than one-third of the county to exclusive single-family zoning left many neighborhoods isolated, signaling a key opportunity to introduce missing middle housing and mixed-use options that better connect residents to daily amenities.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support a growing workforce, planning officials recommend concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors to keep housing attainable, improve transit access, and avoid displacement.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.
quotes.briefing_quote: The document notes that aging suburban office parks can be successfully repositioned through infill and redevelopment to integrate housing, retail, and public spaces, creating the vibrant mixed-use environments that modern employers and residents seek.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.
quotes.briefing_quote: The plan emphasizes the value of adding 'Missing Middle' housing types to more neighborhoods—including duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes—to expand residential choice, build social capital, and facilitate aging in place.

quotes.text: The establishment of the residential wedge consigned more than one-third of the county to zoning exclusively for single-family homes, leaving many of our neighborhoods reliant on automobiles and disconnected from many amenities and services.

quotes.text: By concentrating more housing of different sizes and types near high-quality transit corridors, we can provide housing that will help keep the most productive workers in the county, curb escalating prices in the most desirable locations, and improve accessibility of jobs, transportation, and services while being mindful not to displace current residents.

quotes.text: Existing suburban office parks in locations such as Rock Spring or Clarksburg’s COMSAT site have large existing buildings that can accommodate employment but lack the integration of uses, services, and amenities necessary to succeed in an increasingly competitive office market.

quotes.text: Adding more 'Missing Middle' housing types – ranging from low to medium densities such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs); duplexes; triplexes; quadplexes; live-work units; and clustered housing such as townhouses, courtyard dwellings and smaller apartment buildings to more neighborhoods is intended to provide more choice, enhance intergenerational interaction, promote aging in place, and build social capital.

The community seeks to revitalize its commercial districts—especially the International Corridor—through denser, mixed-use development, streetscape beautification, and creative placemaking. Addressing persistent infrastructure and social challenges, the plan aims to improve pedestrian and bicycle safety, modernize aging multifamily rental housing, preserve environmental assets like the Northwest Branch Trail, and elevate the quality of life through enhanced health, language, and youth recreation services.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Essex aims to leverage its rich maritime history and waterfront assets while revitalizing its commercial corridors along Eastern Boulevard and Back River Neck Road. The community envisions a vibrant, walkable, and transit-oriented destination with a diverse housing stock that supports first-time homebuyers and seniors, enhanced green spaces and water quality, and mixed-use developments that drive economic growth and reduce commercial vacancies. By engaging a robust network of civic associations, local businesses, and government agencies, Essex seeks to foster community pride and sustainable development.

quotes.text: Encourage redevelopment of parcels in commercial corridor with financial incentives to support increased density, workforce housing, and/or mixed-use with housing above retail. This could include a limited number of units reserved for unhoused people.

quotes.text: Open space is being filled up with townhomes and other new development, making this area too congested and overcrowded, especially in the Back River Neck Area.

quotes.text: High commercial turnover resulting in a large number of vacant properties and storefronts along commercial corridor.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The Greater Dundalk/Sparrows Point community envisions a multi-year revitalization strategy focused on increasing economic vitality, expanding environmental resilience, and improving community livability. By leveraging its powerful industrial and deep-water assets like Tradepoint Atlantic and the Port of Baltimore, the community aims to create permanent jobs, expand workforce training, and enhance housing quality. The vision focuses on revitalizing historic commercial corridors like the Historic Dundalk Town Center, preserving waterfront assets, and providing a range of high-quality, affordable housing to support first-time homebuyers and aging-in-place seniors.

3447 Dundalk Avenue, Dundalk, MD

quotes.text: Identify potential zoning changes to encourage the development of high-quality, mixed-use development along major corridors in the Dundalk area.
quotes.briefing_quote: To stimulate corridor revitalization, the plan outlines the need to "identify potential zoning changes to encourage the development of high-quality, mixed-use development along major corridors in the Dundalk area."

quotes.text: Barriers to high density, high-quality development (policies, development approval processes)
quotes.briefing_quote: Local planning assessments highlighted regulatory hurdles, noting "barriers to high density, high-quality development" resulting from current policies and development approval processes.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

The community aspires to grow through equitable neighborhood development, sustainable transit-oriented design, economic empowerment of local small businesses, environmental and climate justice, and the active preservation of cultural heritage and neighborhood stability.

quotes.text: The Fitzgerald apartment building, located at 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue in Mid-Town Belvedere, is an example of a successful Transit Oriented Development project in Baltimore. Built in 2010, adjacent to the Mt. Royal/MICA Light Rail station, the seven-story building has 275 apartment units and two commercial establishments on the lower level
quotes.briefing_quote: A prime example of successful transit-oriented development is the Fitzgerald apartment building, which stands as a seven-story building with 275 apartment units and ground-floor commercial establishments adjacent to the Light Rail, showcasing how dense, mixed-use infill can thrive in Baltimore.

quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. These areas are relatively rich in the resources needed for quality of life and healthy child development, but as a result of a long practice of exclusion, they currently have limited affordable housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To affirmatively further fair housing, the plan emphasizes that in stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed-income developments to reverse long practices of exclusion.

quotes.text: Replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and the vacant former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, new elementary middle school, two new parks, and a renovated and expanded Chick Webb Recreation Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Perkins Somerset Oldtown Transformation Plan represents a massive revitalization effort, replacing obsolete housing with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, and essential community spaces.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. These are largely stable, highly livable, and resilient communities, but unfortunately, they have historically received little benefit from national and local housing policies that have often failed to support the middle class.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing policy experts highlighted the critical need to support middle neighborhoods, noting that these homes generate wealth over generations for families whose future security is tied to their communities' ongoing success.

quotes.text: To provide safe and decent housing and help owners maintain their housing values, the City and Housing Authority dedicate considerable resources to increasing and preserving its supply of affordable housing for both homeowners and renters.

This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Arbutus aspires to transition into a vibrant "college town" leveraging its proximity to the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) while carefully protecting the area's historic single-family character and small-town charm. The community aims to capitalize on its strategic role as a logistics and technology hub, revitalizing key commercial corridors like East Drive and Linden Avenue with diverse retail, arts, and mixed-use transit-oriented developments that serve residents and students alike.
geographic_addresses: Waelchi Avenue & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Linden Avenue & Shelbourne Road, Arbutus, MD
Shelbourne Road & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Tom Day & Southwestern Boulevard, Arbutus, MD

quotes.text: The proposed Arbutus Station is a mixed-use development by a local developer at the intersection of Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road. It is within the proposed Sustainable Community boundary and the County's Commercial Revitalization District that can take advantage of the County's revitalization programs if it meets the County revitalization goals and efforts. The project is now submitted for Department's review and approval. The community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: With proposals like Arbutus Station at Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road, "the community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan."

quotes.text: Finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners. Though the community is always looking for prospective homeowners, there is a lack of rental options to attract the UMBC students and programs to benefit both the landlords and student renters. At the same time the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup discussions highlighted the challenge of "finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners," noting that while there is a lack of student rental options, "the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership."

quotes.text: Bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques similar to Ellicott City and Catonsville.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local economic strategies emphasize the desire to "bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques" to the commercial district, modeling success after nearby Ellicott City and Catonsville.

quotes.text: Convene group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: To preserve neighborhood character, the plan recommends convening a "group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community."

quotes.text: Obtain funding and acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs and UMBC students.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address community health and quality of life, stakeholders recommend seeking funding to "acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs" and support the growing student population.

quotes.text: The Fitzgerald apartment building, located at 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue in Mid-Town Belvedere, is an example of a successful Transit Oriented Development project in Baltimore. Built in 2010, adjacent to the Mt. Royal/MICA Light Rail station, the seven-story building has 275 apartment units and two commercial establishments on the lower level
quotes.briefing_quote: A prime example of successful transit-oriented development is the Fitzgerald apartment building, which stands as a seven-story building with 275 apartment units and ground-floor commercial establishments adjacent to the Light Rail, showcasing how dense, mixed-use infill can thrive in Baltimore.

quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. These areas are relatively rich in the resources needed for quality of life and healthy child development, but as a result of a long practice of exclusion, they currently have limited affordable housing.
quotes.briefing_quote: To affirmatively further fair housing, the plan emphasizes that in stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed-income developments to reverse long practices of exclusion.

quotes.text: Replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and the vacant former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, new elementary middle school, two new parks, and a renovated and expanded Chick Webb Recreation Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Perkins Somerset Oldtown Transformation Plan represents a massive revitalization effort, replacing obsolete housing with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, and essential community spaces.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. These are largely stable, highly livable, and resilient communities, but unfortunately, they have historically received little benefit from national and local housing policies that have often failed to support the middle class.
quotes.briefing_quote: Housing policy experts highlighted the critical need to support middle neighborhoods, noting that these homes generate wealth over generations for families whose future security is tied to their communities' ongoing success.

quotes.briefing_quote: To revitalize local business hubs, Main Street program strategies include offering "financial assistance for design and promotions, architectural services for facade renovations, and streetscape improvements" to draw in new commercial tenants.

quotes.text: To provide safe and decent housing and help owners maintain their housing values, the City and Housing Authority dedicate considerable resources to increasing and preserving its supply of affordable housing for both homeowners and renters.

quotes.text: Despite gains in income, the City continues to experience a shortage of affordable rental and homeownership units particularly for households earning 50% or less of the Area Median Income (AMI) as determined by the U.S. Department of Housing & Urban Development (HUD).

quotes.text: Each district’s Main Street program has a different strategy for spurring economic activity, but support may include marketing and event planning, financial assistance for design and promotions, architectural services for facade renovations, streetscape improvements, technical support, access to grants, and more to support the City’s eight (8) Main Street Districts.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD

Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD
Cowenton Avenue & Pulaski Highway, White Marsh, MD
Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: The community envisions a collaborative approach to improving the quality of life, health, safety, and economic vitality of the Govans area, leveraging the public investment of the modernized school. The community aspires to strengthen connections across the York Road commercial corridor—transforming it from a historic line of division into a cohesive 'zipper' that unites the neighborhoods—while stabilizing and rehabilitating residential middle neighborhoods like Mid-Govans and Woodbourne-McCabe to foster generational wealth, homeownership, and safe, walkable pathways.
geographic_addresses: York Road & Bellona Avenue, Baltimore, MD
York Road & Campbell Lane, Baltimore, MD
York Road & Woodbourne Avenue, Baltimore, MD
Ivanhoe Avenue & Tunbridge Road, Baltimore, MD

quotes.text: With a strong housing market and access to a commercial corridor with varied amenities, the Govans area is attractive for new investment. The only issue is the low number of vacant housing stock available in the area. Matchmaking or direct communication with developers will be important to creating opportunities for rehab.
quotes.briefing_quote: With a strong housing market and access to a commercial corridor with varied amenities, the Govans area is attractive for new investment, presenting a clear opportunity for "matchmaking or direct communication with developers... to create opportunities for rehab" of the area's limited vacant housing stock.

quotes.text: Specific recommendations for this area focus on the creation of a family-serving business corridor with a mix of day and night activity and establishment of a transit hub to meet transportation needs.
quotes.briefing_quote: Prior planning efforts for the York Road entertainment node emphasize a critical need to focus on "the creation of a family-serving business corridor with a mix of day and night activity" and the establishment of a transit hub.

quotes.text: On York Road, there are several vacant or underutilized commercial and office buildings where a co-working space could be a new use. Buildings that could potentially be adapted for this new use include the Verizon Building (5711 York Road), the automotive service building (5602 York Road) next to the Accelerator Space, and the commercially zoned storefronts on the 5700 block of Bellona Avenue.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support local entrepreneurship, planners suggest exploring opportunities to "establish a co-working space... in several vacant or underutilized commercial and office buildings" along York Road, such as the Verizon Building, the automotive service building, or the commercially zoned storefronts on Bellona Avenue.

quotes.text: According to the 2017 Housing Market Typology, the majority of the Govans INSPIRE area is classified as Market Category D, which indicates a community in the Middle Market category. These areas have median sales values above the Baltimore City average and high homeownership rates; however, these areas experience higher foreclosure rates when compared to higher-value market categories. Recommended interventions are generally geared toward code enforcement to convert vacant buildings to rehabbed units as soon as possible.
quotes.briefing_quote: Because the majority of the area is classified as a Middle Market neighborhood with high homeownership, the plan notes that "recommended interventions are generally geared toward code enforcement to convert vacant buildings to rehabbed units" as soon as possible.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

quotes.text: The Fitzgerald apartment building, located at 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue in Mid-Town Belvedere, is an example of a successful Transit Oriented Development project in Baltimore. Built in 2010, adjacent to the Mt. Royal/MICA Light Rail station, the seven-story building has 275 apartment units and two commercial establishments on the lower level
quotes.briefing_quote: A prime example of successful transit-oriented development is the Fitzgerald apartment building, which stands as a seven-story building with 275 apartment units and ground-floor commercial establishments adjacent to the Light Rail, showcasing how dense, mixed-use infill can thrive in Baltimore.

quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. quotes.briefing_quote: To affirmatively further fair housing, the plan emphasizes that in stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed-income developments to reverse long practices of exclusion.

quotes.text: Replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and the vacant former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, new elementary middle school, two new parks, and a renovated and expanded Chick Webb Recreation Center.
quotes.briefing_quote: The Perkins Somerset Oldtown Transformation Plan represents a massive revitalization effort, replacing obsolete housing with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing, a new grocery store, and essential community spaces.

quotes.text: These homes generate wealth over generations for many families whose future security is inextricably tied to their communities’ ongoing success. The community aims to capitalize on its strategic role as a logistics and technology hub, revitalizing key commercial corridors like East Drive and Linden Avenue with diverse retail, arts, and mixed-use transit-oriented developments that serve residents and students alike.

quotes.text: The proposed Arbutus Station is a mixed-use development by a local developer at the intersection of Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road. It is within the proposed Sustainable Community boundary and the County's Commercial Revitalization District that can take advantage of the County's revitalization programs if it meets the County revitalization goals and efforts. The project is now submitted for Department's review and approval. The community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: With proposals like Arbutus Station at Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road, "the community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan."

quotes.text: Finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners. Though the community is always looking for prospective homeowners, there is a lack of rental options to attract the UMBC students and programs to benefit both the landlords and student renters. At the same time the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup discussions highlighted the challenge of "finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners," noting that while there is a lack of student rental options, "the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership."

quotes.text: Bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques similar to Ellicott City and Catonsville.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local economic strategies emphasize the desire to "bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques" to the commercial district, modeling success after nearby Ellicott City and Catonsville.

quotes.text: Convene group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: To preserve neighborhood character, the plan recommends convening a "group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community."

quotes.text: Obtain funding and acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs and UMBC students.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address community health and quality of life, stakeholders recommend seeking funding to "acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs" and support the growing student population.

quotes.text: All new rental housing should be mixed-income, meaning that it must be accessible to people making all ranges of income (from no income to unrestricted income). Each new development should be 1/3 low-income units, 1/3 workforce units, and 1/3 units for unrestricted income renters where economically feasible.
quotes.briefing_quote: To promote socioeconomic diversity and inclusivity, the plan stresses that 'all new rental housing should be mixed-income... each new development should be 1/3 low-income units, 1/3 workforce units, and 1/3 units for unrestricted income renters where economically feasible.'

quotes.text: Construct 80-100 units of high-quality, mixed-income rental housing in a 4-story building on the Patapsco School Site
quotes.briefing_quote: The steering committee highlighted an immediate infill residential opportunity to 'construct 80-100 units of high-quality, mixed-income rental housing in a 4-story building on the Patapsco School Site' next to the local school.

quotes.text: Many of the existing rowhouses in Cherry Hill are roughly 750—900 SF and have 2-3 bedrooms, with 1 full bathroom. Families today are looking for 3 and 4-bedrooms with at least 2 to 2.5 bathrooms;... Shorter lengths of rowhouses (duplexes, triplexes, and 4-unit buildings) would help to break up the streets and provide green between the buildings.
quotes.briefing_quote: To mitigate out-migration of families seeking larger spaces, the plan highlights a strong demand for developers to build 'larger houses with contemporary floor plans' featuring three to four bedrooms and multiple bathrooms.

quotes.text: Cherry Hill currently does not have the spending required to support a supermarket and would need to capture additional demand from surrounding areas... The best way to address residents' needs for groceries is to implement a phased approach.
quotes.briefing_quote: Acknowledging that the area's current spending power sits below national grocery chain thresholds, the plan recommends that developers 'attract a small, private grocery chain or family-owned franchise' as part of a phased food security approach.

quotes.text: In the future, a mixed-use Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) neighborhood may be possible next to the existing Cherry Hill Light RailLink station... The TOD would also be an ideal location for mixed-income rental housing, which combines financing sources to create housing for a range of incomes, from low-income to market rate.
quotes.briefing_quote: The planning team identified a major opportunity to create a 'vibrant mixed-use Transit-Oriented Development neighborhood next to the existing Cherry Hill Light RailLink station' to integrate higher-density housing and local retail.

quotes.text: The Fitzgerald apartment building, located at 1201 W. Mount Royal Avenue in Mid-Town Belvedere, is an example of a successful Transit Oriented Development project in Baltimore. quotes.text: In stronger market neighborhoods, it is essential to build affordable housing as part of mixed income developments to affirmatively further fair housing. plan_quotes.community_vision: Baltimore County envisions a future centered on creating livable, healthy, and equitable communities in harmony with nature, supported by a resilient economy and strong regional partnerships. Facing a depletion of undeveloped greenfield land inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), the County is shifting its growth strategy toward retrofitting and redevelopment. This approach focuses density, walkability, public spaces, and mixed-use developments into designated 'Nodes'—such as aging commercial centers, transit stations, and greyfields—while steadfastly preserving the agricultural and natural resources of its rural areas.
geographic_addresses: Forge Road & Belair Road, Perry Hall, MD
Compass Road & Wampler Road, Middle River, MD
Cowenton Avenue & Pulaski Highway, White Marsh, MD
Rolling Road & Windsor Mill Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Rolling Road, Windsor Mill, MD
Liberty Road & Old Court Road, Randallstown, MD
Wharf Road, Sparrows Point, MD

quotes.text: The availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development in areas within the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL); our water and sewer infrastructure are aging; our transit system needs modernization; our housing supply struggles to meet demand; and our commercial areas require a different perspective than what was used in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: The County Council's opening statement highlighted that "the availability of developable land in the County continues to be a challenge, particularly for in-fill development... and our housing supply struggles to meet demand," underscoring the vital need for modern infill and mixed-use approaches.

quotes.text: The County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles—walking, biking and public transit.
quotes.briefing_quote: Members of the Green Towson Alliance noted that "the County should make every effort to plan for [anticipated] growth by offering multiple forms of mobility other than automobiles," advocating for ped-friendly, transit-oriented mixed-use developments.

quotes.text: There's not a whole lot of land inside the URDL that can have traditional suburban developments, so we need to move towards high standard high-density developments. This is different than the construction/development that has occurred in the past.
quotes.briefing_quote: A workshop participant observed that since traditional suburban land is nearly depleted inside the boundary, "we need to move towards high standard high-density developments" rather than continuing legacy sprawl patterns.

quotes.text: We want more diversity in the business types in retail areas.
quotes.briefing_quote: Owings Mills community members expressed that they "want more diversity in the business types in retail areas," indicating a local push to revitalize and diversify aging retail strips.

quotes.text: Create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development in and near transit stations by utilizing a Smart Growth framework.
quotes.briefing_quote: To support sustainable growth, the plan recommends to "create new and adjust existing overlay districts with implementation tools and incentives to encourage walkable, mixed-use development" near transit hubs.

quotes.text: The Planned Unit Development (PUD) Process should be evaluated and updated.
quotes.briefing_quote: A local resident noted during the public comment phase that "the Planned Unit Development process should be evaluated and updated" to ensure higher quality development, transparency, and explicit community benefits.

plan_quotes.community_vision: Arbutus aspires to transition into a vibrant "college town" leveraging its proximity to the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) while carefully protecting the area's historic single-family character and small-town charm. The community aims to capitalize on its strategic role as a logistics and technology hub, revitalizing key commercial corridors like East Drive and Linden Avenue with diverse retail, arts, and mixed-use transit-oriented developments that serve residents and students alike.
geographic_addresses: Waelchi Avenue & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Linden Avenue & Shelbourne Road, Arbutus, MD
Shelbourne Road & Sulphur Spring Road, Arbutus, MD
Tom Day & Southwestern Boulevard, Arbutus, MD

quotes.text: The proposed Arbutus Station is a mixed-use development by a local developer at the intersection of Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road. It is within the proposed Sustainable Community boundary and the County's Commercial Revitalization District that can take advantage of the County's revitalization programs if it meets the County revitalization goals and efforts. The project is now submitted for Department's review and approval. The community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan.
quotes.briefing_quote: With proposals like Arbutus Station at Waelchi Avenue and Sulphur Spring Road, "the community is actively involved in all development projects in the area to make sure the development fits in with the surrounding area and the project addresses any applicable goals in this plan."

quotes.text: Finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners. Though the community is always looking for prospective homeowners, there is a lack of rental options to attract the UMBC students and programs to benefit both the landlords and student renters. At the same time the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership.
quotes.briefing_quote: Workgroup discussions highlighted the challenge of "finding a balance between renters and prospective homeowners," noting that while there is a lack of student rental options, "the community does not want renters to outprice young families moving in and intends to increase homeownership."

quotes.text: Bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques similar to Ellicott City and Catonsville.
quotes.briefing_quote: Local economic strategies emphasize the desire to "bring diversity in restaurants, quality anchor stores and boutiques" to the commercial district, modeling success after nearby Ellicott City and Catonsville.

quotes.text: Convene group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community.
quotes.briefing_quote: To preserve neighborhood character, the plan recommends convening a "group of design and development professionals to brief community associations on how to rehab and maintain older homes while retaining physical characteristics that add to the charm of the community."

quotes.text: Obtain funding and acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs and UMBC students.
quotes.briefing_quote: To address community health and quality of life, stakeholders recommend seeking funding to "acquire derelict properties to redevelop to meet community needs" and support the growing student population.
